docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Start Small: Use filter_level="minimal" for initial checks, then fetch more data as needed
  2. Use actionable_only: For CI/CD and developer workflows, focus on actionable findings with actionable_only=True
  3. Filter Early: Apply severities filter to reduce data transfer for high-priority checks
  4. Target Scanners: Use scanners filter when debugging or analyzing specific tools
  5. Combine Filters: Use multiple filters together for maximum efficiency
  6. Cache Results: Store filtered results locally to avoid repeated API calls

docs.title: Filter Metadata
docs.text:
When using content filters (scanners, severities, or actionable_only), the response includes a _content_filters field showing which filters were applied:

{
  "_content_filters": {
    "scanners": ["bandit", "semgrep"],
    "severities": ["critical", "high"],
    "actionable_only": true
  }
}

This helps track what filters were used to generate the response.

docs.title: Backward Compatibility
docs.text:
All filtering parameters are optional. Calling get_scan_results without any filter parameters returns the full results, maintaining backward compatibility with existing code:

# This still works exactly as before
results = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output")

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The ASH MCP server was crashing with ClosedResourceError when trying to send responses after long-running scans (2-5 minutes). The client was disconnecting before the server could send the final results.

docs.title: Root Causes Identified
docs.text:
1. Aggressive Polling: Client was polling every 1 second, causing excessive network traffic
  2. Poor Error Handling: No graceful handling of closed connections or cancelled tasks
  3. Large Response Size: Sending 896 findings with 1.6MB of data in a single response
  4. No Connection State Awareness: Server didn't check if connection was still alive before sending
  5. Monolithic Results API: Single tool returned all data, no way to get lightweight summaries

docs.title: 1. Optimized Polling Intervals for 2-5 Minute Scans
docs.text:
Before: Fixed 1-second polling interval After: Adaptive polling optimized for typical scan duration: - 5 seconds when no scanners completed (initialization phase) - 8 seconds when few scanners completed (early phase) - 10 seconds when multiple scanners running (main phase) - 15 seconds for heartbeat interval (up from 10)

Benefit: Reduces network traffic by ~90% while maintaining good responsiveness for 2-5 minute scans.

docs.title: Connection-Aware Progress Reporting
docs.text:
All ctx.report_progress(), ctx.info(), ctx.error(), and ctx.debug() calls now wrapped in try-except blocks:

try:
    await ctx.report_progress(...)
except Exception as e:
    logger.debug(f"Failed to send progress: {str(e)}")
    # Continue monitoring even if client disconnected

Benefit: Server continues monitoring scan even if client disconnects, allowing scan to complete successfully.

docs.title: Graceful Task Cancellation
docs.text:
Added specific handling for asyncio.CancelledError:

except asyncio.CancelledError:
    logger.info(f"Scan monitoring cancelled for scan_id: {scan_id}")
    try:
        await ctx.info("Scan monitoring stopped.")
    except Exception:
        pass  # Ignore if connection closed

Benefit: Clean shutdown without error spam in logs.

docs.title: Server-Level Error Handling
docs.text:
Improved run_mcp_server() to handle connection errors gracefully:

except Exception as e:
    if "ClosedResourceError" in str(e) or "TaskGroup" in str(e):
        logger.warning("MCP server connection closed unexpectedly...")
    else:
        logger.exception(f"Error running MCP server: {str(e)}")
    # Don't re-raise - allow graceful shutdown

Benefit: Server logs helpful warnings instead of crashing with stack traces.

docs.title: Removed Large Data Fields
docs.text: Now removes these fields from MCP responses: - sarif - Large SARIF format data - cyclonedx - Large SBOM data - findings - Detailed findings array - ash_config - Configuration data - validation_checkpoints - Internal validation data

docs.title: Truncated Findings Lists
docs.text:
Limits findings per severity to top 50:

if len(findings_list) > 50:
    summary["findings_by_severity"][severity] = findings_list[:50]
    summary[f"{severity}_truncated"] = True
    summary[f"{severity}_total_count"] = len(findings_list)

Benefit: Reduces response size from ~1.6MB to <100KB while preserving critical summary data.

docs.title: 4. New MCP Tools for Better Data Access
get_scan_summary - Lightweight Summary Tool
docs.text:
New tool that returns only high-level statistics without detailed findings:

Returns: - Scan metadata (timestamps, duration, ASH version) - Findings count by severity (critical, high, medium, low, info) - Findings count by scanner/tool - Scanner execution status - Summary statistics (total, actionable)

Response Size: ~5-10KB (vs 100KB+ for full results)

Use Case: Quick status checks, dashboard displays, CI/CD gates

docs.title: get_scan_result_paths - File Path Discovery Tool
docs.text:
New tool that returns absolute paths to all result files:

Returns: - Paths to all report formats (SARIF, JSON, HTML, CSV, etc.) - File existence status - File sizes in bytes - Scanner-specific result file paths

Use Case: Allows clients to decide which files to read and how to process them

Example Response: 

{
  "success": true,
  "output_dir": "/path/to/.ash/ash_output",
  "reports_dir": "/path/to/.ash/ash_output/reports",
  "files": {
    "sarif": {
      "path": "/path/to/.ash/ash_output/reports/ash.sarif",
      "exists": true,
      "size_bytes": 2456789
    },
    "flat_json": {
      "path": "/path/to/.ash/ash_output/reports/ash.flat.json",
      "exists": true,
      "size_bytes": 1678234
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 5. Enhanced get_scan_results with Filter Parameter
docs.text:
Added optional filter parameter to get_scan_results for flexible response sizing:

Filter Options: - filter="full" (default): Returns all results including raw_results, validation_checkpoints, etc. - filter="summary": Returns only summary data (metadata, findings counts, scanner summaries) - filter="minimal": Returns only basic scan status and completion info

Benefits: - Backward compatible - default behavior unchanged - Progressive data fetching - start with minimal, get more as needed - Flexible response sizing: 1KB (minimal) → 5-15KB (summary) → 50KB-2MB (full)

Example Usage: 

# Minimal status check (1-2KB)
status = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output", filter="minimal")

# Summary for decision making (5-15KB)
summary = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output", filter="summary")

# Full results when needed (50KB-2MB)
full = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output", filter="full")
# Or simply (default):
full = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output")

docs.title: 6. Improved get_scan_results Tool
docs.text:
Enhanced to remove even more large fields: - Now also removes findings array (detailed findings) - Keeps only summary statistics - Adds note about data truncation

Benefit: Clients can use get_scan_summary for quick checks, get_scan_result_paths to discover files, and read specific files directly when needed.

docs.title: 7. Progress Update Timing
docs.text:
Only updates last_progress_time when progress send succeeds:

try:
    await ctx.report_progress(...)
    last_progress_time = current_time  # Only update on success
except Exception as e:
    logger.debug(f"Failed to send progress: {str(e)}")

Benefit: Prevents heartbeat spam if connection is degraded.

docs.title: Recommended Client Workflow
docs.text:
1. Start Scan: Call run_ash_scan()
  2. Monitor Progress: Receive automatic progress updates (every 5-15 seconds)
  3. Get Quick Summary: Call get_scan_summary() when complete (~5KB response)
  4. Discover Files: Call get_scan_result_paths() to see available reports
  5. Read Specific Files: Read SARIF, JSON, or other files directly from disk as needed

This approach minimizes MCP data transfer while giving clients full access to all results.

docs.title: ASH MCP Server Testing Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to test the ASH MCP server locally during development, including configuration, testing procedures, and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• ASH repository cloned locally
  • uv and uvx installed (installation guide)
  • Kiro IDE or another MCP-compatible client
  • Python 3.10 or later

docs.title: 1. Configure MCP Client to Use Local Code
docs.text:
Update your MCP configuration file to point to your local development directory instead of the GitHub repository.

Location: ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json (for Kiro)

Configuration:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ash": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--project=/path/to/your/automated-security-helper",
        "ash",
        "mcp"
      ],
      "autoApprove": [
        "get_scan_progress",
        "get_scan_results",
        "get_scan_summary",
        "get_scan_result_paths",
        "run_ash_scan"
      ],
      "disabled": false,
      "env": {
        "FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL": "DEBUG"
      }
    }
  }
}

Key Parameters: - run --project=/path/to/your/automated-security-helper - Runs the ash entry point from your checkout's project environment (its .venv), where uv installs ASH in editable mode, so code changes take effect when the server restarts. uv run syncs that environment to uv.lock first, and keeps any extras you installed there (for example with uv sync --extra cdk --extra symbols). - FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL: DEBUG - Enables detailed logging for debugging

Do not use uvx ... ash mcp without --from here. uvx installs the package named by its first argument from the package index (PyPI by default), and the PyPI project named ash is unrelated to ASH.

Note: Replace /path/to/your/automated-security-helper with your actual path.

docs.title: 2. Restart MCP Server
docs.text:
After configuration changes:

In Kiro: 1. Open Command Palette (Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P) 2. Search for "MCP: Reconnect Server" 3. Select the ASH server to reconnect

Alternative: Restart your IDE/client completely

docs.title: 3. Verify Configuration
docs.text:
Check that the command the client runs starts ASH from your checkout:

uv run --project=/path/to/your/automated-security-helper ash mcp --help

It prints the ash mcp options. A warning that names a package called ash means the configuration is still running uvx, which resolved that unrelated PyPI project; switch it to the uv run form above.

docs.title: Test 1: Check Installation
docs.text:
Verify ASH is properly installed and accessible.

# Call the check_installation tool
result = await mcp_ash_check_installation()

# Expected response:
{
    "success": true,
    "installed": true,
    "version": "3.2.2",  # or your current version
    "ash_command_available": true,
    "ash_command_output": "ASH version 3.2.2",
    "timestamp": "2026-02-28T10:10:41.009478",
}

What to verify: - success is true - installed is true - version matches your local version - ash_command_available is true

docs.title: Test 2: Run a Scan
docs.text:
Start a security scan on a test directory.

# Start a scan
result = await mcp_ash_run_ash_scan(
    source_dir="/path/to/test/project", severity_threshold="MEDIUM", clean_output=true
)

# Expected response:
{
    "success": true,
    "status": "running",
    "scan_id": "2e0cd8d2-132c-4eb1-a822-38dd237067f3",
    "progress": 0.0,
    "message": "Scan started, initializing scanners...",
    "directory_path": "/path/to/test/project",
}

What to verify: - success is true - scan_id is returned (save this for later tests) - status is "running" - No error messages

Timing: Note the start time to verify polling intervals later.

docs.title: Test 3: Monitor Scan Progress
docs.text:
Check scan progress using the scan ID from Test 2.

# Check progress (wait 15-20 seconds after starting scan)
result = await mcp_ash_get_scan_progress(
    scan_id="2e0cd8d2-132c-4eb1-a822-38dd237067f3"
)

# Expected response:
{
  "scan_id": "2e0cd8d2-132c-4eb1-a822-38dd237067f3",
  "status": "running",  # or "completed"
  "completed_scanners": 3,
  "total_scanners": 9,
  "scanners": {
    "bandit": {
      "source": {
        "status": "completed",
        "finding_count": 45,
        "severity_counts": {...}
      }
    },
    // ... more scanners
  }
}

What to verify: - Progress updates arrive every 5-15 seconds (check timestamps) - completed_scanners increases over time - Scanner statuses transition from "pending" → "running" → "completed"

Expected Duration: 2-5 minutes for typical projects

docs.title: Test 6: Get Full Scan Results
docs.text:
Retrieve scan results with filtering applied.

# Get full results
result = await mcp_ash_get_scan_results(
    output_dir="/path/to/test/project/.ash/ash_output"

What to verify: - Response size is moderate (<100KB, not 1.6MB+) - Large fields are removed (sarif, cyclonedx, findings) - Summary data is still present - Note about data truncation is included

List all scans in the registry.

# List scans

{

        {

docs.title: Polling Intervals
docs.text:
Monitor the timestamps in progress updates to verify adaptive polling:

Expected Intervals: - Early phase (0-2 scanners): ~5 seconds - Mid phase (2-4 scanners): ~8 seconds - Late phase (4+ scanners): ~10 seconds - Heartbeat (no progress): ~15 seconds

How to verify: 1. Note timestamps from multiple get_scan_progress calls 2. Calculate time differences 3. Confirm intervals match expected ranges

docs.title: Response Sizes
docs.text:
Compare response sizes across tools:

Tool Expected Size What to Check get_scan_summary 5-10KB No raw_results, no findings arrays get_scan_result_paths 2-5KB Only paths and metadata get_scan_results <100KB Large fields removed Full aggregated file 5-10MB On disk, not via MCP

How to verify: 1. Save responses to files 2. Check file sizes: ls -lh response.json 3. Inspect content for unexpected large fields

docs.title: Test Connection Resilience
docs.text:
Verify the server handles disconnections gracefully.

Procedure: 1. Start a scan 2. Disconnect/kill the MCP client mid-scan 3. Reconnect after scan completes 4. Verify scan completed successfully 5. Retrieve results

Expected behavior: - Scan continues running after disconnect - Results are saved to disk - No ClosedResourceError in logs - Can retrieve results after reconnect

docs.title: Test Invalid Parameters
docs.text:
Verify error handling for invalid inputs.

# Test with non-existent directory
result = await mcp_ash_get_scan_results(output_dir="/non/existent/path")

# Expected response:
{
    "success": false,
    "error": "Output directory does not exist: /non/existent/path",
    "error_type": "DirectoryNotFound",
}

What to verify: - success is false - Clear error message - Appropriate error_type - No stack traces in response

docs.title: Issue: MCP Server Not Using Local Code
docs.text:
Symptoms: - Changes not reflected after restart - Old behavior persists

Solutions: 1. Check that the configuration runs uv run --project=<your checkout>. A uvx command installs a copy of ASH, which does not change when you edit the checkout.

  1. Reinstall ASH into the checkout's environment (needed after pyproject.toml changes, for example a new entry point). --inexact keeps the extras you installed; a plain uv sync removes them: 

    cd /path/to/ash
uv sync --inexact --reinstall-package automated-security-helper

  2. Verify configuration path is correct

  3. Restart IDE completely

docs.title: Issue: Import Errors
docs.text:
Symptoms: 

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'automated_security_helper'

Solutions: 1. Ensure you're in the correct directory 2. Check the --project path in the config 3. Install dependencies into the checkout's environment, keeping any extras already there: 

cd /path/to/ash
uv sync --inexact

docs.title: Issue: Tools Not Found
docs.text:
Symptoms: 

Tool 'get_scan_summary' not found

Solutions: 1. Verify tool is registered in mcp_server.py 2. Check for syntax errors: python -m py_compile automated_security_helper/cli/mcp_server.py 3. Restart MCP server 4. Check MCP logs for registration errors

docs.title: Issue: Large Response Sizes
docs.text:
Symptoms: - get_scan_summary returns >100KB - Timeouts or slow responses

Solutions: 1. Verify filtering logic in get_scan_summary 2. Check that large fields are being removed 3. Compare with get_scan_result_paths (should be small) 4. Review code for proper data extraction

docs.title: Enable Debug Logging
docs.text:
Set log level in MCP config: 

"env": {
  "FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL": "DEBUG"
}

docs.title: View MCP Logs
docs.text:
In Kiro: - Open "MCP Logs" panel - Filter by server name "ash" - Look for errors, warnings, or debug messages

In Terminal: 

# ASH logs are in the .ash folder of your scan directory
tail -f .ash/ash_output/ash.log

docs.title: Common Log Messages

Normal: 

INFO: Starting scan for directory: /path/to/project
INFO: Scan started with ID: 2e0cd8d2-132c-4eb1-a822-38dd237067f3

ERROR: Error in get_scan_summary: KeyError

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Scans started through the MCP server never run a scanner or other tool found inside the scanned or delivered directory, such as a project's .venv/bin or node_modules/.bin; ASH_ALLOW_IN_TREE_TOOLS and --allow-in-tree-tools are not honored by ash mcp. Install the scanners the server uses outside the repository. See Tools inside the scanned directory.

A scan also refuses an output directory reached through a symlink, as ash scan does (see Output directory). This server writes a scan's output to .ash/ash_output in the scanned directory. A link at .ash or .ash/ash_output is refused before the scan starts, with error_type output_dir_not_permitted; a link at a directory or file ASH writes there fails the scan with ASH exited with code 3: and an error that asks for the link to be replaced with a directory. run_ash_workspace_scan takes output_dir, and its error asks for one that is not a link.

The ASH MCP server provides multiple tools for accessing scan results with different levels of detail. The get_scan_results tool now includes a filter parameter for flexible response sizing, and two new specialized tools provide lightweight alternatives.

docs.title: Which output directories a caller may read
docs.text: All three tools read a caller-named output directory, and the same roots that bound scanning bound reading: an output directory lives at <source_dir>/.ash/ash_output, so a directory a caller may scan is one whose results it may read. On stdio the single local client may read anything outside a short list of system directories unless ASH_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS narrows it. On a network transport (sse or streamable-HTTP) every caller is remote, whatever headers it sends: it may read the directories in ASH_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS and its own session workspace, never another session's. The session is the one the server issued, not a header the client chose; see Session identity. A refusal has error_type: scan_target_not_permitted.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Get scan results with optional filtering to control response size. This is the primary tool for accessing scan data, now with flexible filtering options while maintaining backward compatibility.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
async def get_scan_results(
    ctx: Context, 
    output_dir: str = ".ash/ash_output",
    filter_level: str = "full",
    scanners: str = None,
    severities: str = None,
    actionable_only: bool = False
) -> Dict[str, Any]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• output_dir (str): Path to the scan output directory (absolute path recommended)
  • filter_level (str): Filter level for response data. Options:
  • "full" (default): Return all results including raw_results, validation_checkpoints, etc.
  • "summary": Return only summary data (metadata, findings counts, scanner summaries)
  • "minimal": Return only basic scan status and completion info
  • scanners (str, optional): Comma-separated list of scanner names to include (e.g., "bandit,semgrep"). If not specified, includes all scanners.
  • severities (str, optional): Comma-separated list of severity levels to include (e.g., "critical,high,medium"). Options: critical, high, medium, low, info, suppressed. If not specified, includes all severities.
  • actionable_only (bool): If True, keep only the actionable findings, the ones that make the scan exit 2: not suppressed, and at or above the severity threshold the scan was judged by (a scanner's own threshold where its config sets one). Findings below the threshold, which the scan reports but does not fail on, are left out, as are findings marked as false positives or accepted risks. Adds findings, a flat list of them, with findings_count, in a filter_level="full" response. Default is False.

docs.title: With filter="full" (default - backward compatible)
docs.text:
{
  "success": true,
  "scan_id": "scan-20260228095648",
  "status": "completed",
  "is_complete": true,
  "summary_stats": { ... },
  "scanner_reports": { ... },
  "raw_results": {
    "metadata": { ... },
    "scanner_results": { ... },
    "converter_results": { ... },
    "additional_reports": { ... },
    "validation_checkpoints": [ ... ]
  },
  "validation_checkpoints": [ ... ]
}

docs.title: With filter="summary"
docs.text:
{
  "success": true,

  • filter="summary": ~5-15KB (lightweight summary)

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Full (default): Backward compatibility, detailed analysis, comprehensive reporting
  • Summary: Quick status checks, dashboards, CI/CD gates, monitoring
  • Minimal: Health checks, polling for completion, simple status displays

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
# Get full results (backward compatible - default behavior)
results = await get_scan_results(output_dir="/path/to/.ash/ash_output")

# Get only actionable findings (unsuppressed, at or above the severity threshold)
actionable_results = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir="/path/to/.ash/ash_output", actionable_only=True
)

# Get summary with only actionable findings
actionable_summary = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir="/path/to/.ash/ash_output", filter_level="summary", actionable_only=True
)

# Filter by specific scanners and severities
filtered_results = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir="/path/to/.ash/ash_output",
    scanners="bandit,semgrep",
    severities="critical,high",
    actionable_only=True,
)

# Get summary only (lightweight)
summary = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir="/path/to/.ash/ash_output", filter_level="summary"
)

# Check for critical findings
if summary["findings_summary"]["by_severity"]["critical"] > 0:
    print("CRITICAL findings detected!")
    # Now get full results for detailed analysis
    full_results = await get_scan_results(
        output_dir="/path/to/.ash/ash_output", filter_level="full"
    )

# Get minimal status (smallest response)
status = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir="/path/to/.ash/ash_output", filter_level="minimal"
)
print(
    f"Scan status: {status['status']}, Total findings: {status['summary_stats']['total']}"
)

docs.text: ~2-5KB (just paths and metadata)

docs.title: Available Report Types
docs.text:
• sarif - SARIF format (industry standard)
  • flat_json - Flat JSON format (easy to parse)
  • html - HTML report (human-readable)
  • csv - CSV format (spreadsheet-friendly)
  • markdown - Markdown summary
  • text - Plain text summary
  • ocsf - OCSF format (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework)
  • cyclonedx - CycloneDX SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)
  • junit_xml - JUnit XML (CI/CD integration)
  • gitlab_sast - GitLab SAST format
  • aggregated_results - ASH internal aggregated results

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Discovering which report formats are available
  • Checking file sizes before reading
  • Building file download/export features
  • Integrating with external tools that need specific formats
  • Verifying scan completion (all expected files exist)

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
# Get all result file paths
paths = await get_scan_result_paths(output_dir="/Users/user/project/.ash/ash_output")

# Check if SARIF report exists
if paths["files"]["sarif"]["exists"]:
    sarif_path = paths["files"]["sarif"]["path"]
    print(f"SARIF report: {sarif_path} ({paths['files']['sarif']['size_bytes']} bytes)")

    # Read SARIF file directly
    with open(sarif_path) as f:
        sarif_data = json.load(f)

# Find the smallest report for quick viewing
smallest = min(
    paths["files"].items(),
    key=lambda x: x[1]["size_bytes"] if x[1]["exists"] else float("inf"),
)
print(f"Smallest report: {smallest[0]} ({smallest[1]['size_bytes']} bytes)")

# List all scanner-specific results
for scanner, targets in paths["scanner_results"].items():
    for target, info in targets.items():
        if info["exists"]:
            print(f"{scanner}/{target}: {info['path']}")

docs.title: Comparison: When to Use Each Tool
docs.text: Tool Response Size Use Case Data Included get_scan_results (filter_level="minimal") ~1-2KB Health checks, polling Status + summary stats only get_scan_result_paths ~2-5KB File discovery, integration File paths, sizes, existence get_scan_summary ~5-10KB Quick status check, statistics Metadata, counts by severity/scanner get_scan_results (filter_level="summary") ~5-15KB Detailed summary Same as get_scan_summary get_scan_results (filter_level="full") 50KB-2MB Full analysis All data including raw results get_scan_results (actionable_only=True) Varies Actionable findings only Excludes suppressed and below-threshold findings Direct file read Varies Full detail, specific format Complete data in chosen format

docs.title: Filter by Actionable Findings
docs.text:
Use actionable_only=True to keep only the findings that fail the scan. It excludes suppressed findings (false positives or accepted risks) and findings below the scan's severity threshold:

# Get only findings that require action
actionable = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output", actionable_only=True)

# Combine with other filters
critical_actionable = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir=".ash/ash_output",
    severities="critical,high",
    actionable_only=True,
    filter_level="summary",
)

docs.title: Filter by Scanner
docs.text:
Use scanners parameter to include only specific scanners:

# Get results from specific scanners only
sast_results = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir=".ash/ash_output", scanners="bandit,semgrep"
)

docs.title: Filter by Severity
docs.text:
Use severities parameter to include only specific severity levels:

# Get only high-priority findings
high_priority = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir=".ash/ash_output", severities="critical,high"
)

docs.title: Combine Multiple Filters
docs.text:
All filters can be combined for precise control:

# Get actionable critical/high findings from SAST scanners only
results = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir=".ash/ash_output",
    scanners="bandit,semgrep",
    severities="critical,high",
    actionable_only=True,
    filter_level="summary",
)

docs.title: Workflow 1: Progressive Detail (Recommended)
docs.text:
# 1. Start scan
scan = await run_ash_scan(source_dir="/path/to/code")

# 2. Wait for completion (automatic progress updates)
# Progress updates arrive every 5-15 seconds

# 3. Get minimal status first (1-2KB)
status = await get_scan_results(output_dir=scan["output_dir"], filter="minimal")

# 4. Check if scan completed successfully
if status["status"] == "completed":
    # 5. Get summary for decision making (5-15KB)
    summary = await get_scan_results(output_dir=scan["output_dir"], filter="summary")

    # 6. Decide next steps based on summary
    if summary["findings_summary"]["by_severity"]["critical"] > 0:
        # Critical findings - get full results
        full_results = await get_scan_results(
            output_dir=scan["output_dir"], filter="full"
        )
        # Analyze detailed findings...
    else:
        print("Scan passed - no critical findings!")

docs.title: Workflow 2: Using Specialized Tools
docs.text:
# 1. Start scan
scan = await run_ash_scan(source_dir="/path/to/code")

# 2. Wait for completion

# 3. Get quick summary using dedicated tool
summary = await get_scan_summary(output_dir=scan["output_dir"])

# 4. If detailed analysis needed, get file paths
if summary["findings_summary"]["by_severity"]["high"] > 10:
    paths = await get_scan_result_paths(output_dir=scan["output_dir"])

    # Read specific format directly
    with open(paths["files"]["sarif"]["path"]) as f:
        sarif_data = json.load(f)

    # Or get full results via MCP
    full_results = await get_scan_results(output_dir=scan["output_dir"], filter="full")

docs.title: Workflow 3: CI/CD Pipeline
docs.text:
# Minimal data transfer for fast CI/CD checks
# Get only actionable findings (unsuppressed, at or above the severity threshold)
summary = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir=".ash/ash_output", filter_level="summary", actionable_only=True
)

# Fail pipeline on critical/high actionable findings
critical = summary["findings_summary"]["by_severity"]["critical"]
high = summary["findings_summary"]["by_severity"]["high"]

if critical > 0 or high > 5:
    print(f"Pipeline failed: {critical} critical, {high} high actionable findings")
    sys.exit(1)
else:
    print("Security scan passed!")
    sys.exit(0)

docs.title: Workflow 4: Focus on Actionable Findings
docs.text:
# Get only findings that require action (unsuppressed, at or above the threshold)
actionable = await get_scan_results(
    output_dir=".ash/ash_output", actionable_only=True, filter_level="summary"
)

# Check actionable findings count
if actionable["findings_summary"]["by_severity"]["actionable"] > 0:
    # Get full details for actionable findings only
    full_actionable = await get_scan_results(
        output_dir=".ash/ash_output", actionable_only=True, filter_level="full"
    )

    # Process actionable findings. `findings` holds exactly the ones that fail
    # the scan; the SARIF they come from is not part of the response.
    for finding in full_actionable["findings"]:
        print(f"Finding: {finding['rule_id']} - {finding.get('message')}")

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
1. Reduced Network Traffic: Transfer only the data you need with filter parameter
  2. Faster Response Times: Smaller payloads = faster responses (1KB vs 1MB+)
  3. Flexible Integration: Choose the right level of detail for your use case
  4. Better Error Handling: Less likely to timeout on large results
  5. Client Control: Clients decide what data to fetch and when
  6. Backward Compatibility: Default behavior unchanged - existing integrations work as-is
  7. Progressive Enhancement: Start with minimal data, fetch more as needed

docs.title: For Existing Users
docs.text:
No changes required! The default behavior of get_scan_results is unchanged: 

# This still works exactly as before
results = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output")

docs.title: To Optimize Performance
docs.text:
Add the filter parameter to reduce response size: 

# Before (full results, potentially large)
results = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output")

# After (summary only, ~5-15KB)
summary = await get_scan_results(output_dir=".ash/ash_output", filter="summary")

# Or use dedicated tool
summary = await get_scan_summary(output_dir=".ash/ash_output")

docs.title: Tool Selection Guide
docs.text:
Use get_scan_results with filter="minimal" when: - Polling for scan completion - Health checks and monitoring - You only need status and basic counts

Use get_scan_results with filter="summary" OR get_scan_summary when: - Quick status checks after scan completion - Dashboard displays - CI/CD pipeline gates - Initial assessment before detailed analysis

Use get_scan_results with filter="full" (default) when: - You need complete scan data - Backward compatibility is required - Detailed analysis of findings - Comprehensive reporting

Use get_scan_result_paths when: - You need to read specific file formats (SARIF, CSV, etc.) - Building file download/export features - Integrating with external tools - You want to process files directly

docs.title: Advanced Usage
docs.text: This guide covers advanced features and usage patterns for ASH v3.

docs.title: Execution Modes
docs.text: ASH v3 supports four execution modes:

docs.title: Local Mode
docs.text:
ash --mode local
  • Runs the scan in the local Python process
  • Runs every enabled scanner, using the scanner tools installed on this machine; a scanner whose tool is missing is reported MISSING
  • --python-only limits the scan to the scanners that need nothing but Python
  • Ideal for quick checks during development

docs.title: Tools inside the scanned directory
docs.text:
ASH does not start a scanner or any other tool that it finds inside the directory it is scanning. uv run ash scan . puts the repository's .venv/bin first on PATH, and npm run does the same with node_modules/.bin, so under either a scanner installed in the project, such as a bandit or semgrep dependency, is part of the repository being scanned. ASH skips it and uses the next copy on PATH, or the one uv tool installs. If there is none, the scanner is reported as MISSING, with the in-tree path in its missing_reason, in the log, and in the message the incomplete scan exits with.

ASH also never finds a tool through the working directory: not through an empty, . or relative PATH entry, and on Windows not through the working directory that CreateProcess and shutil.which search first. Tools on ordinary absolute PATH entries are found, including Homebrew, nix profiles, uv and pipx shims, asdf and mise shims, conda, Program Files, scoop and Chocolatey. Programs ASH and its scanners start are given a PATH without the scanned directory's entries, unless you allow in-tree tools.

To run tools from inside the scanned directory, pass --allow-in-tree-tools (or set "allow_in_tree_tools": true in a --cli-json-input document), or set ASH_ALLOW_IN_TREE_TOOLS to 1, true, yes or on. ASH then uses them and logs a warning naming each one. This also covers the scanner sandbox's own programs (bwrap, firejail, readlink and true). A repository's configuration file cannot turn this on, and ash mcp ignores both: an MCP client's scans never run a tool from inside a scanned or delivered directory, so for MCP use, install scanners outside the repository. See Troubleshooting for the message and the fixes.

docs.title: Container Mode
docs.text:
ash --mode container
  • Builds the ASH container image and runs the whole scan inside it
  • Provides full scanner coverage, because the image has every scanner tool installed
  • Requires a container runtime (Docker, Podman, etc.)
  • Ideal for comprehensive scans

docs.title: Precommit Mode
docs.text:
ash --mode precommit
  • A local scan that runs only bandit, detect-secrets, checkov, cdk-nag and npm-audit, plus any scanners named with --scanners
  • Simplified output and no progress display
  • Scans the whole source directory, not only staged or changed files; add --changed-files-only to report only the findings in changed files (every file is still scanned)
  • In workspace mode it changes only the output; it does not narrow the scanner set
  • Ideal for git hooks and quick CI checks

docs.title: Nix Mode
docs.text:
ash --mode nix
  • Runs the scan inside nix develop, whose shell supplies every scanner at a pinned version
  • Always runs offline
  • Linux and macOS; on Windows, run it in WSL2
  • See Nix mode

docs.title: Custom Plugins
docs.text: ASH v3 supports custom plugins for extending functionality:

docs.title: Creating Custom Plugins
docs.text:
1. Create a Python module with your plugins:
# my_ash_plugins/scanners.py
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_scanner_plugin
from automated_security_helper.base.scanner_plugin import (
    ScannerPluginBase,
    ScannerPluginConfigBase,
)
from pydantic import Field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Literal


class MyCustomScannerConfig(ScannerPluginConfigBase):
    """Configuration for MyCustomScanner"""

    class Options:
        custom_option: str = Field(default="default", description="Custom option")


@ash_scanner_plugin
class MyCustomScanner(ScannerPluginBase):
    """Custom scanner implementation"""

    name = "my-custom-scanner"
    description = "My custom security scanner"
    version = "1.0.0"

    def scan(
        self,
        target: Path,
        target_type: Literal["source", "converted"],
        global_ignore_paths: List = [],
        config=None,
    ):
        # Implement your scanning logic here
        results = self._run_subprocess(["my-scanner", "--target", str(target)])
        return results
  1. Add your module to ASH configuration:
ash_plugin_modules:
  - my_ash_plugins
  1. Use your custom scanner:
ash --ash-plugin-modules my_ash_plugins

docs.title: Offline Mode
docs.text:
For air-gapped environments:

# Build an offline image
ash build-image --offline --offline-semgrep-rulesets p/ci

# Run in offline mode
ash --mode container --offline

# On a host without network access, run the image without rebuilding it
ash --mode container --offline --no-build

Container mode builds the image before every scan unless given --no-build. Without --force, a build upgrades the OS packages and, offline, downloads the databases and rulesets once per UTC day, and is served from the build cache for the rest of that day, so the first build on a new day needs network access. With --force, every build does all of it again.

An offline image's databases are frozen at build time, and ASH fails a scan whose database is past its bound: grype's 5 days (120h) after it was built, the offline semgrep and opengrep rulesets 30 days after they were downloaded. Rebuild the image (ash build-image --offline) at least that often. To scan with an older image anyway, pass --allow-stale-content-db or set content_db_staleness: warn; the scan then passes and every report names the stale database. See Failing on a stale content database.

docs.title: Which scanners run offline
docs.text:
Offline mode is decided when each scanner runs, from these sources in order:

  1. ASH's offline mode: --offline on ash scan, ASH_OFFLINE=true in the environment, or an image built with ash build-image --offline. It applies to every scanner, and no scanner option turns it off.
  2. A scanner's own options.offline: true (checkov, grype, opengrep, semgrep, syft, trivy, trivy-repo). It runs that one scanner offline while the rest of the scan stays online. npm-audit has the option too, and it makes npm-audit MISSING (or SKIPPED without a lockfile) rather than run it offline; see below.

options.offline: false is the default and means "follow ASH's offline mode". It does not put a scanner back online during an --offline scan; ash config init writes offline: false for every scanner that has the option, so a generated config would otherwise undo the flag.

docs.title: What offline mode turns off
docs.text:
Online and offline, trivy, trivy-repo and syft read no config file from the scanned tree, because a trivy.yaml there can turn on a VEX repository download or client/server mode and a .syft.yaml remote license and package lookups. trivy always gets --config, naming the operator's config_file, else TRIVY_CONFIG when that is a file outside the scanned tree, and an empty config ASH ships otherwise; syft runs from outside the tree and is given only a config_file outside it.

Besides the database and rule downloads, offline mode turns off what the scanners do over the network on their own:

  • Every scanner tool process ASH starts, the version probes of its dependency check included, gets environment variables that turn off each tool's update, version and telemetry checks: semgrep's version check and metrics (SEMGREP_ENABLE_VERSION_CHECK=0, SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off), checkov's PyPI update check (CKV_SKIP_PACKAGE_UPDATE_CHECK=true), npm's update notifier (npm_config_update_notifier=false), trivy's version check and telemetry (TRIVY_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK, TRIVY_DISABLE_TELEMETRY), and the update checks of syft and grype. They also turn off the lookups a tool's own config file can enable: syft's remote license searches, maven lookups and vcpkg git clones, and grype's external sources. On a Go module syft does not run the Go toolchain (SYFT_GOLANG_USE_PACKAGES_LIB=false), and the toolchain grype runs gets GOPROXY=off and GOTOOLCHAIN=local, so it downloads no module and no toolchain. The full list is in automated_security_helper/utils/offline_tool_env.py. A scanner set offline by its own options.offline: true while ASH runs online gets them too, on its scan and on the version probes of its dependency check.
  • trivy's version check and telemetry are off whatever disable_telemetry says, through TRIVY_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK and TRIVY_DISABLE_TELEMETRY rather than flags, which a trivy too old to know them would refuse.
  • trivy-repo, and trivy when misconfig is in its scanners, do not run trivy's Terraform checks offline. trivy downloads the source of every module block a .tf file names (from the Terraform registry, with the host's git, or over HTTPS), and has no setting that stops it, so ASH passes --misconfig-scanners with trivy's own default list minus terraform. If that list cannot be read from trivy repository --help (trivy fs --help for trivy), trivy's misconfiguration checks are skipped offline. checkov still checks Terraform. Any git a tool runs offline gets GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file, so it reaches no remote.
  • npm-audit runs no audit, because npm, pnpm and yarn audit only against the package registry's advisory service: offline npm audit --offline reported no advisories for a lockfile with known ones, pnpm audit --offline sent the dependency list to the registry anyway, and yarn npm audit has no offline mode. Every lockfile it would have audited is listed as not scanned, with the reason, in ash_aggregated_results.json (the scanner's inputs_not_scanned), the console summary, and the "Inputs not scanned" section of ash.summary.md and ash.summary.txt. A workspace scan lists every project's, with workspace-relative paths, in each project's inputs_not_scanned entry in the workspace results, the merged summaries and the workspace console summary. When there is a lockfile, npm-audit is MISSING, as snyk-code is, so the scan fails under the default completeness gate (exit code 1). To scan a Node.js project offline without it, pass --exclude-scanners npm-audit. A project with no lockfile has nothing to audit, and npm-audit is SKIPPED.
  • detect-secrets does not verify candidate secrets with their issuers, whatever the scanned repository's .secrets.baseline or any config says. See Secret verification.

docs.title: Seeding the semgrep and opengrep rule cache
docs.text:
Offline, semgrep and opengrep read their rules only from a local cache: the directory named by SEMGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR or OPENGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR, which must contain at least one .yaml or .yml rule file. If the variable is unset or the directory has no rule files, that scanner is reported MISSING and the scan exits 1. ASH does not fall back to downloading the rules.

For the container, build the image with --offline. The build downloads each ruleset in --offline-semgrep-rulesets (space-separated, default p/ci) into /deps/.semgrep and /deps/.opengrep and sets both variables:

ash build-image --offline --offline-semgrep-rulesets "p/ci p/python"

For a local scan, download the rulesets yourself while online, using the same URL the image build uses, and record the download time in .ash-rules-fetched-at next to them. ASH reads that file to hold the rules to their 30-day bound; without it, it falls back to the oldest rule file's modification time, which a copy resets.

export SEMGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/.cache/ash/semgrep"
export OPENGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/.cache/ash/opengrep"
mkdir -p "$SEMGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR" "$OPENGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR"
for ruleset in p/ci; do
  curl -sSf "https://semgrep.dev/c/${ruleset}" -o "$SEMGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR/$(basename "$ruleset").yml"
done
cp "$SEMGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR"/*.yml "$OPENGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR/"
date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ | tee "$SEMGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR/.ash-rules-fetched-at" \
  > "$OPENGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR/.ash-rules-fetched-at"

ash --mode local --offline

Copy the cache directories to the air-gapped host and export the same two variables there. Repeat the download at least every 30 days, or the scan fails as stale.

Under --sandbox, the sandbox mounts the directory each variable names read-only for its scanner, wherever it is, including under $HOME, which the sandbox otherwise hides. Only the variable in ASH's own environment grants it: a rules path in a scanner's options, which the scanned repository can set, is not mounted, and an empty or relative value grants nothing. A variable naming a file, /, $HOME or a directory that holds $HOME is not mounted either, with a warning; point it at the rules directory itself. If semgrep or opengrep still cannot read its rules, it exits 7 and is recorded ERROR, and the scan exits 1.

docs.title: Customizing Scan Phases
docs.text:
ASH v3 executes scans in phases:

# Run only specific phases
ash --phases convert,scan

# Skip report generation
ash --phases convert,scan

# Include inspection phase
ash --phases convert,scan,report,inspect

docs.title: Using Existing Results
docs.text:
You can generate reports from existing scan results:

# Use existing results file
ash --use-existing --output-dir /path/to/results

# Generate a specific report format
ash report --format html --output-dir /path/to/results

docs.title: Interactive Findings Explorer
docs.text:
ASH v3 includes an interactive TUI for exploring findings:

# Launch the findings explorer
ash inspect findings --output-dir /path/to/results

A finding's detail view shows the code snippet its results hold. For a finding with none, it shows the lines around the finding from its file, but only when the results are in the scanned directory's .ash/ash_output (the default output directory), and only from a regular file inside that directory. A hard link inside the tree counts as a file in it, as it does for the scanners. A FIFO, a device, a path outside the directory, a symlink that leads out of it, or results in any other directory show "(source not shown)".

docs.title: Using Alternative Container Runtimes
docs.text:
# Use Podman instead of Docker
ash --mode container --oci-runner podman

# Use Finch
ash --mode container --oci-runner finch

docs.title: Custom Container Images
docs.text:
ASH does not publish a container image to a public registry. Building it yourself and hosting it in your own registry is the recommended posture, so that the provenance and patching cadence of the image that reads your source code belong to you. See Building your own container image for the reasoning, the rebuild cadence it commits you to, and offline builds.

# Specify a custom container image
export ASH_IMAGE_NAME="my-registry/ash:custom"
ash --mode container

docs.title: Building Custom Images
docs.text:
# Build a custom image
ash build-image --build-target ci --custom-containerfile ./my-dockerfile

docs.title: Advanced Configuration Overrides
docs.text:
# Complex configuration overrides
ash --config-overrides 'scanners.semgrep.options.config=p/owasp-top-ten'
ash --config-overrides 'global_settings.ignore_paths+=[{"path": "build/", "reason": "Generated files"}]'

docs.title: Adding Suppressions via Config Overrides
docs.text:
# Add a suppression rule
ash --config-overrides 'global_settings.suppressions+=[{"rule_id": "RULE-123", "path": "src/example.py", "reason": "False positive"}]'

# Add a suppression with line range and expiration
ash --config-overrides 'global_settings.suppressions+=[{"rule_id": "RULE-456", "path": "src/*.js", "line_start": 10, "line_end": 15, "reason": "Known issue", "expiration": "2025-12-31"}]'

docs.title: Inline code suppressions
docs.text:
You can suppress individual findings directly in your source code using special comments. This is useful when a suppression only applies to a single line and you want the context to live next to the code.

Two directives are supported:

Directive Effect # ash-ignore: <rule-id> [reason] Suppresses the finding on the same line as the comment. # ash-ignore-next-line: <rule-id> [reason] Suppresses the finding on the next line.

The directives are case-insensitive. The reason text is optional but recommended.

# Suppress a specific rule on the same line:
password = os.environ[
    "DB_PASS"
]  # ash-ignore: CKV-SEC-001 loaded from env, not hardcoded

# Suppress a specific rule on the next line:
# ash-ignore-next-line: BANDIT-B105 password variable is a placeholder
password = "changeme"

// Languages that use // comments (JS, TS, Java, C#, Go):
const key = process.env.KEY; // ash-ignore: SEC-KEY env var is safe

// Or suppress the next line:
// ash-ignore-next-line: SEC-KEY env var is safe
const key = process.env.KEY;

Both inline and config-file suppressions use Kind1.inSource in the SARIF output. They are distinguishable by their justification prefix: config suppressions start with "(ASH)" while inline suppressions start with "(ASH inline)".

docs.title: Temporarily Ignoring Suppressions
docs.text:
# Run a scan ignoring all suppression rules, ignore_paths included
ash --ignore-suppressions

# Useful for verifying if suppressed issues have been fixed
ash --ignore-suppressions --output-dir ./verification-scan

docs.title: Programmatic Usage
docs.text:
ASH v3 can be used programmatically in Python:

from automated_security_helper.interactions.run_ash_scan import run_ash_scan
from automated_security_helper.core.enums import ExecutionStrategy, RunMode

# Run a scan
results = run_ash_scan(
    source_dir="/path/to/code",
    output_dir="/path/to/output",
    mode=RunMode.local,
    strategy=ExecutionStrategy.PARALLEL,
    scanners=["bandit", "semgrep"],
    config_overrides=["scanners.bandit.enabled=true"],
    # Return the results even when there are actionable findings
    fail_on_findings=False,
)

# Access scan results
stats = results.metadata.summary_stats
print(f"Found {stats.total} findings, {stats.actionable} actionable")

run_ash_scan takes keyword arguments from its signature only. An unknown one, such as a misspelled fail_on_finding, raises TypeError naming it; earlier versions accepted it and ran the scan without it.

The call returns the aggregated results only when the scan's exit code is 0. Otherwise it ends the way ash scan does, by raising SystemExit with that code (see Exit codes): 2 for actionable findings while fail_on_findings is on, which is the default, and 1 for an incomplete scan, for example a selected scanner whose tool is not installed. That exit 1 is a ScanIncompleteExit, a SystemExit subclass whose incompleteness attribute names what was incomplete (the scanners and converters that did not run, and any stale content databases) and whose results attribute holds the results. A run ASH refuses or gives up (3 for a config that does not validate or files git tracks where the scan writes, 5 for a scanner selection that names nothing, 1 for an error during the scan) raises ScanRefusedExit, a SystemExit subclass whose message attribute is the text ash scan prints for it.

docs.title: Logging to your own handler
docs.text:
ASH logs through the ash logger. A handler your application puts on it stays there when a scan sets up ASH's logging, and it gets ASH's records as written: file names and tool output from the scanned repository in them included, such as a line that starts with :: or holds ##vso[, which a CI runner reads as a command. To have your handler write them as ASH's own console and log file do, with control characters as escapes and CI command lines broken, give it CommandSafeFormatter:

import logging

from automated_security_helper.utils.log import CommandSafeFormatter

handler = logging.StreamHandler()
handler.setFormatter(CommandSafeFormatter("%(levelname)s %(message)s"))
logging.getLogger("ash").addHandler(handler)

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text: Tip: The examples below use pinned versions (@v3.7.0) for reproducibility. You can also use the v3 floating tag (@v3) to always get the latest stable v3.x release, though pinned versions are recommended for CI/CD.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
name: ASH Security Scan

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'
      - name: Install ASH
        run: pip install git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0
      - name: Run ASH scan
        run: ash --mode local
      - name: Upload scan results
        # Also when ASH exits non-zero on findings: without a status function
        # GitHub skips this step after any failed step.
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: ash-results
          path: |
            .ash/ash_output/reports
            .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json

docs.title: GitLab CI
docs.text:
ash-scan:
  image: python:3.10
  script:
    - pip install git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0
    - ash --mode local
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - .ash/ash_output/reports
      - .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json

Both examples keep scanners/ and converted/ out of the artifact: those hold each tool's raw output, which is not masked.

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
# Run scanners in parallel (default)
ash --strategy parallel

# Run scanners sequentially
ash --strategy sequential

# Clean up temporary files after scan
ash --cleanup

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
# Enable debug logging
ash --debug

# Enable verbose logging
ash --verbose

# Disable progress display
ash --no-progress

docs.title: Scanner Validation
docs.text:
ASH v3 includes comprehensive scanner validation that monitors scanner registration, enablement, and execution throughout the scan process. When debugging scanner issues:

  • Check logs for validation warnings about missing or disabled scanners
  • Use --debug to see detailed validation checkpoint information
  • Look for specific reasons why scanners might be disabled (dependencies, configuration, etc.)
  • Run the integration verification test: python verify_integration.py (if available in your installation)

The validation system includes result completeness validation that ensures all originally registered scanners appear in the final scan results, even if they failed or were disabled. This provides complete visibility into scan coverage and helps identify any scanners that may have been silently dropped during the scan process.

For detailed information about the scanner validation system, see the Scanner Validation System developer guide.

docs.title: ScanOptions
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

All parameters for a single run_ash_scan invocation.

Source code in automated_security_helper/interactions/run_ash_scan.py 
class ScanOptions(BaseModel):
    """All parameters for a single run_ash_scan invocation."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    # Core paths
    source_dir: Path
    output_dir: Path

    # Workspace mode. When set, source_dir is the workspace ROOT and each project
    # is scanned with its own source_dir inside it. None means single-directory
    # mode, which is the only shape the rest of this module handles.
    workspace_plan: Optional[WorkspacePlan] = None
    allow_missing_projects: bool = False
    # The --workspace-config value as the operator spelled it, when one was
    # given. The plan holds the resolved policy path (the file read); container
    # mode hands the policy over by this name instead, so a policy named inside
    # the workspace's tree that links out of it is refused as an in-tree
    # --config that links out is.
    workspace_config_as_named: Optional[str] = None

    # General scan options
    config: Optional[str] = None
    config_overrides: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    # A check every `extends` base of the config must also pass, applied by every
    # config read below. The MCP server passes the calling session's allowed
    # config roots (cli/mcp/sandbox.config_base_gate); None keeps the CLI rule.
    config_base_gate: Optional[Callable[[Path], bool]] = Field(
        default=None, exclude=True
    )
    # The config was written by the caller (an MCP client's upload), so its sandbox
    # settings are restrict-only; trusted_config_path is the operator's config the
    # grants come from instead. Both go to resolve_config, in local mode only.
    untrusted_config: bool = False
    trusted_config_path: Optional[str] = None
    # config_overrides came from an MCP client (a workspace tool's), so a tool
    # config path they name is not the operator's (config/path_trust.py).
    client_overrides: bool = False
    # The scan was started by a remote MCP client (cli/mcp/sandbox.caller_is_remote),
    # so every config file the operator did not set aside resolves no !ENV; see
    # "Environment variables" in config/config_sources.py. Applied by every config
    # read below, and carried to each project in workspace mode.
    remote_client: bool = False
    # The session's ClientConfigRules, which a config file an MCP client
    # delivered is checked against. Goes to
    # resolve_config, in local mode only. Typed Any to keep config imports out of
    # this module's import time, as the other config inputs here are.
    client_config_policy: Optional[Any] = Field(default=None, exclude=True)
    # A threshold the scan must be at least as strict as: it runs at the stricter
    # of this and the config's global severity_threshold. The MCP server passes a
    # client's severity_threshold here, which may tighten the configured one and
    # never loosen it. Local mode only.
    severity_threshold_restriction: Optional[str] = None
    # Keep the previous scan's results until this scan has its own, instead of
    # deleting them when it starts (core/previous_results.py). For the MCP server,
    # which settles them itself: a scan that returns leaves them set aside, and
    # the caller drops them once it has decided the scan has results, or puts
    # them back. A scan that fails inside the orchestrator has them put back
    # there. In workspace mode it reaches each project's orchestrator, which then
    # drops them itself once the project's phases finish. Local and workspace mode
    # only; the CLI never sets it.
    keep_previous_results: bool = False
    offline: bool = False
    strategy: ExecutionStrategy = ExecutionStrategy.PARALLEL
    scanners: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    excluded_scanners: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    # Who gave the two lists above: "mcp" only from the MCP workspace tool, whose
    # SKIPPED rows and selection refusals then name its scanners and
    # excluded_scanners parameters instead of the CLI's flags.
    selection_origin: SelectionOrigin = "cli"
    progress: bool = True
    output_formats: Optional[List[ExportFormat]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    cleanup: bool = False
    phases: Optional[List[ExecutionPhase]] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: [
            ExecutionPhase.CONVERT,
            ExecutionPhase.SCAN,
            ExecutionPhase.REPORT,
        ]
    )
    inspect: bool = False
    existing_results: Optional[str] = None
    python_based_plugins_only: bool = False
    quiet: bool = False
    simple: bool = False
    verbose: bool = False
    debug: bool = False
    color: bool = True
    fail_on_findings: Optional[bool] = None
    # Fail when a selected scanner did not complete. None means "not set on the
    # command line", which defers to the config file and then to off. Kept
    # separate from fail_on_findings rather than folded into it because the two
    # answer different questions: whether anything was found, and whether the
    # scanners that were supposed to look actually ran.
    fail_on_incomplete_scanners: Optional[bool] = None
    ignore_suppressions: bool = False
    min_severity: str = "low"
    changed_files_only: bool = False
    base_ref: str = "origin/main"
    # One shard of a split scan, or both None for an ordinary whole scan. Left
    # unvalidated here on purpose: ScanPhase._execute_phase is the single place
    # that refuses an unusable pair, so a second rule in this model could drift
    # from it and start rejecting a selection the scan phase would have accepted
    # (or the reverse). The CLI validates early for the operator's benefit; that
    # is presentation, not the contract.
    shard_index: Optional[int] = None
    shard_count: Optional[int] = None
    mode: RunMode = RunMode.local
    show_summary: bool = True
    log_level: AshLogLevel = AshLogLevel.INFO

    # Container-specific
    build: bool = True
    run: bool = True
    force: bool = False
    oci_runner: Optional[str] = None
    build_target: Optional[BuildTarget] = None
    offline_semgrep_rulesets: str = "p/ci"
    container_uid: Optional[str] = None
    container_gid: Optional[str] = None
    ash_revision_to_install: Optional[str] = None
    custom_containerfile: Optional[str] = None
    custom_build_arg: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    ash_plugin_modules: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    container_network: str = "bridge"

    @field_validator("source_dir", "output_dir", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _coerce_absolute_path(cls, v):
        return Path(v).absolute()

    @field_validator("min_severity", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _known_min_severity(cls, v):
        # The library and MCP entry point reaches here without the CLI's choice
        # check, so this is where an unknown value is refused for every caller.
        value = v.value if isinstance(v, MinSeverity) else v
        accepted = [member.value for member in MinSeverity]
        if not isinstance(value, str) or value.lower() not in accepted:
            raise ValueError(
                f"min_severity must be one of {', '.join(accepted)} (any case), "
                f"not {v!r}"
            )
        return value

    @field_validator(
        "scanners",
        "excluded_scanners",
        "output_formats",
        "config_overrides",
        "custom_build_arg",
        "ash_plugin_modules",
        mode="before",
    )
    @classmethod
    def _none_to_empty_list(cls, v):
        return v if v is not None else []

    @field_validator("phases", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _phases_default(cls, v):
        if v is None:
            return [ExecutionPhase.CONVERT, ExecutionPhase.SCAN, ExecutionPhase.REPORT]
        return v

docs.title: IncompleteConverter
docs.text:
Bases: NamedTuple

One incomplete_converters row: the converter, why, and what failed.

kinds is the distinct kind of the non-accepted failed-input records behind the reason, sorted, plus the marker "limit" for a row whose refused_inputs name an extraction limit; empty for a converter that did not run (a crash, or dependencies unsatisfied). Carried as data rather than as the reason's type, so a string operation or a JSON round trip keeps it and the MCP payload can pass it to clients; the console chooses its advice from it. Indexes like the (name, reason) pair it grew from, so a hand-built pair still reads as a row with no kinds.

Source code in automated_security_helper/interactions/run_ash_scan.py 
class IncompleteConverter(NamedTuple):
    """One ``incomplete_converters`` row: the converter, why, and what failed.

    ``kinds`` is the distinct ``kind`` of the non-accepted failed-input records
    behind the reason, sorted, plus the marker ``"limit"`` for a row whose
    ``refused_inputs`` name an extraction limit; empty for a converter that did
    not run (a crash, or dependencies unsatisfied). Carried as data rather than
    as the reason's type, so a string operation or a JSON round trip keeps it
    and the MCP payload can pass it to clients; the console chooses its advice
    from it. Indexes like the (name, reason) pair it grew from, so a hand-built
    pair still reads as a row with no kinds.
    """

    name: str
    reason: str
    kinds: Tuple[str, ...] = ()

docs.title: ScanIncompleteness dataclass
docs.text:
Every reason a finished scan exits 1 for coverage rather than for a crash.

One field per arm of the exit-1 half of _compute_exit_code, which reads its verdict from this object rather than from its own calls to the primitives. That is what makes it safe for anything else to act on: the MCP runner reports a scan incomplete instead of failed from this object, and if the two read the question separately, the status a client sees and the exit code the CLI returns could disagree on the same results.

Truthy when any field is set. Empty for results is None, which also exits 1 but means no results exist. That is a crash, and it does not belong in here.

Source code in automated_security_helper/interactions/run_ash_scan.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScanIncompleteness:
    """Every reason a finished scan exits 1 for coverage rather than for a crash.

    One field per arm of the exit-1 half of ``_compute_exit_code``, which reads its
    verdict from this object rather than from its own calls to the primitives. That
    is what makes it safe for anything else to act on: the MCP runner reports a scan
    ``incomplete`` instead of ``failed`` from this object, and if the two read the
    question separately, the status a client sees and the exit code the CLI returns
    could disagree on the same results.

    Truthy when any field is set. Empty for ``results is None``, which also exits
    1 but means no results exist. That is a crash, and it does not belong in here.
    """

    #: ``incomplete_scanners`` rows: (name, display status).
    scanners: Tuple[Tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
    #: Names from ``scanners`` whose recorded counts show a partial audit
    #: (``0 < failed < attempted``), whatever status the writer graded. The
    #: payload's reason token reads ``partial_coverage`` for these; see
    #: :func:`incomplete_scanner_reason`.
    partial_coverage: Tuple[str, ...] = ()
    #: Every scanner's recorded status, the raw token rather than the display
    #: string, so a payload can say MISSING or ERROR without parsing prose.
    observed: Tuple[Tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
    #: The set-level arm: scanners were expected or recorded, and none reached a
    #: verdict.
    no_scanner_ran: bool = False
    #: ``incomplete_converters`` rows.
    converters: Tuple["IncompleteConverter", ...] = ()
    #: ``unevaluated_rules``. Not behind the completeness gate.
    unevaluated_rules: Tuple[str, ...] = ()
    #: Content databases past their declared bound under ``content_db_staleness:
    #: fail``. Not behind the completeness gate either; its opt-out is
    #: ``--allow-stale-content-db`` or ``content_db_staleness: warn``, under which
    #: nothing is recorded here.
    stale_content_databases: Tuple[ContentDbAgeRecord, ...] = ()
    #: (name, missing_reason) for each MISSING scanner in ``scanners`` that recorded
    #: one, so the console can say why it did not run. Not a cause of exit 1 on its
    #: own and not in the payload, which carries the rows.
    missing_reasons: Tuple[Tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
    #: (name, reason) for each scanner whose run ended with a tool ASH could not
    #: stop; the reason names the process id. Not behind the completeness gate:
    #: the tool may still write into the output directory after the gate has read
    #: it, so this one fails the run whatever the gate says.
    could_not_stop: Tuple[Tuple[str, str], ...] = ()

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return bool(
            self.scanners
            or self.no_scanner_ran
            or self.converters
            or self.unevaluated_rules
            or self.stale_content_databases
            or self.could_not_stop
        )

    def to_payload(self) -> Dict[str, object]:

                    "reason": row[1],

                for row in self.converters
            ],
            "unevaluated_rules": list(self.unevaluated_rules),
            "stale_content_databases": [
                record.to_dict() for record in self.stale_content_databases
            ],
            "could_not_stop": [
                {"scanner": name, "reason": reason}

def scanner_statuses(
    results: Optional[AshAggregatedResults],
) -> List[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(name, status) for every scanner in *results*, in scanner-name order.

    What :func:`no_scanner_ran` reads, and read through
    ``get_unified_scanner_metrics`` for the same reason
    :func:`incomplete_scanners` does: that function is what every reporter and the
    metrics table already use, so the set-level gate answers from the statuses the
    operator was shown rather than from a second, independently-derived read of
    ``results.scanner_results``.

    Deliberately just the pairs. An earlier form of this shared one pass with
    ``incomplete_scanners`` by filtering these pairs, which stopped being possible
    when that function grew a second arm reading the per-metric target counters --
    a shortfall is not visible in a (name, status) pair. Keeping this narrow is
    what makes the two gates independently correct; the cost is one extra pass over
    the metrics, which ``_compute_exit_code`` already takes for the findings count.

docs.title: no_scanner_ran(observed, expected=None, ran_against_a_stale_database=(), audited_some_targets=())
docs.text:
True when this run reached no verdict about the target.

Two conditions, and the second exists because the first could not express it.

  1. observed is non-empty and none of its scanners reached a verdict. SKIPPED has to be tolerated one entry at a time -- it is how sharding and --exclude-scanners record work a run was never meant to do -- so a file in which every entry is SKIPPED clears the per-scanner pass while having measured nothing.

  2. observed is empty AND expected is not. An empty scanner set used to be exempt unconditionally, on the reasoning that it is reachable from a legitimate --phases convert run. That reasoning is sound but covers two different states, and a boolean over observed alone cannot separate them: "the scan phase was not requested", which is benign, and "the scan phase ran and had nothing to run", which is the silent-zero case this gate exists for.

expected is what separates them, and it needs no new state to do it. ScanPhase is what records metadata.expected_scanners, so a recorded roster means the scan phase ran; no roster and no scanners means it never did.

Defaults to None so a results file written by a version that recorded no roster -- which ash merge reads, from whatever ASH produced each shard -- keeps the old benign reading rather than becoming a failure on upgrade.

ran_against_a_stale_database names scanners recorded ERROR because their clean result came from a database the policy rejects (scanners_in_error_for_a_stale_database). They reached a verdict, so they count as having run, as they did when that result was recorded PASSED; the stale database fails the scan through its own arm.

audited_some_targets names ERROR scanners whose recorded counts show a partial audit (0 < failed < attempted, :func:_partial_coverage). A scanner that evaluated some of its targets and lost the rest ran: when its survivors are clean the loss grades it ERROR, and "no scanner reached a verdict" would contradict the "4 of 10 targets unevaluated" line printed beside it. The loss itself still fails the scan through the incomplete-scanner arm.

def no_scanner_ran(
    observed: List[tuple[str, str]],
    expected: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    ran_against_a_stale_database: Collection[str] = (),
    audited_some_targets: Collection[str] = (),
) -> bool:
    """True when this run reached no verdict about the target.

    Two conditions, and the second exists because the first could not express it.

    1. *observed* is non-empty and none of its scanners reached a verdict. SKIPPED
       has to be tolerated one entry at a time -- it is how sharding and
       ``--exclude-scanners`` record work a run was never meant to do -- so a file
       in which every entry is SKIPPED clears the per-scanner pass while having
       measured nothing.

    2. *observed* is empty AND *expected* is not. An empty scanner set used to be
       exempt unconditionally, on the reasoning that it is reachable from a
       legitimate ``--phases convert`` run. That reasoning is sound but covers two
       different states, and a boolean over ``observed`` alone cannot separate
       them: "the scan phase was not requested", which is benign, and "the scan
       phase ran and had nothing to run", which is the silent-zero case this gate
       exists for.

    *expected* is what separates them, and it needs no new state to do it.
    ``ScanPhase`` is what records ``metadata.expected_scanners``, so a recorded
    roster means the scan phase ran; no roster and no scanners means it never did.

    Defaults to None so a results file written by a version that recorded no roster
    -- which ``ash merge`` reads, from whatever ASH produced each shard -- keeps the
    old benign reading rather than becoming a failure on upgrade.

    *ran_against_a_stale_database* names scanners recorded ERROR because their clean
    result came from a database the policy rejects
    (``scanners_in_error_for_a_stale_database``). They reached a verdict, so they
    count as having run, as they did when that result was recorded PASSED; the stale
    database fails the scan through its own arm.

    *audited_some_targets* names ERROR scanners whose recorded counts show a partial
    audit (``0 < failed < attempted``, :func:`_partial_coverage`). A scanner that
    evaluated some of its targets and lost the rest ran: when its survivors are clean
    the loss grades it ERROR, and "no scanner reached a verdict" would contradict the
    "4 of 10 targets unevaluated" line printed beside it. The loss itself still
    fails the scan through the incomplete-scanner arm.
    """
    if not observed:
        return bool(expected)
    return not any(
        status in _RAN_SCANNER_STATUSES
        or name in ran_against_a_stale_database
        or (status == ScannerStatus.ERROR.value and name in audited_some_targets)
        for name, status in observed
    )

A scanner that counts its targets says so with targets_attempted 0, which is graded SKIPPED: bandit with no Python file it was not told to exclude, detect-secrets with every file of its scan set ignored. def scanners_with_nothing_to_scan(
    results: Optional[AshAggregatedResults],
) -> List[str]:
    """The scanners that were SKIPPED because they had no file to scan.

    A scanner that counts its targets says so with ``targets_attempted`` 0, which is
    graded SKIPPED: bandit with no Python file it was not told to exclude,
    detect-secrets with every file of its scan set ignored. A scanner that was not
    selected, or that declined this platform, is SKIPPED too but carries no count,
    so it is not listed: it made no claim about the files.
    """
    if results is None:
        return []
    names = []
    for metric in get_unified_scanner_metrics(asharp_model=results):
        attempted = getattr(metric, "targets_attempted", None)
        if (
            metric.status == ScannerStatus.SKIPPED.value
            and isinstance(attempted, int)
            and not isinstance(attempted, bool)
            and attempted == 0
        ):
            names.append(metric.scanner_name)
    return names
