docs.title: Converter Plugins
docs.text:
Converter plugins transform files before scanning to make them compatible with security scanners. For example, converting Jupyter notebooks to Python files.

For detailed visual diagrams of converter plugin architecture and workflow, see Converter Plugin Diagrams.

docs.title: Converter Plugin Interface
docs.text:
A converter subclasses ConverterPluginBase and implements convert(self):

from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Literal

from automated_security_helper.base.converter_plugin import (
    ConverterPluginBase,
    ConverterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_converter_plugin


class MyConverterConfig(ConverterPluginConfigBase):
    name: Literal["my-converter"] = "my-converter"


@ash_converter_plugin
class MyConverter(ConverterPluginBase[MyConverterConfig]):
    """My custom converter implementation"""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = MyConverterConfig()
        return super().model_post_init(context)

    def convert(self) -> List[Path]:
        """Convert this converter's inputs and return the files written."""
        return []

ASH calls convert() once per scan, with no arguments. The converter:

  • finds its inputs under self.context.source_dir, usually from the scan set (automated_security_helper.utils.get_scan_set.scan_set, which applies .gitignore and .ignore files), skipping the config's global_settings.ignore_paths;
  • reads each input through self.open_source_file(path), which refuses a symlink or a path outside the scanned directory, and passes a refusal to self.record_refused_input();
  • writes its output under self.results_dir, which is <output-dir>/converted/<converter name>;
  • returns the list of paths it wrote, or an empty list when there was nothing to convert.

ASH then scans the files under <output-dir>/converted as a second target, of type converted.

A converter written as convert(self, target), the signature ConverterPluginBase declared in earlier versions, does not run: ASH refuses any convert() that requires an argument, and the converter's row records an error that names it and says to declare convert(self).

docs.title: Converter Plugin Configuration
docs.text:
Define a configuration class for your converter. Options go in a class derived from ConverterOptionsBase:

from typing import Annotated, List, Literal

from pydantic import Field

from automated_security_helper.base.converter_plugin import ConverterPluginConfigBase
from automated_security_helper.base.options import ConverterOptionsBase


class MyConverterConfigOptions(ConverterOptionsBase):
    suffixes: List[str] = Field(
        default=[".py.tmpl"],
        description="File name endings to convert into .py files",
    )


class MyConverterConfig(ConverterPluginConfigBase):
    name: Literal["my-converter"] = "my-converter"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: Annotated[
        MyConverterConfigOptions,
        Field(description="Configure my-converter"),
    ] = MyConverterConfigOptions()

docs.title: Converter Plugin Example
docs.text:
Here is a complete converter. It is the converter of the example plugin package in the ASH repository, examples/ash_plugins_example, which a test runs through a real scan. It copies each Python template in the scan set, *.py.tmpl, to a .py file, so that scanners which select files by extension read it too:

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, List, Literal

from pydantic import Field

from automated_security_helper.base.converter_plugin import (
    ConverterPluginBase,
    ConverterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.base.options import ConverterOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_converter_plugin
from automated_security_helper.utils.get_scan_set import scan_set
from automated_security_helper.utils.log import ASH_LOGGER
from automated_security_helper.utils.scanned_tree import TreeInputRefused
from automated_security_helper.utils.suppression_matcher import file_path_matches


class ExampleConverterConfigOptions(ConverterOptionsBase):
    suffixes: List[str] = Field(
        default=[".py.tmpl"],
        description="File name endings to convert into .py files",
    )


class ExampleConverterConfig(ConverterPluginConfigBase):
    """Configuration for the example converter."""

    name: Literal["my-example-converter"] = "my-example-converter"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: Annotated[
        ExampleConverterConfigOptions,
        Field(description="Configure my-example-converter"),
    ] = ExampleConverterConfigOptions()


@ash_converter_plugin
class ExampleConverter(ConverterPluginBase[ExampleConverterConfig]):
    """Copies Python templates (``*.py.tmpl``) to ``.py`` files the scanners read."""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        # Do not assign to self.context: it is shared by every plugin in the run.
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = ExampleConverterConfig()
        return super().model_post_init(context)

    def validate_plugin_dependencies(self) -> bool:
        """Pure Python, so there is nothing to install."""
        return True

    def convert(self) -> List[Path]:
        source_dir = Path(self.context.source_dir)
        suffixes = tuple(self.config.options.suffixes)
        ignore_paths = self.context.config.global_settings.ignore_paths or []

        written: List[Path] = []
        for name in scan_set(source=source_dir, output=self.context.output_dir):
            # Only the line ending a cached list leaves: "a.py.tmpl " is its own file.
            candidate = Path(name.rstrip("\n"))
            if not candidate.name.endswith(suffixes) or not candidate.is_file():
                continue
            relative = candidate.relative_to(source_dir)
            if any(
                file_path_matches(relative.as_posix(), ignore.path)
                for ignore in ignore_paths
            ):
                continue

            # Read through open_source_file, never open(): it refuses a symlink or
            # a path outside the scanned tree before anything is read.
            try:
                handle = self.open_source_file(candidate)
            except TreeInputRefused as refused:
                self.record_refused_input(refused)
                continue
            with handle:
                content = handle.read()

            suffix = next(s for s in suffixes if candidate.name.endswith(s))
            target = self.results_dir.joinpath(
                relative.parent, candidate.name[: -len(suffix)] + ".py"
            )
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(content)
            ASH_LOGGER.debug(f"ExampleConverter: {relative.as_posix()} -> {target}")
            written.append(target)

        return written

docs.title: Converter Plugin Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Preserve Line Numbers: Keep each converted line on the line it came from where you can, so a finding in the converted file points at the right place in the original
  2. Read Through open_source_file: Never open() an input by name; record a refused input with record_refused_input
  3. Write Under results_dir: Do not assign to self.context, which every plugin in the run shares
  4. Error Handling: Catch the errors a single input can raise, so one bad file does not stop the others; an exception out of convert() marks the whole converter failed
  5. Return Paths: Return the list of files written, or an empty list

docs.title: Converter Plugin Configuration in ASH
docs.text:
Configure your converter in the ASH configuration file:

# ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project)
converters:
  jupyter:
    enabled: true
    options:
      tool_version: null      # Version constraint for the conversion tool
      install_timeout: 300    # Seconds allowed for tool installation

docs.title: Testing Converter Plugins
docs.text:
Create unit tests for your converter. Construct it with a PluginContext and call convert():

from pathlib import Path

from automated_security_helper.base.plugin_context import PluginContext
from automated_security_helper.config.ash_config import AshConfig
from my_ash_plugins.converter import ExampleConverter


def test_example_converter(tmp_path):
    source = tmp_path / "src"
    source.mkdir()
    (source / "settings.py.tmpl").write_text("NAME = 'x'\n", encoding="utf-8")
    context = PluginContext(
        source_dir=source,
        output_dir=tmp_path / "out",
        config=AshConfig(project_name="converter-test"),
    )

    converter = ExampleConverter(context=context)
    written = converter.convert()

    assert [Path(p).name for p in written] == ["settings.py"]
    assert Path(written[0]).read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "NAME = 'x'\n"

docs.title: Plugin Development Guide
docs.text: This guide provides comprehensive information on developing custom plugins for ASH. Whether you're creating scanners, reporters, converters, or event subscribers, this document will help you understand the plugin architecture and development process.

docs.title: Plugin Architecture Overview
docs.text: ASH's plugin system is designed to be extensible and modular. Plugins are Python classes that inherit from base plugin classes and implement specific interfaces.

docs.title: Plugin Types
docs.text:
ASH supports four main types of plugins:

  1. Scanner Plugins: Analyze code and infrastructure for security issues
  2. Reporter Plugins: Generate reports in various formats
  3. Converter Plugins: Process files before scanning
  4. Event Subscribers: React to events during the scan lifecycle

docs.title: Plugin Lifecycle
docs.text:
All plugins follow a similar lifecycle:

  1. Registration: Plugins are registered with the plugin manager
  2. Configuration: Plugin settings are loaded from the ASH configuration
  3. Initialization: Plugins are initialized with required dependencies
  4. Execution: Plugins perform their specific tasks
  5. Cleanup: Plugins clean up resources when done

docs.title: Basic Plugin Structure
docs.text:
A plugin is a class derived from a base plugin class, paired with a config class whose name is the key used in the ASH configuration file. Options go in a class derived from the matching options base and sit under options in the config:

from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import Field

from automated_security_helper.base.options import ScannerOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.base.scanner_plugin import (
    ScannerPluginBase,
    ScannerPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_scanner_plugin


class MyCustomScannerConfigOptions(ScannerOptionsBase):
    custom_option: str = "default_value"


class MyCustomScannerConfig(ScannerPluginConfigBase):
    """Configuration for MyCustomScanner."""

    name: Literal["my-custom-scanner"] = "my-custom-scanner"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: Annotated[MyCustomScannerConfigOptions, Field()] = (
        MyCustomScannerConfigOptions()
    )


@ash_scanner_plugin
class MyCustomScanner(ScannerPluginBase[MyCustomScannerConfig]):
    """Custom scanner implementation."""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        # ASH constructs plugins with keyword arguments (context=..., config=...);
        # supply the default config here rather than overriding __init__.
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = MyCustomScannerConfig()
        return super().model_post_init(context)

    def validate_plugin_dependencies(self) -> bool:
        return True

    def _execute_scan(self, target, target_type, global_ignore_paths):
        """Return (argv, results_file, subprocess_env) for the tool to run."""
        raise NotImplementedError("see Scanner Plugin Development below")

A plugin class, and a config or options class derived from ASH's bases, inherits hide_input_in_errors=True. A validation error then names the field and the problem but not the value it refused: a config value can be a secret read from the environment, and the error's text can reach the console, the log and an MCP response. Keep that setting if a class sets its own model_config. pydantic merges a subclass's settings with its base's, so leaving the key out keeps it.

If your validate_plugin_dependencies can start the tool where a PATH lookup does not find it (it runs a library in-process, or finds the tool its own way), set resolves_tool_off_path: ClassVar[bool] = True on the class: ash dependencies install asks the check only for scanners that do, and judges the rest by the PATH lookup. The check is asked only when the PATH lookup fails, only for a plugin a scan here would run or one named with --tool, and never after one of the plugin's install commands failed or errored. A tool managed through uv tool run is judged by uv tool list instead, so the flag has no effect there. The check runs in check-only mode: ASH's own install helpers are skipped and every uv tool run probe runs --offline, but that mode cannot stop an install the check performs itself (its own pip install, for example), so a flagged check must answer without installing anything.

docs.title: Plugin Registration
docs.text: The @ash_scanner_plugin, @ash_reporter_plugin and @ash_converter_plugin decorators register a class when its module is imported. ASH imports the modules named in ash_plugin_modules in the configuration file or with --ash-plugin-modules; there is no separate registration call. A module named there must sit in a top-level package whose name ends in ash_plugins (for example my_ash_plugins, or ash_plugins itself), or be a module of ASH's own automated_security_helper package; ASH logs a warning for any other name.

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Development
docs.text: Scanner plugins analyze code and infrastructure for security issues.

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Interface
docs.text:
scan() is a template method rather than an abstract one: it owns the fixed sequence around a scan, and _execute_scan() is the abstract hook it calls for the tool-specific part.

class ScannerPluginBase(PluginBase, Generic[T]):
    """Base class for all scanner plugins."""

    @abstractmethod
    def _execute_scan(
        self,
        target: Path,
        target_type: Literal["source", "converted"],
        global_ignore_paths,
    ) -> Tuple[List[str], Path, Optional[dict]]:
        """Return (argv, results_file, subprocess_env) for this tool."""

    def scan(
        self,
        target: Path,
        target_type: Literal["source", "converted"],
        global_ignore_paths=None,
        config=None,
    ) -> Any | SarifReport | CycloneDXReport:
        """Template: preamble -> _execute_scan -> read results -> invocation -> postamble."""

Only _execute_scan() is required. A plugin that does not fit the template overrides scan() instead, and still declares _execute_scan() as a stub that raises — see Scanner Plugins for that variant. There is no abstract cleanup(); release resources in _post_scan() if you need to.

ASH calls scan() once for the source directory and, when a converter wrote files, once more for the converted files (target_type="converted"). Only a SarifReport carries findings into the reports. A dict is recorded as PASSED with 0 findings, so its findings are lost; return False when the scanner cannot run, which ASH records as MISSING.

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Example
docs.text:
A pure-Python scanner that reports lines matching a regular expression. It overrides scan() and returns a SarifReport:

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, List, Literal

from pydantic import Field

from automated_security_helper.base.options import ScannerOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.base.scanner_plugin import (
    ScannerPluginBase,
    ScannerPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_scanner_plugin
from automated_security_helper.schemas.sarif_schema_model import SarifReport
from automated_security_helper.utils.get_scan_set import scan_set
from automated_security_helper.utils.scanned_tree import (
    TreeInputRefused,
    open_in_scanned_tree,
)


class CustomRegexScannerConfigOptions(ScannerOptionsBase):
    patterns: List[str] = Field(
        default=[r"password\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]"],
        description="Regular expressions to report",
    )


class CustomRegexScannerConfig(ScannerPluginConfigBase):
    """Configuration for CustomRegexScanner."""

    name: Literal["custom-regex"] = "custom-regex"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: Annotated[CustomRegexScannerConfigOptions, Field()] = (
        CustomRegexScannerConfigOptions()
    )


@ash_scanner_plugin
class CustomRegexScanner(ScannerPluginBase[CustomRegexScannerConfig]):
    """Scanner that uses regex patterns to find security issues."""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = CustomRegexScannerConfig()
        return super().model_post_init(context)

    def validate_plugin_dependencies(self) -> bool:
        return True

    def _execute_scan(self, target, target_type, global_ignore_paths):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"{self.__class__.__name__} overrides scan() directly."
        )

    def scan(
        self,
        target,
        target_type,
        global_ignore_paths=None,
        config=None,
        *args,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        if not self._pre_scan(target=target, target_type=target_type, config=config):
            self._post_scan(target=target, target_type=target_type)
            return False

        patterns = [re.compile(p) for p in self.config.options.patterns]
        if target_type == "converted":
            root = Path(target)
            files = [p for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file()]
        else:
            root = Path(self.context.source_dir)
            files = [
                Path(name.rstrip("\n"))
                for name in scan_set(
                    source=self.context.source_dir, output=self.context.output_dir
                )
            ]

        results = []
        for path in files:
            # Never open a file by name: open_in_scanned_tree refuses a symlink, a
            # file with a second hard link and a path outside the tree.
            try:
                with open_in_scanned_tree(path, root) as handle:
                    lines = handle.read().decode("utf-8").splitlines()
            except (TreeInputRefused, OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                continue
            for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
                for pattern in patterns:
                    if pattern.search(line):
                        results.append(
                            {
                                "ruleId": "CUSTOM-REGEX",
                                "level": "error",
                                "message": {"text": f"Matched {pattern.pattern}"},
                                "locations": [
                                    {
                                        "physicalLocation": {
                                            "artifactLocation": {
                                                "uri": path.absolute().as_posix()
                                            },
                                            "region": {"startLine": number},
                                        }
                                    }
                                ],
                            }
                        )

        self._post_scan(target=target, target_type=target_type)
        return SarifReport.model_validate(
            {
                "version": "2.1.0",
                "runs": [
                    {
                        "tool": {"driver": {"name": "custom-regex", "rules": []}},
                        "results": results,
                    }
                ],
            }
        )

ASH makes a URI under the source directory relative to it. The example plugin package in the ASH repository, examples/ash_plugins_example, has a scanner written the same way, and a test runs it through a real scan.

docs.title: Reporter Plugin Development
docs.text: Reporter plugins generate reports in various formats.

docs.title: Reporter Plugin Interface
docs.text:
class ReporterPluginBase(PluginBase, Generic[T]):
    """Base class for all reporter plugins."""

    @abstractmethod
    def report(self, model: AshAggregatedResults) -> str | None:
        """Return the report, which ASH writes to reports/ash.<extension>."""

Return the report as a string and let ASH write it to reports/ash.<extension>. Set extension on the config class explicitly, as the example below does.

docs.title: Reporter Plugin Example
docs.text:
import json
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import Field

from automated_security_helper.base.options import ReporterOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.base.reporter_plugin import (
    ReporterPluginBase,
    ReporterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.models.asharp_model import AshAggregatedResults
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_reporter_plugin


class CustomJSONReporterConfigOptions(ReporterOptionsBase):
    pretty_print: bool = True


class CustomJSONReporterConfig(ReporterPluginConfigBase):
    """Configuration for CustomJSONReporter."""

    name: Literal["custom-json"] = "custom-json"
    extension: str = "custom.json"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: Annotated[CustomJSONReporterConfigOptions, Field()] = (
        CustomJSONReporterConfigOptions()
    )


@ash_reporter_plugin
class CustomJSONReporter(ReporterPluginBase[CustomJSONReporterConfig]):
    """Reporter that generates a custom JSON report."""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = CustomJSONReporterConfig()
        return super().model_post_init(context)

    def report(self, model: AshAggregatedResults) -> str:
        counts = model.metadata.summary_stats.severity_counts
        report_data = {
            "project": model.metadata.project_name,
            "generated_at": model.metadata.generated_at,
            "summary": {
                "total": model.metadata.summary_stats.total,
                "critical": counts.critical,
                "high": counts.high,
                "medium": counts.medium,
                "low": counts.low,
                "info": counts.info,
            },
            "findings": [],
        }

        if model.sarif and model.sarif.runs:
            for run in model.sarif.runs:
                for result in run.results or []:
                    report_data["findings"].append(
                        {
                            "rule_id": result.ruleId,
                            "level": getattr(result.level, "value", result.level),
                            "message": result.message.root.text
                            if result.message
                            else "No message",
                        }
                    )

        indent = 2 if self.config.options.pretty_print else None
        return json.dumps(report_data, indent=indent)

docs.title: Converter Plugin Development
docs.text: Converter plugins process files before scanning.

docs.title: Converter Plugin Interface
docs.text:
class ConverterPluginBase(PluginBase):
    """Base class for all converter plugins."""

    @abstractmethod
    def convert(self) -> List[Path]:
        """Convert this converter's inputs and return the files written."""

ASH calls convert() once per scan, with no arguments. A converter finds its inputs under self.context.source_dir, reads each one through self.open_source_file(), writes its output under self.results_dir, and returns the paths it wrote. ASH scans those files as a second, converted, target. A converter declared as convert(self, target), the signature of earlier versions, is refused with an error that says to declare convert(self).

docs.title: Converter Plugin Example
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Literal

from automated_security_helper.base.converter_plugin import (
    ConverterPluginBase,
    ConverterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_converter_plugin
from automated_security_helper.utils.get_scan_set import scan_set
from automated_security_helper.utils.scanned_tree import TreeInputRefused


class YamlTemplateConverterConfig(ConverterPluginConfigBase):
    """Configuration for YamlTemplateConverter."""

    name: Literal["yaml-template"] = "yaml-template"
    enabled: bool = True


@ash_converter_plugin
class YamlTemplateConverter(ConverterPluginBase[YamlTemplateConverterConfig]):
    """Copies ``*.yaml.tmpl`` files to ``.yaml`` files the scanners read."""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = YamlTemplateConverterConfig()
        return super().model_post_init(context)

    def convert(self) -> List[Path]:
        source_dir = Path(self.context.source_dir)
        written: List[Path] = []
        for name in scan_set(source=source_dir, output=self.context.output_dir):
            candidate = Path(name.rstrip("\n"))
            if not candidate.name.endswith(".yaml.tmpl"):
                continue
            try:
                handle = self.open_source_file(candidate)
            except TreeInputRefused as refused:
                self.record_refused_input(refused)
                continue
            with handle:
                content = handle.read()
            relative = candidate.relative_to(source_dir)
            target = (
                self.results_dir / relative.parent / candidate.name[: -len(".tmpl")]
            )
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(content)
            written.append(target)
        return written

See Converter Plugins for the full contract and a tested example.

docs.title: Event Subscriber Development
docs.text: Event subscribers react to events during the scan lifecycle.

docs.title: Event Subscriber Interface
docs.text:
# automated_security_helper/plugins/events.py (excerpt)
class AshEventType(Enum):
    SCAN_START = auto()  # as each scanner starts
    SCAN_COMPLETE = auto()  # as each scanner finishes
    CONVERT_START = auto()
    CONVERT_COMPLETE = auto()
    REPORT_START = auto()
    REPORT_COMPLETE = auto()
    ERROR = auto()
    WARNING = auto()
    INFO = auto()


# A subscriber is any callable that takes keyword arguments.
EventSubscriberFunc = Callable[..., bool]

docs.title: Event Subscriber Example
docs.text:
from automated_security_helper.plugins.events import AshEventType


def scan_complete_handler(**kwargs):
    """Handle scan completion events."""
    scanner = kwargs.get("scanner", "unknown")
    remaining = kwargs.get("remaining_count", 0)

    print(f"Scanner {scanner} completed. {remaining} scanners remaining.")

    # Return True to indicate successful handling
    return True


# In the plugin package's __init__.py: ASH registers these when it loads the package.
ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [scan_complete_handler],
}

Where the handler is defined decides which scans notify it. A handler defined in your own program, outside ASH's plugin namespace, is notified in every scan that program runs. A handler defined in a plugin package is notified only in scans whose ash_plugin_modules name that package, and only when the package defines, imports or lists it (see Using Custom Plugin Packages).

docs.title: Plugin Configuration
docs.text:
Plugins are configured through the ASH configuration file. Each plugin's options go under options:

ash_plugin_modules:
  - my_ash_plugins

# Custom scanner configuration
scanners:
  custom-regex:
    enabled: true
    options:
      patterns:
        - "password\\s*=\\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]"
        - "api_key\\s*=\\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]"

# Custom reporter configuration
reporters:
  custom-json:
    enabled: true
    options:
      pretty_print: true

# Custom converter configuration
converters:
  yaml-template:
    enabled: true

docs.title: Creating a Plugin Package
docs.text:
To distribute your plugins, create a Python package whose top-level package name ends in ash_plugins:

my-ash-plugins/
├── pyproject.toml
├── my_ash_plugins/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── scanners.py
│   ├── reporters.py
│   └── converters.py

Install it into the Python environment ASH runs in. examples/ash_plugins_example in the ASH repository is a complete package of this shape.

docs.title: Plugin Registration in Package
docs.text:
Import the plugin modules in the package's __init__.py, so that importing the package runs the decorators:

from my_ash_plugins.scanners import CustomRegexScanner
from my_ash_plugins.reporters import CustomJSONReporter
from my_ash_plugins.converters import YamlTemplateConverter

# Read by the loader to report what the package provided; the decorators do the
# registering.
ASH_SCANNERS = [CustomRegexScanner]
ASH_REPORTERS = [CustomJSONReporter]
ASH_CONVERTERS = [YamlTemplateConverter]

docs.title: Using Custom Plugin Packages
docs.text:
Configure ASH to use your custom plugin package:

# ASH configuration
ash_plugin_modules:
  - "my_ash_plugins"

Or specify via command line:

ash --ash-plugin-modules my_ash_plugins

The flag can be repeated, and it, the ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES environment variable and each ash_plugin_modules entry also take a comma-separated list, such as "my_ash_plugins, other_ash_plugins".

The package name has to be inside ASH's plugin namespace, which my_ash_plugins is because it ends in _ash_plugins; a name outside it refuses the scan with exit code 3 (see Custom Plugin Modules).

A scan that names your package uses three kinds of plugin from it: those defined in the package's own __init__.py, the classes and functions __init__.py imports into its namespace (as in the example above), and those it lists in ASH_SCANNERS, ASH_REPORTERS, ASH_CONVERTERS or ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS. A plugin defined only in a submodule, such as a class in my_ash_plugins/scanners.py that __init__.py neither imports nor lists, is not used through the package; the scan uses it only if it names that submodule (my_ash_plugins.scanners) itself. The same holds for a plugin defined in another package, for example a helper library whose classes carry @ash_scanner_plugin: from helper_lib import HelperScanner in __init__.py makes the scan use it, and import helper_lib alone does not, though the class registers either way. The scan logs how many registered plugins it leaves out ("... registered plugin(s) not used by this scan"), in the console and in ash.log in the output directory. Run it with --debug to have the console list them, in a line starting "Registered plugins not used by this scan". ash.log keeps only the count, because in a process that runs several scans, such as the MCP server, the plugins one scan leaves out are often the ones other scans named.

Plugin classes are registered by module and class name, so your class may share its name with a class in another plugin package or with one of ASH's built-in plugins. Each one registers, neither replaces the other, and each takes part in the scans that select it.

A process that runs several scans, such as the MCP server or a program calling run_ash_scan more than once, keeps every plugin module any of them imported registered, but each scan still uses only the modules it names. A module the operator named for one scan, for example in one MCP session's profile, takes no part in a later scan that does not name it. If your own program registers plugin classes itself instead of shipping them in a package, define them in a module inside the plugin namespace and name that module in each scan's ash_plugin_modules: a class registered from a module the scan does not name is not used by that scan.

ash plugin list --ash-plugin-modules my_ash_plugins shows the plugins that are registered once the modules are imported, which is the set a scan selects from: a decorated class appears whether or not the package lists it in ASH_SCANNERS, and a listed class that no decorator registered does not.

docs.title: Plugin Design
docs.text:
• Single Responsibility: Each plugin should do one thing well
  • Configurability: Make plugins configurable for different use cases
  • Error Handling: Handle errors gracefully and provide useful error messages
  • Performance: Optimize for performance, especially for large codebases
  • Documentation: Document your plugins thoroughly

docs.title: Logging from threads your plugin starts
docs.text:
Each scan logs to its own ash.log. ASH knows which scan a line belongs to from the context the line is logged in, and ASH's own scanner threads carry that context. A thread your plugin starts with threading.Thread, or a task it submits to a ThreadPoolExecutor, starts in an empty context, so its lines belong to no scan. A CLI scan's ash.log still takes them, because that scan is the process's only one. The MCP server runs several sessions' scans in one process, so it puts such lines in no scan's ash.log, only in the server's own log (stderr, at the level the server was started with — its own log-level option, INFO when not given; quiet and simple name no logging level, so with either it is ASH_LOG_LEVEL, or WARNING when that is unset — when the server has no handler of its own on that logger). So start every thread your plugin makes with ash_thread: when the MCP server runs your plugin, a line from a thread without the scan's context never reaches the scan's ash.log.

Under ash scan, a line no handler takes reaches stderr at the scan's console level: its flags first, then ASH_DEBUG or ASH_VERBOSE, then INFO, and ERROR for --quiet and --simple unless --verbose or --debug is also given. --log-level INFO reads as the default, so it does not override ASH_DEBUG or ASH_VERBOSE; every other --log-level does. ASH_LOG_LEVEL does not change it there; under the MCP server it is the fallback for quiet and simple.

Start the thread with ash_thread, which runs the target in a copy of the scan's context, and submit to an executor through a copy the same way:

import contextvars
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from automated_security_helper.utils.log import ASH_LOGGER
from automated_security_helper.utils.threads import ash_thread


def check_one(path):
    ASH_LOGGER.info("checked %s", path)


worker = ash_thread(check_one, args=("app.py",), name="my-plugin-worker")
worker.start()
worker.join()

with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as pool:
    pool.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, check_one, "lib.py").result()

ash_thread takes the copy when it makes the thread, so make it in your scanner's own code (inside scan()), not at import time. It returns the thread unstarted, as threading.Thread does.

docs.title: Testing Plugins
docs.text:
Create tests for your plugins. Construct a plugin with a PluginContext and call the method ASH calls:

from pathlib import Path

from automated_security_helper.base.plugin_context import PluginContext
from automated_security_helper.config.ash_config import AshConfig
from my_ash_plugins.scanners import CustomRegexScanner


def test_custom_regex_scanner(tmp_path):
    source = tmp_path / "src"
    source.mkdir()
    (source / "test.py").write_text('password = "secret123"\n', encoding="utf-8")
    context = PluginContext(
        source_dir=source,
        output_dir=tmp_path / "out",
        config=AshConfig(project_name="scanner-test"),
    )

    scanner = CustomRegexScanner(context=context)
    report = scanner.scan(target=source, target_type="source")

    (result,) = report.runs[0].results
    location = result.locations[0].physicalLocation.root
    assert Path(location.artifactLocation.uri).name == "test.py"
    assert location.region.startLine == 1

docs.title: Event Subscribers
docs.text:
ASH provides a comprehensive event system that allows plugins to react to various events during the scanning process. This enables you to create custom logging, notifications, integrations, and other reactive behaviors.

For detailed visual diagrams of the event system architecture and workflow, see Event Subscriber Diagrams.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The event system uses a discovery-based pattern similar to how ASH discovers scanners, converters, and reporters. Event subscribers are registered using the ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS dictionary in your plugin module.

docs.title: Basic Event Subscriber
docs.text:
Here's a simple example of creating an event subscriber:

# my_ash_plugins/__init__.py
from automated_security_helper.plugins.events import AshEventType


def handle_scan_complete(**kwargs):
    """Handle scan complete event"""
    scanner = kwargs.get("scanner", "Unknown")
    remaining_count = kwargs.get("remaining_count", 0)

    print(f"Scanner '{scanner}' completed!")
    if remaining_count > 0:
        print(f"{remaining_count} scanners still running")
    else:
        print("All scanners completed!")

    return True


# Event callback registry
ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [handle_scan_complete],
}

docs.title: Available Event Types
docs.text: ASH provides the following event types:

docs.title: Phase Events
docs.text:
• AshEventType.CONVERT_START: Fired when the convert phase begins
  • AshEventType.CONVERT_COMPLETE: Fired when the convert phase completes
  • AshEventType.SCAN_START: Fired when the scan phase begins
  • AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: Fired when each individual scanner completes
  • AshEventType.REPORT_START: Fired when the report phase begins
  • AshEventType.REPORT_COMPLETE: Fired when the report phase completes

docs.title: General Events
docs.text:
• AshEventType.ERROR: Fired when errors occur
  • AshEventType.WARNING: Fired for warning conditions
  • AshEventType.INFO: Fired for informational events

docs.title: Event Data
docs.text: Each event type provides specific data through keyword arguments:

docs.title: SCAN_COMPLETE Event Data
docs.text:
The SCAN_COMPLETE event is fired each time an individual scanner finishes and provides:

  • scanner: Name of the completed scanner
  • completed_count: Number of scanners completed so far
  • total_count: Total number of scanners
  • remaining_count: Number of scanners still running
  • remaining_scanners: List of remaining scanner names
  • message: Human-readable summary message
  • phase: The phase name ("scan")
  • plugin_context: The current plugin context

docs.title: Common Event Data
docs.text:
All events include:

  • phase: The name of the current phase
  • plugin_context: The current plugin context with source/output directories and configuration

docs.title: Multiple Event Subscribers
docs.text:
You can register multiple subscribers for the same event:

def log_scan_completion(**kwargs):
    """Log scan completion to file"""
    scanner = kwargs.get("scanner")
    with open("/tmp/scan.log", "a") as f:
        f.write(f"Scanner {scanner} completed at {datetime.now()}\n")
    return True


def notify_scan_completion(**kwargs):
    """Send notification about scan completion"""
    scanner = kwargs.get("scanner")
    remaining = kwargs.get("remaining_count", 0)
    # Send notification logic here
    return True


ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [
        log_scan_completion,
        notify_scan_completion,
    ],
}

docs.title: Multiple Event Types
docs.text:
You can subscribe to multiple event types:

def handle_phase_start(**kwargs):
    """Handle any phase start"""
    phase = kwargs.get("phase", "Unknown")
    print(f"Phase '{phase}' started")
    return True


def handle_phase_complete(**kwargs):
    """Handle any phase completion"""
    phase = kwargs.get("phase", "Unknown")
    print(f"Phase '{phase}' completed")
    return True


ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_START: [handle_phase_start],
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [handle_scan_completion],
    AshEventType.CONVERT_START: [handle_phase_start],
    AshEventType.CONVERT_COMPLETE: [handle_phase_complete],
    AshEventType.REPORT_START: [handle_phase_start],
    AshEventType.REPORT_COMPLETE: [handle_phase_complete],
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Event subscribers should handle errors gracefully to avoid disrupting the scan process:

def robust_event_handler(**kwargs):
    """Event handler with proper error handling"""
    try:
        scanner = kwargs.get("scanner", "Unknown")
        # Your event handling logic here
        print(f"Processing completion of {scanner}")
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        # Log the error but don't re-raise to avoid disrupting the scan
        print(f"Error in event handler: {e}")
        return False

docs.title: Slack Notifications
docs.text:
import requests


def notify_slack_on_completion(**kwargs):
    """Send Slack notification when all scanners complete"""
    remaining_count = kwargs.get("remaining_count", 0)

    if remaining_count == 0:  # All scanners completed
        webhook_url = os.environ.get("SLACK_WEBHOOK", None)
        if webhook_url is None:
            ASH_LOGGER.error("SLACK_WEBHOOK variable is unset! Unable to send webhook.")
            return False
        message = {
            "text": "🎉 ASH security scan completed successfully!",
            "channel": "#security-alerts",
        }
        try:
            requests.post(webhook_url, json=message)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to send Slack notification: {e}")

    return True


ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.EXECUTION_COMPLETE: [notify_slack_on_completion],
}

docs.title: Custom Metrics Collection
docs.text:
import time

# Global state for tracking metrics
scan_metrics = {}


def track_scan_metrics(**kwargs):
    """Track scan performance metrics"""
    scanner = kwargs.get("scanner")
    completed_count = kwargs.get("completed_count", 0)
    total_count = kwargs.get("total_count", 0)

    # Record completion time
    scan_metrics[scanner]["completed_at"] = time.time()

    # Calculate progress
    progress = (completed_count / total_count) * 100 if total_count > 0 else 0
    print(f"Scan progress: {progress:.1f}% ({completed_count}/{total_count})")

    return True


ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [track_scan_metrics],
}

docs.title: Integration with External Systems
docs.text:
import json
import requests
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def send_to_monitoring_system(**kwargs):
    """Send scan completion data to external monitoring system"""
    try:
        scanner = kwargs.get("scanner")
        completed_count = kwargs.get("completed_count", 0)
        total_count = kwargs.get("total_count", 0)
        remaining_count = kwargs.get("remaining_count", 0)

        # Prepare monitoring data
        monitoring_data = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "event_type": "scanner_completed",
            "scanner_name": scanner,
            "progress": {
                "completed": completed_count,
                "total": total_count,
                "remaining": remaining_count,
                "percentage": (completed_count / total_count * 100)
                if total_count > 0
                else 0,
            },
        }

        # Send to monitoring endpoint
        response = requests.post(
            "https://monitoring.example.com/api/events",
            json=monitoring_data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            timeout=5,
        )

        if response.status_code == 200:
            print(f"Successfully sent monitoring data for {scanner}")
        else:
            print(f"Failed to send monitoring data: {response.status_code}")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error sending monitoring data: {e}")

    return True


ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [send_to_monitoring_system],
}

docs.title: Database Logging
docs.text:
import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime


def log_to_database(**kwargs):
    """Log scan events to SQLite database"""
    try:
        scanner = kwargs.get("scanner")
        completed_count = kwargs.get("completed_count", 0)
        total_count = kwargs.get("total_count", 0)
        phase = kwargs.get("phase", "unknown")

        # Connect to database
        conn = sqlite3.connect("/tmp/ash_scan_log.db")
        cursor = conn.cursor()

        # Create table if it doesn't exist
        cursor.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scan_events (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                timestamp TEXT,
                phase TEXT,
                scanner TEXT,
                completed_count INTEGER,
                total_count INTEGER,
                progress_percentage REAL
            )
        """)

        # Insert event data
        progress = (completed_count / total_count * 100) if total_count > 0 else 0
        cursor.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO scan_events
            (timestamp, phase, scanner, completed_count, total_count, progress_percentage)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
        """,
            (
                datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                phase,
                scanner,
                completed_count,
                total_count,
                progress,
            ),
        )

        conn.commit()
        conn.close()

        print(f"Logged scan event for {scanner} to database")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error logging to database: {e}")

    return True


ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [log_to_database],
}

docs.title: Plugin Discovery
docs.text:
ASH automatically discovers event subscribers by:

  1. Loading modules specified in the internal_modules list (for built-in plugins)
  2. Loading additional modules specified in configuration via ash_plugin_modules
  3. Scanning for ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS constants in loaded modules
  4. Registering discovered event subscribers with the plugin manager

The event subscribers are called in the order they appear in the callback list for each event type.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Return Values: Always return True for successful handling or False for errors
  2. Error Handling: Use try-catch blocks to prevent event handler errors from disrupting scans
  3. Performance: Keep event handlers lightweight to avoid slowing down the scan process
  4. Logging: Use appropriate log levels and avoid excessive output
  5. State Management: Be careful with global state in multi-threaded environments
  6. Resource Cleanup: Clean up any resources (files, connections) in your event handlers
  7. Timeouts: Use timeouts for external API calls to prevent hanging
  8. Graceful Degradation: Design handlers to fail gracefully without affecting the main scan process

docs.title: Conditional Event Handling
docs.text:
def conditional_handler(**kwargs):
    """Only handle events under certain conditions"""
    scanner = kwargs.get("scanner")
    remaining_count = kwargs.get("remaining_count", 0)

    # Only notify for critical scanners or when all complete
    critical_scanners = ["bandit", "semgrep", "checkov"]

    if scanner in critical_scanners or remaining_count == 0:
        print(f"Important: {scanner} completed!")
        # Send notification logic here

    return True

docs.title: Event Filtering
docs.text:
def filtered_handler(**kwargs):
    """Filter events based on context"""
    plugin_context = kwargs.get("plugin_context")

    # Only handle events for certain source directories
    if plugin_context and "production" in str(plugin_context.source_dir):
        scanner = kwargs.get("scanner")
        print(f"Production scan: {scanner} completed")
        # Handle production-specific logic

    return True

docs.title: Stateful Event Handling
docs.text:
class ScanProgressTracker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.start_time = None
        self.completed_scanners = []

    def handle_scan_start(self, **kwargs):
        """Track scan start time"""
        self.start_time = time.time()
        self.completed_scanners = []
        print("Scan progress tracking started")
        return True

    def handle_scan_complete(self, **kwargs):
        """Track individual scanner completion"""
        scanner = kwargs.get("scanner")
        remaining_count = kwargs.get("remaining_count", 0)

        self.completed_scanners.append(scanner)

        if self.start_time:
            elapsed = time.time() - self.start_time
            print(f"Scanner {scanner} completed after {elapsed:.1f}s")

        if remaining_count == 0:
            total_time = time.time() - self.start_time if self.start_time else 0
            print(f"All scanners completed in {total_time:.1f}s")
            print(f"Completion order: {', '.join(self.completed_scanners)}")

        return True


# Create tracker instance
tracker = ScanProgressTracker()

ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_START: [tracker.handle_scan_start],
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [tracker.handle_scan_complete],
}

docs.title: Integration with Built-in Events
docs.text:
ASH includes built-in event subscribers for core functionality like scan completion logging. Your custom event subscribers will run alongside these built-in handlers, allowing you to extend ASH's behavior without replacing core functionality.

The built-in scan completion logger provides enhanced logging that shows remaining scanners:

INFO: Completed scanner: bandit
INFO: Remaining scanners (2): semgrep, checkov

Your custom event subscribers will receive the same event data and can provide additional functionality like notifications, metrics collection, or integration with external systems.

docs.title: Plugin Best Practices
docs.text: This guide provides best practices for developing ASH plugins.

docs.title: General Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Follow the Plugin Interface: Implement all required methods for your plugin type
  2. Use Pydantic Models: For configuration and data validation
  3. Handle Errors Gracefully: Use try/except blocks and provide meaningful error messages
  4. Document Your Plugin: Add docstrings and comments to explain your plugin's functionality
  5. Test Thoroughly: Create unit tests for your plugins
  6. Version Your Plugins: Use semantic versioning for your plugins
  7. Respect the Plugin Context: Use the provided directories for outputs
  8. Clean Up After Yourself: Remove temporary files when done

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Generate SARIF Reports: SARIF is the standard format for security findings
  2. Handle Ignore Paths: Skip the files under the global_ignore_paths passed to scan, which is empty under --ignore-suppressions
  3. Use Subprocess Utilities: Use the provided _run_subprocess method for running external commands
  4. Add Metadata: Add useful metadata to the results container
  5. Support Both File and Directory Scanning: Handle both individual files and directories

docs.title: Reporter Plugin Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Validate Dependencies: Implement the validate method to check dependencies
  2. Output to Files: Write reports to the reports directory
  3. Return Content: Return the report content as a string
  4. Use Model Methods: Use the model's helper methods like to_simple_dict() and to_flat_vulnerabilities()
  5. Handle Large Reports: Be mindful of memory usage when generating large reports

docs.title: Converter Plugin Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Preserve Line Numbers: Try to preserve line numbers for better mapping of findings back to original files
  2. Handle Directories: Support converting both individual files and directories
  3. Return Paths: Return the path to the converted file or directory
  4. Skip Unsupported Files: Only convert files with supported extensions
  5. Maintain File Structure: Preserve the directory structure when converting directories

docs.title: Plugin Dependencies
docs.text:
You can specify dependencies for your plugins:

from automated_security_helper.base.plugin_dependency import (
    PluginDependency,
    CustomCommand,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_scanner_plugin

docs.title: Plugin Event Subscribers
docs.text:
ASH supports event subscribers for reacting to events during the scan process. Event subscribers are registered using the ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS dictionary pattern:

# my_ash_plugins/__init__.py
from automated_security_helper.plugins.events import AshEventType


def handle_scan_complete(**kwargs):
    """Handle scan complete event"""
    scanner = kwargs.get("scanner", "Unknown")
    remaining_count = kwargs.get("remaining_count", 0)
    remaining_scanners = kwargs.get("remaining_scanners", [])

    print(f"Scanner '{scanner}' completed!")
    if remaining_count > 0:
        print(f"{remaining_count} scanners remaining: {', '.join(remaining_scanners)}")
    else:
        print("All scanners completed!")

    return True


def handle_report_complete(**kwargs):
    """Handle report complete event"""
    phase = kwargs.get("phase", "Unknown")
    print(f"Report phase '{phase}' completed!")
    return True


# Event callback registry following the same pattern as ASH_SCANNERS, ASH_REPORTERS, etc.
ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {
    AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [handle_scan_complete],
    AshEventType.REPORT_COMPLETE: [handle_report_complete],
}

docs.title: Available Event Types
docs.text:
• AshEventType.SCAN_START: Fired when the scan phase begins
  • AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: Fired when each individual scanner completes
  • AshEventType.CONVERT_START: Fired when the convert phase begins
  • AshEventType.CONVERT_COMPLETE: Fired when the convert phase completes
  • AshEventType.REPORT_START: Fired when the report phase begins
  • AshEventType.REPORT_COMPLETE: Fired when the report phase completes
  • AshEventType.ERROR: Fired when errors occur
  • AshEventType.WARNING: Fired for warning conditions
  • AshEventType.INFO: Fired for informational events

docs.title: Event Data
docs.text:
Event subscribers receive keyword arguments with relevant data. For example, SCAN_COMPLETE events include:

  • scanner: Name of the completed scanner
  • completed_count: Number of scanners completed so far
  • total_count: Total number of scanners
  • remaining_count: Number of scanners still running
  • remaining_scanners: List of remaining scanner names
  • message: Human-readable summary message
  • phase: The phase name ("scan")
  • plugin_context: The current plugin context

docs.title: Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
1. Not Handling Errors: Always catch and handle exceptions to prevent the entire scan from failing
  2. Ignoring Configuration: Always respect the plugin configuration options
  3. Hard-coding Paths: Use the paths provided in the plugin context
  4. Not Validating Dependencies: Always check that required dependencies are available
  5. Returning Incorrect Types: Make sure to return the expected types from plugin methods

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
1. Validate User Input: Never trust user input without validation
  2. Avoid Shell Injection: Use lists for subprocess commands instead of strings
  3. Handle Secrets Securely: Never log or expose sensitive information
  4. Limit Resource Usage: Be mindful of memory and CPU usage
  5. Clean Up Temporary Files: Always clean up temporary files after use

docs.title: Reporter Plugin Example
docs.text:
Here's a complete example of a custom reporter plugin based on the S3Reporter in your codebase:

import json
import logging
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, Literal, Optional, TYPE_CHECKING

import boto3
from pydantic import Field

from automated_security_helper.base.options import ReporterOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.base.reporter_plugin import (
    ReporterPluginBase,
    ReporterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_reporter_plugin
from automated_security_helper.utils.log import ASH_LOGGER

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from automated_security_helper.models.asharp_model import AshAggregatedResults


class S3ReporterConfigOptions(ReporterOptionsBase):
    aws_region: Annotated[
        str | None,
        Field(
            pattern=r"(af|il|ap|ca|eu|me|sa|us|cn|us-gov|us-iso|us-isob)-(central|north|(north(?:east|west))|south|south(?:east|west)|east|west)-\d{1}"
        ),
    ] = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION", os.environ.get("AWS_DEFAULT_REGION", None))
    aws_profile: Optional[str] = os.environ.get("AWS_PROFILE", None)
    bucket_name: str | None = os.environ.get("ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME", None)
    key_prefix: str = "ash-reports/"
    file_format: Literal["json", "yaml"] = "json"


class S3ReporterConfig(ReporterPluginConfigBase):
    name: Literal["s3"] = "s3"
    extension: str = "s3.json"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: S3ReporterConfigOptions = S3ReporterConfigOptions()


@ash_reporter_plugin
class S3Reporter(ReporterPluginBase[S3ReporterConfig]):
    """Formats results and uploads to an S3 bucket."""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = S3ReporterConfig()
        return super().model_post_init(context)

    def validate_plugin_dependencies(self) -> bool:
        """Validate reporter configuration and requirements."""
        self.dependencies_satisfied = False
        if (
            self.config.options.aws_region is None
            or self.config.options.bucket_name is None
        ):
            return self.dependencies_satisfied
        try:
            session = boto3.Session(
                profile_name=self.config.options.aws_profile,
                region_name=self.config.options.aws_region,
            )
            sts_client = session.client("sts")
            caller_id = sts_client.get_caller_identity()

            # Check if S3 bucket exists and is accessible
            s3_client = session.client("s3")
            s3_client.head_bucket(Bucket=self.config.options.bucket_name)

            self.dependencies_satisfied = "Account" in caller_id
        except Exception as e:
            self._plugin_log(
                f"Error when validating S3 access: {e}",
                level=logging.WARNING,
                target_type="source",
                append_to_stream="stderr",
            )
        return self.dependencies_satisfied

    def report(self, model: "AshAggregatedResults") -> str | None:
        """Upload the results to S3 and return the URL, or None on failure."""
        if isinstance(self.config, dict):
            self.config = S3ReporterConfig.model_validate(self.config)

        # Create a key for the S3 object from the time the results were generated
        timestamp = model.metadata.generated_at or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(
            timespec="seconds"
        )
        file_extension = "json" if self.config.options.file_format == "json" else "yaml"
        s3_key = (
            f"{self.config.options.key_prefix}ash-report-{timestamp}.{file_extension}"
        )

        # Format the results based on the specified format
        if self.config.options.file_format == "json":
            output_dict = model.to_simple_dict()
            output_content = json.dumps(output_dict, default=str, indent=2)
        else:
            import yaml

            output_dict = model.to_simple_dict()
            output_content = yaml.dump(output_dict, default_flow_style=False)

        # Create a session with the specified profile and region
        session = boto3.Session(
            profile_name=self.config.options.aws_profile,
            region_name=self.config.options.aws_region,
        )
        s3_client = session.client("s3")

        try:
            # Upload the content to S3
            s3_client.put_object(
                Bucket=self.config.options.bucket_name,
                Key=s3_key,
                Body=output_content,
                ContentType="application/json"
                if file_extension == "json"
                else "application/yaml",
            )

            s3_url = f"s3://{self.config.options.bucket_name}/{s3_key}"
            ASH_LOGGER.info(f"Successfully uploaded report to {s3_url}")

            # Also write to local file if needed
            output_path = (
                Path(self.context.output_dir)
                / "reports"
                / f"s3-report.{file_extension}"
            )
            output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

            with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(output_content)

            return s3_url
        except Exception as e:
            error_msg = f"Error uploading to S3: {str(e)}"
            self._plugin_log(
                error_msg,
                level=logging.ERROR,
                append_to_stream="stderr",
            )
            # None, not the message: ASH treats a None result as a reporter that
            # produced nothing and writes no report file for it. A returned
            # message would be written into that file as if it were the report.
            return None

docs.title: Simple Reporter Plugin Example
docs.text:
Here's a simpler example of a custom reporter plugin:

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import Field

from automated_security_helper.base.options import ReporterOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.base.reporter_plugin import (
    ReporterPluginBase,
    ReporterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_reporter_plugin


class SimpleReporterConfigOptions(ReporterOptionsBase):
    include_details: bool = Field(default=True, description="Include detailed findings")
    max_findings: int = Field(
        default=100, description="Maximum number of findings to include"
    )
    output_file: str = Field(
        default="simple-report.txt", description="Output file name"
    )


class SimpleReporterConfig(ReporterPluginConfigBase):
    name: Literal["simple"] = "simple"
    extension: str = "simple.txt"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: SimpleReporterConfigOptions = SimpleReporterConfigOptions()


@ash_reporter_plugin
class SimpleReporter(ReporterPluginBase[SimpleReporterConfig]):
    """Generates a simple text report."""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = SimpleReporterConfig()
        return super().model_post_init(context)

    def report(self, model):
        """Generate a simple text report."""
        # Create the report content
        content = []
        content.append("# Security Scan Report")
        content.append("")
        stats = model.metadata.summary_stats
        content.append(f"Project: {model.metadata.project_name}")
        content.append(f"Scan Time: {model.metadata.generated_at}")
        content.append("")
        content.append("## Summary")
        content.append("")
        content.append(f"Total Findings: {stats.total}")
        content.append(f"Critical: {stats.severity_counts.critical}")
        content.append(f"High: {stats.severity_counts.high}")
        content.append(f"Medium: {stats.severity_counts.medium}")
        content.append(f"Low: {stats.severity_counts.low}")
        content.append(f"Info: {stats.severity_counts.info}")
        content.append("")

        # Add detailed findings if configured
        if self.config.options.include_details:
            content.append("## Detailed Findings")
            content.append("")

            # Get flat vulnerabilities
            vulnerabilities = model.to_flat_vulnerabilities()

            # Limit the number of findings
            max_findings = min(len(vulnerabilities), self.config.options.max_findings)

            for i, vuln in enumerate(vulnerabilities[:max_findings]):
                content.append(f"### Finding {i + 1}")
                content.append(f"Title: {vuln.title}")
                content.append(f"Severity: {vuln.severity}")
                content.append(f"File: {vuln.file_path}")
                content.append(f"Line: {vuln.line_start}")
                content.append(f"Description: {vuln.description}")
                content.append("")

        # Write the report to a file
        report_text = "\n".join(content)
        output_path = (
            Path(self.context.output_dir) / "reports" / self.config.options.output_file
        )
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(report_text)

        return report_text

docs.title: Reporter Plugin Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Handle Configuration: Use Pydantic models for configuration
  2. Validate Dependencies: Implement the validate_plugin_dependencies method to check dependencies
  3. Error Handling: Use try/except blocks and provide meaningful error messages
  4. Output to Files: Write reports to the reports directory. Return the report and ASH writes it to ash.<extension>; write any other file there with write_report_file and return its name from companion_file_names(), so that a link already at that name stops the run before any reporter writes
  5. Return Content: Return the report content as a string, or None when the report could not be produced (ASH then writes no file for it)
  6. Use Model Methods: Use the model's helper methods like to_simple_dict() and to_flat_vulnerabilities()

docs.title: Reporter Plugin Configuration in ASH
docs.text:
Configure your reporter in the ASH configuration file:

# ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project)
reporters:
  simple:
    enabled: true
    options:
      include_details: true
      max_findings: 50
      output_file: custom-report.txt

docs.title: Declaring destination options
docs.text:
A reporter that sends findings somewhere, or writes them to a path its options name, declares those options in destination_options:

from typing import ClassVar, Tuple


@ash_reporter_plugin
class WebhookReporter(ReporterPluginBase[WebhookReporterConfig]):
    destination_options: ClassVar[Tuple[str, ...]] = ("webhook_url", "api_token")

List every option that chooses where findings are sent or written, or which credentials send them: an endpoint, a region, an account, a bucket, a profile, a token, an output path. Name each as its field in the options model. An alias of the field is covered as well. The default is ().

When the config was built from a file inside the scanned tree (a discovered .ash/.ash.yaml, a --config inside the tree, an extends base, or ASH_CONFIG), or from a file an MCP client delivered, ASH takes these options from the trusted base instead: the defaults, an operator config outside the tree, and --config-overrides. A value such a file set is replaced, under any spelling of the reporter's section that ASH reads as this reporter's, and one warning names each option it ignored. The reporter's other options still apply from the file. ASH does this once it has imported your plugin module and before it builds any reporter, in a scan and in ash report. The built-in AWS reporters declare theirs the same way; see Settings a repository's config cannot choose.

A reporter that declares any destination option sends findings somewhere, so whether it runs is the operator's choice too, in both directions. Its enabled comes from the trusted base, or from the default of your config model's enabled when the trusted base sets none: such a file's enabled: true or enabled: false is replaced with a warning where it differs, and leaving the section out leaves the reporter as the trusted base has it. A reporter that declares no destination options writes only local files, and its enabled applies from the file.

Under the MCP server, a delivered file that sets a declared option is scanned with the server's value rather than refused, because the server checks the file against denied_paths before it imports your plugin module. To have such a file refused, add the option to the profile's global_settings.mcp.runtime_overrides.denied_paths, for example /reporters/webhook/options/webhook_url.

docs.title: Testing Reporter Plugins
docs.text:
Create unit tests for your reporter:

import pytest
from pathlib import Path

from automated_security_helper.base.plugin_context import PluginContext
from automated_security_helper.models.asharp_model import AshAggregatedResults
from my_ash_plugins.reporters import SimpleReporter


def test_simple_reporter():
    # Create a plugin context
    context = PluginContext(
        source_dir=Path("test_data"), output_dir=Path("test_output")
    )

    # Create reporter instance
    reporter = SimpleReporter(context=context)

    # Create a model; the project name is part of its metadata
    model = AshAggregatedResults()
    model.metadata.project_name = "test-project"

    # Generate the report
    report = reporter.report(model)

    # Assert report content
    assert "Security Scan Report" in report
    assert "test-project" in report
