docs.title: Scanner Plugins
docs.text:
Scanner plugins perform security scans on files and generate findings. They are the core of ASH's security scanning functionality.

For detailed visual diagrams of scanner plugin architecture and workflow, see Scanner Plugin Diagrams.

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Interface
docs.text:
ScannerPluginBase.scan() is a template method. It runs a fixed sequence — preamble, tool invocation, read the result file, attach the SARIF invocation, postamble — and calls into your plugin for the one part that is tool-specific. That hook is _execute_scan(), and it is abstract: every subclass must define it, even one that does not use the template.

_execute_scan() returns a three-tuple of (argv, results_file, subprocess_env). The template runs argv, then reads SARIF from results_file, so a plugin that fits this shape does not implement scan() at all:

from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Literal, Optional, Tuple

from automated_security_helper.base.scanner_plugin import (
    ScannerPluginBase,
    ScannerPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_scanner_plugin


@ash_scanner_plugin
class MyScanner(ScannerPluginBase[MyScannerConfig]):
    """My custom scanner implementation"""

    def _execute_scan(
        self,
        target: Path,
        target_type: Literal["source", "converted"],
        global_ignore_paths,
    ) -> Tuple[List[str], Path, Optional[dict]]:
        """Return the argv to run, where it writes SARIF, and any extra env."""
        results_file = self.results_dir.joinpath(target_type, "results_sarif.sarif")
        results_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        argv = [
            "my-scanner-tool",
            "--sarif",
            "--output",
            str(results_file),
            str(target),
        ]
        return argv, results_file, None

Hooks such as _process_config_options(), _resolve_arguments(), _pre_scan(), _post_scan() and _post_process_sarif() let you adjust individual steps without replacing the template.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: success_exit_codes names the exit codes your tool uses for a run that completed: 0, plus the code it uses for "completed, findings found" if it has one. The default is {0, 1}; grype, for example, declares {0, 2}, and a tool with no findings code declares {0}. When the tool exits with any other code, the template does not read the results file and raises ScannerError, so the scanner is recorded ERROR with the code and the tool's stderr. A failed tool can leave a file that holds no findings, and reading it would grade the run PASSED. With an accepted code, an empty results file and SARIF with no run are ERROR too, because they record no scan. The run check reads the report as the tool wrote it, before _post_process_sarif() or any other hook changes it. A tool that writes an empty file for a clean scan overrides _handle_empty_results() to return a report. Cite the tool's own documentation or source for each code you add: a set that is too wide records a failed tool as a clean scan, and one that is too narrow turns ordinary scans into errors.

docs.title: Overriding scan() directly
docs.text:
A scanner whose workflow does not fit the template — one that calls a Python API instead of a subprocess, for example — overrides scan() and returns a SarifReport. The executor also grades a dict that has severity_counts, a findings list, or a status that says its tool completed (passed, completed, success or ok, in any case); a CycloneDXReport (an SBOM, which has no findings); and True. A falsy result is MISSING. A dict whose status is failed, error or any other value is ERROR, and so is anything else (a list, a string, a dict with none of those keys), because it has nothing the executor can grade. Because _execute_scan() is abstract, such a plugin still has to declare it, so give it a stub that says why it is unreachable:

@ash_scanner_plugin
class ApiScanner(ScannerPluginBase[ApiScannerConfig]):
    def _execute_scan(self, target, target_type, global_ignore_paths):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"{self.__class__.__name__} overrides scan() directly."
        )

    def scan(self, target, target_type, global_ignore_paths=None, config=None): ...

Omitting the stub makes the class abstract, and it fails at instantiation rather than at scan time. examples/ash_plugins_example/my_ash_plugins/scanner.py follows this pattern.

An override that runs one tool per target applies the same exit-code rule itself, after the run and before it reads the results file:

        response = self._run_subprocess(command=argv, results_dir=results_dir)
        self._record_target_exit_code(response)
        self._refuse_rejected_exit_code(results_file)

_record_target_exit_code makes exit_code this run's code (the plugin otherwise keeps the largest code any of its runs returned), and _refuse_rejected_exit_code raises ScannerError naming the code, the accepted set and the tool's stderr when the code is not in success_exit_codes.

The executor scans the source tree and then the converted tree with one plugin instance, and records exit_code on each target's row. Start an override with self.exit_code = 0, as the template does, so a target it returns from before its tool runs (an empty tree, missing dependencies) does not report the previous target's code.

docs.title: Declaring whether a scanner is Python-only
docs.text:
--python-only (--python-based-plugins-only) runs only the scanners that need nothing but Python, and records every other scanner SKIPPED without looking for its tool. A scanner says which it is with the python_only class variable:

from typing import ClassVar


@ash_scanner_plugin
class ApiScanner(ScannerPluginBase[ApiScannerConfig]):
    # Calls a Python library in-process and starts no other program.
    python_only: ClassVar[bool | None] = True

True puts the scanner in a --python-only run. False keeps it out: use it for a scanner that runs a binary, Node.js or anything else that is not a Python package. A scanner that declares nothing (None, the default) counts as Python-only only when it runs its tool through uv (use_uv_tool = True), so an in-process scanner like the one above is left out of a --python-only run unless it declares True.

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Configuration
docs.text:
Define a configuration class for your scanner:

from pydantic import Field


class MyScannerConfig(ScannerPluginConfigBase):
    name: str = "my-scanner"
    enabled: bool = True

    class Options:
        severity_threshold: str = Field(
            default="MEDIUM", description="Minimum severity level"
        )
        include_tests: bool = Field(default=False, description="Include test files")

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Example
docs.text:
Here's a complete example of a custom scanner plugin:

import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Literal

from pydantic import Field

from automated_security_helper.base.scanner_plugin import (
    ScannerPluginBase,
    ScannerPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_scanner_plugin
from automated_security_helper.models.scan_results_container import ScanResultsContainer


class CustomScannerConfig(ScannerPluginConfigBase):
    """Configuration for CustomScanner"""

    name: str = "custom-scanner"
    enabled: bool = True

    class Options:
        tool_path: str = Field(
            default="custom-tool", description="Path to the scanning tool"
        )
        severity_threshold: str = Field(
            default="MEDIUM", description="Minimum severity level"
        )


@ash_scanner_plugin
class CustomScanner(ScannerPluginBase):
    """Custom scanner implementation"""

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        """Initialize the scanner with configuration"""
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = CustomScannerConfig()

        self.command = "custom-tool"
        # Enable UV tool execution if your tool should be managed via UV
        # self.use_uv_tool = True
        self.tool_type = "SAST"  # or "IAC", "SCA", "SECRETS", etc.

        super().model_post_init(context)

    def scan(
        self,
        target: Path,
        target_type: Literal["source", "converted"],
        global_ignore_paths: List = None,
        config=None,
    ):
        """Scan the target using a custom tool"""
        if config is None:
            config = self.config

        # Create results container
        container = ScanResultsContainer()

        try:
            # Run the external tool
            cmd = [
                config.options.tool_path,
                "--scan",
                str(target),
                "--severity",
                config.options.severity_threshold,
            ]

            result = self._run_subprocess(
                cmd, stdout_preference="return", stderr_preference="write"
            )

            # Parse the output
            if result.stdout:
                findings = json.loads(result.stdout)

                # Create SARIF report
                sarif_report = {
                    "version": "2.1.0",
                    "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oasis-tcs/sarif-spec/master/Schemata/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json",
                    "runs": [
                        {
                            "tool": {
                                "driver": {"name": config.name, "version": "1.0.0"}
                            },
                            "results": [],
                        }
                    ],
                }

                # Convert findings to SARIF format
                for finding in findings:
                    sarif_report["runs"][0]["results"].append(
                        {
                            "ruleId": finding["id"],
                            "level": finding["severity"].lower(),
                            "message": {"text": finding["message"]},
                            "locations": [
                                {
                                    "physicalLocation": {
                                        "artifactLocation": {"uri": finding["file"]},
                                        "region": {"startLine": finding["line"]},
                                    }
                                }
                            ],
                        }
                    )

                # Write SARIF report
                sarif_path = self.results_dir / f"{config.name}.sarif"
                with open(sarif_path, "w") as f:
                    json.dump(sarif_report, f, indent=2)

                container.sarif_report = sarif_report

        except Exception as e:
            container.add_error(f"Error running scanner: {str(e)}")

        return container

docs.title: UV Tool Integration
docs.text: ASH v3 supports UV tool integration for scanner plugins that use CLI tools. This provides automatic tool isolation and management without requiring users to manually install tools.

docs.title: Enabling UV Tool Integration
docs.text:
To enable UV tool integration in your scanner plugin:

@ash_scanner_plugin
class MyScanner(ScannerPluginBase):
    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = MyScannerConfig()

        self.command = "my-tool"
        self.use_uv_tool = True  # Enable UV tool execution
        self.tool_type = "SAST"

        # Get tool version via UV
        self.tool_version = self._get_uv_tool_version("my-tool")

        super().model_post_init(context)

    def validate_plugin_dependencies(self) -> bool:
        """Validate scanner dependencies"""
        # UV tool availability is automatically validated
        if not self._validate_uv_tool_availability():
            return False

        # For UV tool-based scanners, dependencies are satisfied if UV is available
        if self.use_uv_tool:
            self.dependencies_satisfied = True
            return True

        return super().validate_plugin_dependencies()

docs.title: Benefits of UV Tool Integration
docs.text:
• Automatic Tool Management: Tools are downloaded and managed automatically
  • Isolation: Tools run in isolated environments without affecting project dependencies
  • Version Control: Consistent tool versions across environments
  • Fallback Support: Automatic fallback to direct execution if UV is unavailable

docs.title: Built-in UV Tool Scanners
docs.text: The following built-in scanners use UV tool integration: - Checkov: Infrastructure-as-Code scanning - Semgrep: Static Application Security Testing

docs.title: Dependency Checks That Resolve the Tool Off PATH
docs.text: ash dependencies install verifies an installed tool with a PATH lookup. A scanner whose validate_plugin_dependencies can start the tool anyway (it runs a library in-process, or finds the tool its own way) sets resolves_tool_off_path: ClassVar[bool] = True on the class, and the installer asks the check instead of failing the tool for the PATH. The flag has no effect on a UV tool scanner: a tool run through uv tool run is judged by uv tool list, not by a PATH lookup or by this check. See the Plugin Development Guide for when the check is asked and why it must not install anything itself.

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Generate SARIF Reports: SARIF is the standard format for security findings
  2. Handle Errors Gracefully: Use try/except blocks to handle errors
  3. Respect Global Ignore Paths: Skip the files under the global_ignore_paths your scan method is passed, rather than reading global_settings.ignore_paths from the config. Under --ignore-suppressions ASH passes an empty list, so a scanner that uses the list it is given scans those files as the built-in scanners do
  4. Use Subprocess Utilities: Use the provided _run_subprocess method for running external commands. It looks the program up through the absolute PATH entries only, and gives the tool an empty standard input (subprocess.DEVNULL), so a tool that asks a question reads end-of-file instead of waiting. Pass the tool its input as a file or an argument. spawn_run in automated_security_helper.utils.subprocess_utils accepts input= for a tool that must read standard input.
  5. Add Metadata: Add useful metadata to the results container
  6. UV Tool Integration: For CLI tools that can be managed via UV, set use_uv_tool = True in your model_post_init method to enable automatic tool isolation and management

docs.title: Scanner Plugin Configuration in ASH
docs.text:
Configure your scanner in the ASH configuration file:

# ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project)
scanners:
  custom-scanner:
    enabled: true
    options:
      tool_path: /path/to/custom-tool

docs.title: Testing Scanner Plugins
docs.text:
Create unit tests for your scanner:

import pytest
from pathlib import Path

from automated_security_helper.base.plugin_context import PluginContext
from my_ash_plugins.scanners import CustomScanner


def test_custom_scanner():
    # Create a plugin context
    context = PluginContext(
        source_dir=Path("test_data"), output_dir=Path("test_output")
    )

    # Create scanner instance
    scanner = CustomScanner(context=context)

    # Run the scanner
    results = scanner.scan(Path("test_data/sample.py"), "source")

    # Assert results
    assert results is not None
    assert results.sarif_report is not None
    assert len(results.sarif_report["runs"][0]["results"]) > 0

docs.title: Loading the plugins
docs.text:
ASH loads only its built-in plugins by default. The four AWS reporters are in the automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins package, and once it is loaded each one that is enabled (see Enabling the AWS reporters) sends findings to AWS with the credentials of whoever runs ASH. So only the operator running ASH can load it, in one of these ways:

  • --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins
  • the ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES environment variable, set to the same module name
  • --config-overrides 'ash_plugin_modules+=["automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins"]'
  • ash_plugin_modules in a config file outside the scanned tree, passed with --config

A repository's own config cannot load it. An ash_plugin_modules entry that names the package, or a module inside it, in a config file inside the scanned tree (such as the repository's .ash/.ash.yaml) is ignored with a warning naming the entry. Nor can it select the reporters through another installed package that lists or imports them: a reporter defined in this package is selected only when one of the ways above loads the package, the reporter's module, or the package that lists it. Each one that is not is named in a warning.

Under the MCP server, list the package in ash_plugin_modules of a profile registered with ash mcp --profile NAME=path/to/ash.yaml; scans in a session bound to that profile with select_profile load it. A config an MCP client delivered cannot add it.

docs.title: Enabling the AWS reporters
docs.text:
All four AWS reporters are disabled by default. Each sends findings to an AWS service with the credentials of the host running ASH, so it runs only when your configuration turns it on: enabled: true in its section of a config file you pass with --config or ASH_CONFIG, or --config-overrides reporters.<name>.enabled=true.

  • An enabled AWS reporter runs in a scan that passes no --output-formats. --output-formats (-f) accepts aws-security-hub, bedrock-summary-reporter, cloudwatch-logs and s3, which ash scan --help lists apart from the other formats. With the AWS plugin module loaded and the reporter enabled, a scan that names the reporter runs it; naming it does not enable it. A scan whose --output-formats leave it out neither checks nor runs it. A reporter's dependency check (STS, Security Hub's DescribeHub, Bedrock's model list) runs only for a reporter the scan will run.
  • A section that sets a reporter's options but not enabled, as a config written when these reporters were on by default does, leaves the reporter off. A scan or ash merge that would otherwise run it logs one warning naming the reporter and the key to set; the warning names no option value and changes nothing.
  • ash report --format <name> refuses an AWS reporter that is not enabled, and exits 1 with the setting to change. For ash report that setting, and the reporter's destination options, come from --config-overrides: stored results do not record which tree was scanned, so a --config or ASH_CONFIG file may be the scanned repository's own, and its values for these reporters are ignored with a warning (ash report).
  • ash merge runs an AWS reporter only when the operator's --config-overrides enable it, whatever the shards' recorded config says, in either direction. Its --config file does not enable or aim one, for the reason ash report's does not.
  • A reporter plugin that sends findings off the host declares sends_off_host = True on its class. ASH then runs it only when its section of the config sets enabled: true, whatever its own default is.
  • A run uses only ASH's built-in reporters and those of the plugin modules it names (ash_plugin_modules), even in a process where another run loaded more.

docs.title: Settings only the operator can set
docs.text:
These reporter options choose where findings are sent or written, which credentials send them, which findings Security Hub imports and archives, what the Bedrock reporter sends to the model (which findings, how many, the text added to the prompts, which model may receive them, and which of its calls are made), and how long a reporter keeps calling its service when it is refused:

Reporter section Options aws-security-hub aws_region, aws_profile, account_id, findings_scope, archive_resolved_findings bedrock-summary-reporter aws_region, aws_profile, model_id, output_file, output_executive_file, output_technical_file, include_code_snippets, custom_prompt, exclude_scanner_types, actionable_only, max_findings_to_analyze, max_findings_per_severity, summarize_findings, batch_processing, industry_context, compliance_frameworks, custom_context, enable_fallback_models, add_section_headers, output_markdown, include_sections, exclude_sections, group_by_severity, max_retries, base_delay, max_delay cloudwatch-logs aws_region, log_group_name, log_stream_name, max_retries, base_delay, max_delay s3 aws_region, aws_profile, bucket_name, key_prefix, max_retries, base_delay, max_delay

They take effect only from the defaults (including the environment variables each reporter's page lists), --config-overrides, or a config file outside the scanned tree. A config file inside the scanned tree cannot set them: each one it sets is ignored, with one warning naming them, and the operator's value applies; one that repeats the operator's value is no change. This holds for every spelling of the section ASH reads as that reporter's, such as s3-reporter or BedrockSummary, and of the option, with - or _. Each reporter's options model also caps its retries, from every source: max_retries at most 10, max_delay at most 60 seconds, and base_delay at most max_delay. A larger value is a validation error naming the option and its limit, and the reporter is not built.

Whether each reporter runs is the operator's too, in both directions. A config file inside the scanned tree neither turns a reporter on nor turns one off: where its enabled: true or enabled: false differs from the operator's settings, or from the reporter's own default where those set none, it is ignored with a warning, and a tree config that leaves the section out, which would return the reporter to its own default, leaves it as the operator has it. To run or skip a reporter for one scan, set it with --config-overrides, such as --config-overrides reporters.s3.enabled=true or reporters.s3.enabled=false, or in a config file outside the tree. The reporters' other options still apply from the tree.

Under the MCP server the whole section of each of these reporters is a default denied_paths entry, enabled included: /reporters/s3/**, /reporters/aws-security-hub/**, /reporters/cloudwatch-logs/** and /reporters/bedrock-summary-reporter/**. So the settings the table leaves to a repository's config, such as S3's file_format or the Bedrock reporter's model parameters, are the operator's there too. A config an MCP client delivered, or a client's runtime override, that changes one is refused with error_type: config_field_denied; one that leaves them at the server's values scans. One that sets enabled: false scans too, but the server's enabled applies and a warning names the client's value. enabled of a reporter that writes only local files, such as sarif or html, is not a default entry: a client's config may turn one on or off. See Configs an MCP client delivered.

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
1. Configure AWS credentials: 

    aws configure
# or use IAM roles (recommended)

  2. Write a config file outside the scanned tree that loads the plugins and sets their destinations (see Loading the plugins and Settings only the operator can set): 

    # /etc/ash/aws-reporters.yml
ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins

reporters:
  aws-security-hub:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: "us-east-1"
      findings_scope: "my-org/my-service"

  s3:
    enabled: true
    options:
      bucket_name: "my-security-reports"
      aws_region: "us-east-1"

  3. Run a scan with that config (no --output-formats, so every enabled reporter runs): 

    ash scan --source-dir /path/to/code --config /etc/ash/aws-reporters.yml

docs.title: Enterprise Setup
docs.text:
For enterprise deployments, combine multiple AWS plugins. As above, this goes in a config file outside the scanned tree:

# Enterprise configuration
ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins
reporters:
  aws-security-hub:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: "us-east-1"
      findings_scope: "my-org/my-service"

  bedrock-summary-reporter:
    enabled: true
    options:
      model_id: "anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0"
      aws_region: "us-east-1"
      summary_style: "executive"

  cloudwatch-logs:
    enabled: true
    options:
      log_group_name: "/aws/ash/security-scans"
      aws_region: "us-east-1"

  s3-reporter:
    enabled: true
    options:
      bucket_name: "enterprise-security-reports"
      key_prefix: "ash-scans"
      aws_region: "us-east-1"

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",

    {

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
name: Security Scan with AWS Integration
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write  # For OIDC
      contents: read

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3

    - name: Configure AWS credentials
      uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
      with:
        role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActions-ASH
        aws-region: us-east-1

    - name: Run ASH Security Scan
      env:
        # Security Hub imports only from the default branch: every scan of the
        # repository updates the same findings, so a pull request or a feature
        # branch would overwrite, and with archiving on archive, what the
        # default branch reported.
        IMPORT_TO_SECURITY_HUB: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref_name == github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        # The repository's findings in Security Hub. Set here, by the job that
        # holds the credentials, and not in the repository's .ash config.
        FINDINGS_SCOPE: ${{ github.repository }}
      run: |
        # The other reporters are enabled in .ash/.ash.yaml
        if [ "$IMPORT_TO_SECURITY_HUB" = "true" ]; then
          ash --source-dir . \
            --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled=true' \
            --config-overrides "reporters.aws-security-hub.options.findings_scope=$FINDINGS_SCOPE"
        else
          # Off whatever .ash/.ash.yaml says: a pull request can change that file.
          ash --source-dir . \
            --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled=false'
        fi

    - name: Post AI Summary to PR
      if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      uses: actions/github-script@v6
      with:
        script: |
          const fs = require('fs');
          if (fs.existsSync('output/bedrock-summary.md')) {
            const summary = fs.readFileSync('output/bedrock-summary.md', 'utf8');
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: `## 🔒 Security Scan Summary\n\n${summary}`
            });
          }

docs.title: Jenkins Pipeline
docs.text:
pipeline {
    agent any
    environment {
        AWS_REGION = 'us-east-1'
        ASH_S3_BUCKET = 'jenkins-security-reports'
    }

    stages {
        // A multibranch pipeline, where `branch` matches BRANCH_NAME. Only the
        // default branch imports into Security Hub: every scan of the repository
        // updates the same findings, so another branch would overwrite them.
        // /etc/ash/aws-reporters.yml loads the AWS plugins (ash_plugin_modules:
        // [automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins]) and sets
        // the Security Hub Region.
        stage('Security Scan (imports to Security Hub)') {
            when { branch 'main' }
            steps {
                withAWS(role: 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Jenkins-ASH') {
                    // The config file is on the agent, outside the checked-out
                    // workspace, and the scope is one name for this repository.
                    sh '''
                        ash --source-dir . \
                          --config /etc/ash/aws-reporters.yml \
                          --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled=true' \
                          --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.options.findings_scope=my-org/my-service'
                    '''
                }
            }
        }

        stage('Security Scan') {
            when { not { branch 'main' } }
            steps {
                // The `when` above and the override below are what keep this
                // stage from importing; to enforce it, give branch builds a role
                // without securityhub:BatchImportFindings.
                withAWS(role: 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Jenkins-ASH') {
                    // Off whatever the checked-out configuration says.
                    sh '''
                        ash --source-dir . \
                          --config /etc/ash/aws-reporters.yml \
                          --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled=false'
                    '''
                }
            }
        }

        stage('Process Results') {
            steps {
                script {
                    // Archive results and send notifications
                    def reportUrl = "https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/buckets/${env.ASH_S3_BUCKET}"
                    currentBuild.description = "Security Report: ${reportUrl}"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: AWS Lambda Integration
docs.text:
Deploy ASH as a Lambda function for serverless scanning:

import json
import subprocess
import boto3
from pathlib import Path


def lambda_handler(event, context):
    # Download code from S3 or CodeCommit
    # Run ASH scan
    # Results automatically go to configured AWS services

    try:
        # Example: Scan code from S3 trigger
        bucket = event["Records"][0]["s3"]["bucket"]["name"]
        key = event["Records"][0]["s3"]["object"]["key"]

        # Download and extract code
        s3 = boto3.client("s3")
        s3.download_file(bucket, key, "/tmp/code.zip")

        # Extract and scan
        subprocess.run(["unzip", "/tmp/code.zip", "-d", "/tmp/code"])

        # One findings_scope per repository, so two repositories never share
        # finding Ids in Security Hub. Here the object key names the repository,
        # for example "repos/my-service.zip". Set by this function, not by the
        # scanned code's own .ash config.
        findings_scope = Path(key).stem

        # Run ASH with AWS reporters
        result = subprocess.run(
            [
                "ash",
                "scan",
                "--source-dir",
                "/tmp/code",
                # The reporters are enabled in the config file.
                "--config",
                "/opt/ash-lambda-config.yml",
                "--config-overrides",
                f"reporters.aws-security-hub.options.findings_scope={findings_scope}",
            ],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )

        return {
            "statusCode": 200,
            "body": json.dumps(
                {
                    "message": "Scan completed successfully",
                    "findings_count": result.stdout.count("finding"),
                }
            ),
        }

    except Exception as e:
        return {"statusCode": 500, "body": json.dumps({"error": str(e)})}

docs.title: Bedrock Summary Reporter
docs.text:
Generates AI-powered executive summaries and detailed security analysis using Amazon Bedrock's foundation models, providing human-readable insights from ASH scan results.

For detailed visual diagrams of the Bedrock Summary Reporter architecture and workflow, see Bedrock Summary Reporter Diagrams.

Note: This reporter has been updated to match the documentation. All features described in this document are now implemented.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Bedrock Summary Reporter leverages Amazon Bedrock to:

  • Generate executive summaries for stakeholders and management
  • Provide detailed technical analysis with remediation recommendations
  • Create risk assessments based on finding severity and context
  • Support multiple foundation models for different analysis styles
  • Customize output format for various audiences

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This reporter is disabled by default: it sends findings to AWS with the host's credentials, so it runs only when your config sets enabled: true for it (see Enabling the AWS reporters).

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
reporters:
  bedrock-summary-reporter:
    enabled: true
    options:
      model_id: "anthropic.claude-v2"
      aws_region: "us-east-1"

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
reporters:
  bedrock-summary-reporter:
    enabled: true
    options:
      model_id: "anthropic.claude-instant-v1"
      aws_region: "us-west-2"
      max_tokens: 4000
      temperature: 0.1
      top_p: 0.9
      include_code_snippets: true
      summary_style: "executive"  # executive, technical, or detailed
      custom_prompt: "Focus on business impact and compliance risks"
      # Retry and fallback configuration
      max_retries: 5      # Default: 3, at most 10
      base_delay: 2.0     # Default: 1.0 seconds, at most max_delay
      max_delay: 30.0     # Default: 60.0 seconds, at most 60
      enable_fallback_models: true

docs.title: What is sent to Bedrock
docs.text:
The reporter receives results ASH has already masked: secret values that findings expose are masked in every snippet and message before any reporter runs (see "Secret values in reports" in the output formats page). On top of that:

  • Findings from secrets scanners are counted, not sent. exclude_scanner_types (default ["SECRET"]) names scanner tool types whose findings go into the prompts only as a count ("Secret findings: N"). A finding's type is its scanner's tool type, looked up from the scanner's name (detect-secrets, ferret-scan and gitleaks are SECRETS), or a tool_type:: tag on the finding. SECRET and SECRETS both name the secrets type. With the secrets type excluded, a finding from any rule that detects a credential or key is counted too: semgrep's and opengrep's generic.secrets.* rules, checkov's CKV_SECRET_*, and rules tagged secret, secrets, CWE-798 or CWE-321. A hard-coded password check such as bandit's B105 (CWE-259) is sent, with the value masked.
  • A finding whose scanner type cannot be determined is sent without its code. Its message and location are sent, its snippets are not, and they are left out of the local summary too.
  • include_code_snippets decides whether code is sent or written. With it off (the default), no prompt holds a snippet, and the "Raw JSON" blocks in reports/ash.bedrock.summary.md are written without the result's snippets.

docs.title: Which findings are sent to Bedrock
docs.text:
With actionable_only: true (the default), the reporter sends Bedrock only findings that are not suppressed and whose severity is at or above the threshold of the scanner that reported them (scanners.<name>.options.severity_threshold, else global_settings.severity_threshold). Severity is read the way every other report reads it: issue_severity when the scanner set one, else the SARIF level (error CRITICAL, warning MEDIUM, note LOW, none INFO). With the default MEDIUM threshold, LOW and INFO findings are not sent. In a single-directory scan these are the findings the exit-code gate counts. In workspace mode they can differ: a project's verdict uses one threshold for all of its scanners (its gate_threshold, which a workspace max_severity_threshold can tighten) and can leave out scanners the workspace policy added, while this filter uses each scanner's own threshold from the project's configuration.

Set actionable_only: false to send every finding, suppressed ones included. The Finding Details section at the end of the report is written locally from the scan results, not by the model, and lists every finding either way.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
# AWS region
export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"

# Bedrock model ID
export ASH_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID="anthropic.claude-v2"

# Custom configuration
export ASH_BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS="3000"
export ASH_BEDROCK_TEMPERATURE="0.2"

docs.title: Output files
docs.text: With output_markdown on (the default), the reporter writes its summary to output_file (default ash.bedrock.summary.md), and the executive summary and technical analysis to output_executive_file and output_technical_file (defaults bedrock-executive.md and bedrock-technical.md), in the reports directory. Each must be a plain file name, from any source, --config-overrides included. A value with a /, \ or NUL in it, or one that is . or .., such as ../summary.md, is replaced by the option's default, with a warning naming the key. ASH also writes these files only when the resolved file is directly inside the reports directory.

docs.title: Where these options can be set
docs.text:
These options are the operator's:

  • aws_region, aws_profile, model_id, output_file, output_executive_file and output_technical_file choose where findings are sent or written and which credentials send them.
  • include_code_snippets, custom_prompt, industry_context, compliance_frameworks and custom_context choose what is sent to the model with them: source from the scanned tree, and text added to the prompts.
  • exclude_scanner_types (which keeps secret findings out by default), actionable_only, max_findings_to_analyze, max_findings_per_severity, summarize_findings and batch_processing choose which findings are sent, and how many.
  • enable_fallback_models chooses whether a model other than model_id may receive them.
  • add_section_headers, output_markdown, include_sections, exclude_sections and group_by_severity choose which of the reporter's calls are made, and each of those calls sends findings: the single summary call or the sectioned report, the calls behind the executive and technical files, the call for each section, and a call for each severity.
  • max_retries, base_delay and max_delay choose how long the reporter keeps calling Bedrock when it is refused. max_retries is at most 10, max_delay at most 60 seconds, and base_delay at most max_delay.

They take effect only from the defaults (AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, AWS_PROFILE and ASH_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID), --config-overrides, or a config file outside the scanned tree. A config file inside the scanned tree, or one an MCP client delivered, cannot set them: from the tree they are ignored with a warning, under either spelling of the name (exclude-scanner-types is the same option as exclude_scanner_types), and under the MCP server they are default denied_paths entries, so a delivered config that changes one is refused. A repository config that repeats the operator's value is no change, and is not warned about. The model parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), add_table_of_contents, summary_style and enable_caching still apply from the tree.

Whether the reporter runs is the operator's too: a config file inside the scanned tree neither turns it on nor turns it off (see Settings only the operator can set). Under the MCP server every setting of the section is a default denied_paths entry (/reporters/bedrock-summary-reporter/**), so a delivered config that changes one is refused. A client's enabled: false is not refused, but the server's enabled applies.

The reporter is in the ash_aws_plugins package, which only the operator can load, with --ash-plugin-modules, ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES or the operator's own config, never a repository's. See Loading the plugins.

docs.title: Executive Summary Generation
docs.text:
Generates concise summaries for leadership:

# Security Scan Executive Summary

## Overview
Your codebase scan identified **15 security findings** across 3 categories, with **2 critical issues** requiring immediate attention.

## Key Risks
- **Hardcoded credentials** in configuration files (CRITICAL)
- **SQL injection vulnerabilities** in user input handling (HIGH)
- **Insecure cryptographic practices** in data encryption (MEDIUM)

## Business Impact
- **Compliance risk**: Potential GDPR violations due to data exposure
- **Security risk**: Unauthorized access to customer data
- **Operational risk**: Potential service disruption

## Recommended Actions
1. Immediately rotate exposed credentials
2. Implement parameterized queries for database access
3. Update cryptographic libraries to current standards

docs.title: Technical Analysis
docs.text:
Provides detailed technical insights:

# Technical Security Analysis

## Critical Findings Analysis

### 1. Hardcoded API Keys (2 instances)
**Location**: `src/config/database.py:15`, `src/utils/api_client.py:23`
**Risk**: Direct exposure of authentication credentials
**Remediation**:
- Move credentials to environment variables
- Implement AWS Secrets Manager integration
- Add credential scanning to CI/CD pipeline

### 2. SQL Injection Vulnerability
**Location**: `src/models/user.py:45-52`
**Risk**: Potential database compromise
**Code Pattern**: Direct string concatenation in SQL queries
**Remediation**:

- Implement input validation

import boto3

from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart


def send_email_summary(summary_file, recipients):
    ses = boto3.client("ses")

    with open(summary_file, "r") as f:

    msg["From"] = "security@company.com"

docs.title: CloudWatch Logs Reporter
docs.text:
Streams ASH scan results to Amazon CloudWatch Logs for real-time monitoring and analysis.

For detailed visual diagrams of the CloudWatch Logs Reporter architecture and workflow, see CloudWatch Logs Reporter Diagrams.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The CloudWatch Logs Reporter publishes security scan results directly to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, enabling:

  • Real-time monitoring of security scan results
  • Integration with CloudWatch alarms for automated alerting
  • Centralized logging across multiple scan environments
  • Long-term retention with configurable log retention policies

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This reporter is disabled by default: it sends findings to AWS with the host's credentials, so it runs only when your config sets enabled: true for it (see Enabling the AWS reporters).

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
reporters:
  cloudwatch-logs:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: "us-east-1"
      log_group_name: "/aws/ash/scan-results"
      log_stream_name: "ASHScanResults"

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
The reporter supports configuration via environment variables:

# AWS region (falls back to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION)
export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"

# CloudWatch log group name
export ASH_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_NAME="/aws/ash/scan-results"

docs.title: Complete Configuration Example
docs.text:
reporters:
  cloudwatch-logs:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: "us-east-1"
      log_group_name: "/aws/ash/security-scans"
      log_stream_name: "production-scans"

docs.title: Where these options can be set
docs.text:
aws_region, log_group_name and log_stream_name choose where findings are sent, and max_retries, base_delay and max_delay how long the reporter keeps calling CloudWatch Logs when it is refused, so they are the operator's. They take effect only from the defaults (AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and ASH_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_NAME), --config-overrides, or a config file outside the scanned tree. A config file inside the scanned tree cannot set them; each one it sets is ignored with a warning. Under the MCP server every cloudwatch-logs setting is a default denied_paths entry (/reporters/cloudwatch-logs/**), so a config an MCP client delivered that changes any of them is refused; enabled: false is not refused, but the server's enabled applies. A config file inside the scanned tree neither turns the reporter on nor turns it off (see Settings only the operator can set).

The reporter is in the ash_aws_plugins package, which only the operator can load, with --ash-plugin-modules, ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES or the operator's own config, never a repository's. See Loading the plugins.

docs.title: AWS Permissions
docs.text:
The reporter requires the following IAM permissions:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "logs:CreateLogGroup",
        "logs:CreateLogStream",
        "logs:PutLogEvents",
        "logs:DescribeLogGroups",
        "logs:DescribeLogStreams"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:logs:*:*:log-group:/aws/ash/*",
        "arn:aws:logs:*:*:log-group:/aws/ash/*:*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: AWS Credentials
docs.text:
Ensure AWS credentials are configured using one of:

  • AWS CLI: aws configure
  • Environment variables: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  • IAM roles (recommended for EC2/ECS/Lambda)
  • AWS profiles: AWS_PROFILE=myprofile

docs.title: CloudWatch Log Group
docs.text:
The log group must exist before publishing logs:

# Create log group
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name "/aws/ash/scan-results"

# Set retention policy (optional)
aws logs put-retention-policy \
  --log-group-name "/aws/ash/scan-results" \
  --retention-in-days 30

docs.title: Structured Logging
docs.text:
Results are published as structured JSON logs:

{
  "timestamp": "2024-06-11T00:00:00Z",
  "scan_id": "ash-scan-20240611-000000",
  "source": "ASH",
  "level": "INFO",
  "message": "Security scan completed",
  "results": {
    "total_findings": 15,
    "critical": 2,
    "high": 5,
    "medium": 6,
    "low": 2,
    "scanners_executed": ["bandit", "semgrep", "checkov"],
    "scan_duration": 45.2
  }
}

The event's ash_config is the configuration the results record, as the settings that were set, and null when they record none. ASH's defaults, or the file ASH_CONFIG names where ash report runs, are never put in its place.

docs.title: Automatic Log Stream Management
docs.text:
• Auto-creation: Log streams are created automatically if they don't exist
  • Timestamped entries: Each log entry includes precise timestamps
  • Batch processing: Multiple findings are efficiently batched for performance

docs.title: Integration with CloudWatch Features
docs.text:
• CloudWatch Insights: Query and analyze scan results using CloudWatch Logs Insights
  • Metric Filters: Create custom metrics from log data
  • Alarms: Set up alarms based on security findings
  • Dashboards: Visualize security trends over time

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Run scan with CloudWatch Logs reporting
ash /path/to/code --reporters cloudwatch-logs

docs.title: With Custom Configuration
docs.text:
# Set log group via environment variable
export ASH_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_NAME="/security/ash-scans"
ash /path/to/code --reporters cloudwatch-logs

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text:
# GitHub Actions example
- name: Run ASH Security Scan
  env:
    AWS_REGION: us-east-1
    ASH_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_NAME: "/ci-cd/security-scans"
  run: |
    ash . --reporters cloudwatch-logs,sarif

docs.title: Query Recent Scan Results
docs.text:
fields @timestamp, scan_id, results.total_findings, results.critical, results.high
| filter @message like /Security scan completed/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 20

docs.title: Find High-Severity Findings
docs.text:
fields @timestamp, scan_id, results.critical, results.high
| filter results.critical > 0 or results.high > 0
| sort @timestamp desc

docs.title: Analyze Scanner Performance
docs.text:
fields @timestamp, scan_id, results.scan_duration, results.scanners_executed
| stats avg(results.scan_duration) by bin(5m)

docs.title: CloudWatch Alarms
docs.text:
Create alarms for critical security findings:

aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm \
  --alarm-name "ASH-Critical-Findings" \
  --alarm-description "Alert on critical security findings" \
  --metric-name "CriticalFindings" \
  --namespace "ASH/Security" \
  --statistic "Sum" \
  --period 300 \
  --threshold 1 \
  --comparison-operator "GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold"

docs.title: Metric Filters
docs.text:
Extract metrics from log data:

aws logs put-metric-filter \
  --log-group-name "/aws/ash/scan-results" \
  --filter-name "CriticalFindings" \
  --filter-pattern '[timestamp, scan_id, source, level, message, results.critical > 0]' \
  --metric-transformations \
    metricName=CriticalFindings,metricNamespace=ASH/Security,metricValue=1

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix "/aws/ash"

Log Group Not Found

docs.title: Retry Configuration
docs.text:
The operator configures retry behavior for API calls, with --config-overrides or a config file outside the scanned tree (see Where these options can be set). max_retries is at most 10, max_delay at most 60 seconds, and base_delay at most max_delay:

reporters:
  cloudwatch-logs:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: "us-east-1"
      log_group_name: "/aws/ash/scan-results"
      log_stream_name: "ASHScanResults"
      # Retry configuration
      max_retries: 5      # Default: 3, at most 10
      base_delay: 2.0     # Default: 1.0 seconds, at most max_delay
      max_delay: 30.0     # Default: 60.0 seconds, at most 60
``````

### Debug Mode

Enable debug logging to troubleshoot issues:

```bash
# Run with debug output
ash /path/to/code --reporters cloudwatch-logs --log-level DEBUG
