docs.title: S3 Reporter
docs.text: Uploads ASH security scan reports to Amazon S3 for centralized storage and archival.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The S3 Reporter provides:

  • Simple upload of ASH scan results to S3 buckets
  • JSON or YAML format support for report files
  • Configurable S3 key prefixes for organization
  • Retry logic for reliable uploads
  • Local backup of uploaded reports

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This reporter is disabled by default: it sends findings to AWS with the host's credentials, so it runs only when your config sets enabled: true for it (see Enabling the AWS reporters).

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
reporters:
  s3:
    enabled: true
    options:
      bucket_name: myorg-ash-reports
      aws_region: us-east-1
      file_format: json  # or yaml
      key_prefix: ash-reports/

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
reporters:
  s3:
    enabled: true
    options:
      # Use environment variables to insert the bucket name. The braces are
      # required: `!ENV ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME` resolves to the literal string
      # "ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME". With no default, `${ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME}` refuses
      # the configuration when the variable is not set; `:None` allows it.
      bucket_name: !ENV ${ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME:None}
      aws_region: !ENV ${AWS_REGION:None}
      aws_profile: !ENV ${AWS_PROFILE:None}
      file_format: json
      key_prefix: security-scans/
      # Retry configuration
      max_retries: 5      # Default: 3, at most 10
      base_delay: 2.0     # Default: 1.0 seconds, at most max_delay
      max_delay: 30.0     # Default: 60.0 seconds, at most 60

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
# Required: S3 bucket name
export ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME="my-security-reports"

# Required: AWS region
export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"

# Optional: AWS profile
export AWS_PROFILE="my-profile"

docs.title: Where these options can be set
docs.text:
aws_region, aws_profile, bucket_name and key_prefix choose where reports are uploaded and which credentials upload them, and max_retries, base_delay and max_delay how long the reporter keeps calling S3 when it is refused, so they are the operator's. They take effect only from the defaults (the environment variables above, and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION), --config-overrides, or a config file outside the scanned tree, which is where the advanced configuration above belongs. A config file inside the scanned tree, or one an MCP client delivered, cannot set them: from the tree they are ignored with a warning, and under the MCP server they are default denied_paths entries, so a delivered config that changes one is refused.

Whether the reporter runs is the operator's too: a config file inside the scanned tree neither turns it on nor turns it off, and under the MCP server the whole section, /reporters/s3/**, is a default denied_paths entry, so a delivered config or a client's runtime override that turns it on, or changes any of its settings, file_format included, is refused. A client's enabled: false is not refused, but the server's enabled applies. See Settings only the operator can set.

The reporter is in the ash_aws_plugins package, which only the operator can load, with --ash-plugin-modules, ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES or the operator's own config, never a repository's. See Loading the plugins.

docs.title: S3 Bucket Setup
docs.text:
1. Create S3 bucket: 

    aws s3 mb s3://my-security-reports --region us-east-1

  2. Configure bucket policy (optional): 

    {
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ASH-Scanner-Role"
      },
      "Action": [
        "s3:PutObject",
        "s3:PutObjectAcl"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::my-security-reports/*"
    }
  ]
}

  3. Enable versioning (recommended): 

    aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
  --bucket my-security-reports \
  --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled

docs.title: IAM Permissions
docs.text:
The reporter requires the following IAM permissions:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "s3:PutObject",
        "s3:HeadBucket"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::my-security-reports",
        "arn:aws:s3:::my-security-reports/*"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "sts:GetCallerIdentity"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: AWS Credentials
docs.text:
Ensure AWS credentials are configured using one of:

  • AWS CLI: aws configure
  • Environment variables: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  • IAM roles (recommended for EC2/ECS/Lambda)
  • AWS profiles: AWS_PROFILE=myprofile

docs.title: File Format Support
docs.text:
The S3 reporter supports two output formats:

options:
  file_format: json  # Default: JSON format
  # OR
  file_format: yaml  # YAML format

Note: Only one format can be selected per configuration. The reporter uploads the ASH aggregated results in the specified format.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Store reports in S3
export ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME="my-security-reports"
export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"
ash /path/to/code --reporters s3

docs.title: With Custom Configuration
docs.text:
# Set bucket and prefix via environment variables
export ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME="security-reports-prod"
export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"
ash /path/to/code --reporters s3,sarif

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text:
# GitHub Actions example
- name: Run Security Scan
  env:
    AWS_REGION: us-east-1
    ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME: "ci-security-reports"
    AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
    AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
  run: |
    ash . --reporters s3,sarif

- name: Generate Report URL
  run: |
    echo "Report available at: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/buckets/ci-security-reports"

docs.title: Jenkins Pipeline
docs.text:
pipeline {
    agent any
    environment {
        AWS_REGION = 'us-east-1'
        ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME = 'jenkins-security-reports'
    }
    stages {
        stage('Security Scan') {
            steps {
                sh 'ash . --reporters s3,html --'
            }
        }
        stage('Archive Results') {
            steps {
                script {
                    def reportUrl = "https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/buckets/${env.ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME}/"
                    currentBuild.description = "Security Report: ${reportUrl}"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Output Format
docs.text:
The S3 reporter uploads ASH aggregated results in the specified format (JSON or YAML). The uploaded file contains:

  • Metadata: Scan information, timestamps, and configuration
  • Findings: Security issues discovered by scanners
  • Summary statistics: Counts by severity level
  • Scanner details: Information about which scanners were run

Its ash_config is the configuration the results record, as the settings that were set. When the results record no configuration, ash_config is null. ASH's defaults, or the file ASH_CONFIG names where ash report runs, are never put in its place.

docs.title: File Naming
docs.text:
Files are uploaded with the following naming pattern: 

{key_prefix}ash-report-{timestamp}.{extension}

For example: - ash-reports/ash-report-2024-01-15T10:30:00+00:00.json - security-scans/ash-report-2024-01-15T10:30:00+00:00.yaml

{timestamp} is the scan's metadata.generated_at, so each scan gets its own object, and re-running ash report --format s3 against the same results replaces that scan's object rather than adding another. In a workspace scan the project key is inserted after the prefix: {key_prefix}{project}/ash-report-{timestamp}.{extension}.

docs.title: Local Backup
docs.text:
The reporter also creates a local copy of the uploaded report in: 

{output_dir}/reports/s3-report.{extension}

docs.title: Upload receipt
docs.text:
{output_dir}/reports/ash.s3.json records where the report went:

{
  "url": "s3://my-security-reports/ash-reports/ash-report-2024-01-15T10:30:00+00:00.json",
  "bucket": "my-security-reports",
  "key": "ash-reports/ash-report-2024-01-15T10:30:00+00:00.json",
  "file_format": "json",
  "local_copy": "/path/to/output/reports/s3-report.json"
}

local_copy is null when the local copy could not be written, for example because the reports directory is not writable. A warning is logged and the upload still counts. If a symlink or directory junction is at s3-report.json (or s3-report.yaml) when the report phase starts, the run stops with exit 1 before any reporter writes, so nothing is uploaded.

If the upload fails, no receipt is written and the reporter is logged as having produced no report.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Access Denied - Verify that the AWS credentials have the required IAM permissions - Check that the bucket exists and is in the correct region - Ensure the bucket name is correctly configured

Bucket Not Found - Verify the bucket name is correct - Check that the bucket exists in the specified AWS region - Ensure AWS credentials have access to the bucket

Upload Failures - Check network connectivity to AWS - Verify AWS credentials are valid and not expired - Review the retry configuration if uploads are timing out

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Enable debug logging to see detailed error information:

ash /path/to/code --reporters s3 --log-level DEBUG

docs.title: Retry Configuration
docs.text:
The reporter includes built-in retry logic. The operator configures it, with --config-overrides or a config file outside the scanned tree, like the options in Where these options can be set. max_retries is at most 10, max_delay at most 60 seconds, and base_delay at most max_delay; a larger value is a validation error naming the option and its limit.

reporters:
  s3:
    enabled: true
    options:
      bucket_name: "my-security-reports"
      aws_region: "us-east-1"
      # Retry configuration
      max_retries: 5      # Default: 3, at most 10
      base_delay: 2.0     # Default: 1.0 seconds, at most max_delay
      max_delay: 30.0     # Default: 60.0 seconds, at most 60

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use descriptive bucket names that reflect your organization
  2. Implement lifecycle policies to manage costs
  3. Enable versioning for important reports
  4. Set up monitoring for upload failures
  5. Use appropriate storage classes based on access patterns
  6. Implement proper access controls with IAM
  7. Enable encryption for sensitive data
  8. Monitor costs and optimize storage regularly
  9. Set up automated cleanup for old reports
  10. Use cross-region replication for critical reports

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text:
• Amazon S3 User Guide
  • S3 Storage Classes
  • S3 Lifecycle Management
  • ASH Configuration Guide
  • Other AWS Reporters

docs.title: Security Hub Reporter Diagrams
docs.text: These diagrams show what the Security Hub Reporter does during a scan in which it is enabled.

docs.title: Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant RP as ReportPhase
    participant SHR as aws-security-hub reporter
    participant STS as AWS STS
    participant SH as AWS Security Hub

    RP->>SHR: validate_plugin_dependencies()
    SHR->>SHR: Region set
    SHR->>SH: DescribeHub
    SH-->>SHR: hub ARN (Security Hub is enabled)
    opt account_id not set
        SHR->>STS: GetCallerIdentity
        STS-->>SHR: account ID
    end
    RP->>SHR: report(results)
    SHR->>SHR: enabled, config valid, not a workspace's unified results
    SHR->>SHR: Region set, findings_scope set
    SHR->>STS: GetCallerIdentity
    STS-->>SHR: caller account (must equal account_id when set)
    SHR->>SHR: one ASFF finding per SARIF result
    SHR->>SHR: drop exact duplicates (same Id)
    loop Each page of findings already stored for the scan target
        SHR->>SH: GetFindings (ProductArn, ash/target)
        SH-->>SHR: Findings, NextToken
    end
    SHR->>SHR: keep stored CreatedAt, build archive records
    loop Each batch of at most 100 findings and archive records
        SHR->>SH: BatchImportFindings
        SH-->>SHR: SuccessCount, FailedCount, FailedFindings
    end
    SHR-->>RP: receipt (written to reports/ash.aws-security-hub.asff.json)

GetFindings runs only when archive_resolved_findings is true (it is false by default).

docs.title: Finding identity
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    N[findings_scope option] --> H["sha256(json.dumps([target, key]))"]
    S[scanner, rule] --> K[key]
    F["file path, one spelling, or a converted file's path under the converted files"] --> K
    P[package name and path] --> K
    W[workspace project key] --> K
    FP{usable fingerprints?}
    FP -->|yes| FG[fingerprints or partialFingerprints] --> K
    FP -->|no: none, placeholder, or shared by two locations| L[start line, end line] --> K
    L --> O{other results with this key?}
    O -->|yes| OS["occurrence: 8 hex of sha256([column, message]); ordinal for exact duplicates"] --> K
    K --> H
    H --> I["Id = ash/<digest>"]

The scan time, the report id, the message, the severity, the column and the package version are not in the key, so a re-scan updates the same finding. The column and message only tell apart findings that share a key.

docs.title: Which stored findings are archived
docs.text:
Only with archive_resolved_findings: true.

flowchart TD
    S{one shard, changed files only, or no changed-files or scan_source marker?} -->|Yes| K0[nothing is archived]
    S -->|No| A[stored finding from GetFindings]
    A --> B{ACTIVE, Id starts with ash/?}
    B -->|No| K[left alone]
    B -->|Yes| C{produced by this scan?}
    C -->|Yes| K
    C -->|No| O{same ash/target and workspace project?}
    O -->|No| K
    O -->|Yes| D{its scanner PASSED or FAILED, and no target failed?}
    D -->|No| K
    D -->|Yes| SC{same ash/scope: recorded directory and converted tree?}
    SC -->|No| K
    SC -->|Yes| E{last updated before this scan?}
    E -->|No| K
    E -->|Yes| X[re-imported with RecordState ARCHIVED]

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[report] --> R0{enabled, config valid, not workspace results?}
    R0 -->|No| X0[SecurityHubImportError: what to fix]
    R0 -->|Yes| B{findings_scope and Region set?}
    B -->|No| X[SecurityHubImportError: what to set]
    B -->|Yes| C{Findings, or anything to archive?}
    C -->|No| R[Receipt with imported 0, no AWS call]
    C -->|Yes| AC{caller's account matches account_id?}
    AC -->|No| XA[SecurityHubImportError: use that account's credentials]
    AC -->|Yes| GF{GetFindings succeeded?}
    GF -->|No| GE[import without archiving, then SecurityHubImportError: grant GetFindings]
    GF -->|Yes| D[Send next batch]
    D --> E{Request succeeded?}
    E -->|Throttled| F[Back off and retry, up to max_retries]
    F --> E
    E -->|Failed| Y[SecurityHubImportError: cause, imported so far, not sent]
    E -->|Yes| G{Every finding in the batch rejected with InvalidAccess?}
    G -->|Yes| J
    G -->|No| I{More batches?}
    I -->|Yes| D
    I -->|No| J{Any finding rejected or not sent?}
    J -->|Yes| K[Log each rejected Id and error, then SecurityHubImportError with the counts by error code]
    J -->|No| R2[Receipt with the imported and archived findings]

A SecurityHubImportError makes the reporter fail: ReportPhase logs it and writes no receipt, and ash report exits 1.

docs.title: Security Hub Reporter
docs.text:
The aws-security-hub reporter imports ASH's findings into AWS Security Hub. It converts each finding to the AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF), sends the findings with the Security Hub BatchImportFindings API, archives the findings an earlier scan imported that this scan no longer reports, and writes a receipt to reports/ash.aws-security-hub.asff.json.

The reporter is off by default. Loading the AWS plugins for another reporter (S3, CloudWatch Logs, Bedrock) does not turn it on; see Enable it.

For diagrams of the import flow, see Security Hub Reporter Diagrams.

docs.title: What it sends
docs.text:
One ASFF finding per finding in ASH's SARIF results, including suppressed findings. The findings go out in requests of at most 100, the per-request maximum of BatchImportFindings.

Each finding carries:

ASFF field Value Id ash/ followed by a SHA-256 of the finding's identity (see Finding identity) ProductArn The account's default product ARN, arn:<partition>:securityhub:<region>:<account-id>:product/<account-id>/default, where the partition is the Region's (aws, aws-us-gov, aws-cn) AwsAccountId The account that owns the credentials, or account_id if set GeneratorId ash/<scanner>/<rule id> Title <rule id>: <first line of the finding message>, up to 256 characters Description The finding message without its fenced code blocks, up to 1024 characters Severity.Label and FindingProviderFields.Severity.Label ASH's severity: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or INFORMATIONAL for ASH's INFO Types and FindingProviderFields.Types Software and Configuration Checks/Vulnerabilities/CVE when the rule id is a CVE, otherwise Software and Configuration Checks/Vulnerabilities Resources One resource of type Other whose Id is <scan target>/<file path> CreatedAt The scan's time. With archive_resolved_findings: true, kept from Security Hub for a finding that already exists there UpdatedAt The time the scan started (generated_at in ash_aggregated_results.json), in UTC as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ RecordState ARCHIVED for a suppressed finding, ACTIVE otherwise ProductName, CompanyName Automated Security Helper, AWS Labs ProductFields ash/target, ash/scope, ash/scanner, ash/ruleId, ash/severity, ash/suppressed, ash/file, ash/startLine, ash/endLine, and where they apply ash/workspaceProject, ash/suppressionJustification, ash/packageName, ash/packageVersion

This reporter is disabled by default: it sends findings to AWS with the host's credentials, so it runs only when your config sets enabled: true for it (see Enabling the AWS reporters).

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
The severity is the one ASH's own summary counts and severity_threshold gate use. A SARIF error result that has no explicit severity is therefore CRITICAL.

What is removed from the message before it is sent:

  • the quoted password in bandit's hardcoded-password messages (rules B105, B106 and B107, Possible hardcoded password: '...'), which ASH masks the way the flat-json and CSV reports do;
  • every fenced code block (```), which ASH treats as a code snippet.

Nothing else in a message is masked, and no code snippet from the SARIF result is sent. A scanner message that names a file by its absolute path, or quotes a value outside a fenced block, is sent as written.

docs.title: Finding identity
docs.text:
Security Hub keys a finding on its Id within the product ARN. A later import with the same Id and a later UpdatedAt updates the finding instead of adding a second one. The Id is "ash/" + sha256(json.dumps([target, key], sort_keys=True)), where the target is the reporter's findings_scope option (see Enable it). The key is the identity the id of a finding in ash.flat.json and ash.csv is a hash of. ash report uses the configuration it runs with, so it produces a scan's Ids only with the same findings_scope. ash merge takes no findings_scope from the configuration the shards recorded (see Options only the operator sets). The key holds:

  • the scanner and the rule id;
  • the file path, spelled one way: in a path written on Windows each backslash is a separator and becomes /, a path inside the scan root is made relative, and . and .. segments are resolved. Anywhere else a backslash is part of the file name, so on Linux or macOS a\b.py and a/b.py are two files with two Ids. A file a converter wrote (a converted notebook, a file inside an archive) is identified by its path under the converted files instead, marked as converted, so its findings keep their Id wherever the output directory is;
  • for dependency findings, the package name and path;
  • in a workspace, the project's key;
  • the result's SARIF fingerprints, or its partialFingerprints when it has no usable fingerprints. When it has neither, the start line and end line instead.

A fingerprint value counts as absent when it is a placeholder (semgrep without a login writes requires login on every result) or when results at different locations in the same scan share it, because then it does not identify one finding.

docs.title: Where these options can be set
docs.text:
aws_region, aws_profile and account_id choose where findings are sent and which credentials send them, and findings_scope and archive_resolved_findings choose which findings the reporter imports and whether it archives the ones that are resolved, so they are the operator's. They take effect only from the defaults (AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and AWS_PROFILE), --config-overrides, or a config file outside the scanned tree. A config file inside the scanned tree, or one an MCP client delivered, cannot set them: from the tree they are ignored with a warning, and under the MCP server they are default denied_paths entries, so a delivered config that changes one is refused.

Whether the reporter runs is the operator's too: a config file inside the scanned tree neither turns it on nor turns it off. Under the MCP server every setting of the section is a default denied_paths entry (/reporters/aws-security-hub/**), so a delivered config that turns the reporter on, or changes any of its settings, is refused. A client's enabled: false is not refused, but the server's enabled applies. See Settings only the operator can set.

The reporter is in the ash_aws_plugins package, which only the operator can load, with --ash-plugin-modules, ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES or the operator's own config, never a repository's. See Loading the plugins.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The id and the Id are keyed differently in one case: a path that is absolute in the results and lies inside the scan root. The id keys it as written, because ash.flat.json and ash.csv are built without the scan root, and the Id makes it relative first. So when one result names a file by its absolute path and another names the same file by its relative path, a fingerprint value both carry is shared for the Id, which sees one file, but not for the id, which sees two.

The scan time, the report id, the message and the severity are not part of the key, so a re-scan, a reworded message or a re-rated finding updates the existing finding. Nor are the column, which most scanners do not report, and the package version, so upgrading a package to a release that still has the vulnerability updates the finding. The account and Region are not part of it either, because the product ARN already contains them.

A finding identified by its lines gets a new Id when an edit moves it to another line. A finding with fingerprints keeps its Id.

When findings without fingerprints share a key (two secrets on one line, for example), each gets an occurrence suffix computed from its own column and message: the first 8 hex digits of sha256(json.dumps([column, message])), with -1 as the column when the scanner reports none. A newcomer therefore never takes an existing finding's Id, and removing one finding never hands its Id to another. A finding alone with its key has no suffix. Only exact duplicates, with the same column and message, are told apart by their order: the first has no ordinal, the next 1, then 2. Two results with the same fingerprints at the same place are one finding: it is sent once and the scan logs a WARNING.

docs.title: Suppressed findings
docs.text: A suppressed finding is sent with RecordState: ARCHIVED, so a finding that an earlier scan imported as ACTIVE is archived by the first scan after it is suppressed. If the suppression is removed, the next scan sends it as ACTIVE again, which reactivates it. ASH does not set Workflow: Security Hub ignores BatchImportFindings changes to Workflow once a finding exists.

docs.title: Findings a scan no longer reports
docs.text:
By default, a finding that a later scan no longer reports stays ACTIVE in Security Hub until Security Hub's retention removes it, 90 days after its last update. A finding a scan did not report is not always fixed: the scanner may have failed on the file, the scan may have covered less of the repository, or a new ignore_paths entry or rule change may hide it. So archiving them is opt-in.

With archive_resolved_findings: true, the reporter reads the findings already in Security Hub for this scan target (GetFindings, filtered on the product ARN and the ash/target product field) and re-imports, with RecordState: ARCHIVED and the scan's UpdatedAt, each one that:

  • is ACTIVE and has an Id that starts with ash/;
  • this scan did not produce;
  • came from a scanner that finished in this scan (status PASSED or FAILED, not excluded) without failing on a single target. A scanner that failed on some of its targets (cdk-nag on 4 of 10 templates, for example) still rolls up to FAILED; its findings are left alone, as are those of a scanner that errored, was missing or was skipped;
  • belongs to this scan's target and workspace project (ash/target and ash/workspaceProject). Both are compared because ash/target is <findings_scope>/<project key>: scope org with project repo reads the same as scope org/repo with none;
  • has this scan's scope (ash/scope): the same scanned directory relative to the repository root, and the converted tree (archives, notebooks) scanned in both or in neither. A scan of services/api under the same findings_scope does not archive what a scan of the whole repository found. Deleting the last notebook or archive changes the scope as well (converted=yes becomes converted=no), so the findings recorded under the earlier scope stay ACTIVE until Security Hub's retention removes them;
  • was last updated before this scan. A finding a later scan wrote is never archived by re-reporting an older one.

The scanned directory is the one the scan recorded in its results (scan_source in the metadata), not one the reporter works out where it runs. So ash report on another host, or on the output of ash merge on a collector without the checkout, compares the scan's scope. ash merge records no directory, and so the report archives nothing, when the shards recorded different ones; it records changed_files_only: true when any shard was filtered to changed files.

In container mode the scanned directory is always /src inside the container, where git sees only the mount. ash works the directory out on the host and always passes it in, empty when it has none. Running the ASH image yourself (as a CI job image, for example) is not container mode in this sense, unless it mounts the directory at /src or sets ASH_ACTUAL_SOURCE_DIR, as the legacy ./ash and PowerShell (Invoke-ASH) wrappers do.

A scan the legacy ./ash or Invoke-ASH wrapper starts records no directory, so with archive_resolved_findings: true it never archives. The wrappers pass no directory into the container, and git there sees only the mount, so it cannot tell a repository's root from a clone nested in another repository. Such a run prints a notice to stderr, once, whatever the log level. To archive, use ash --mode container, or run ASH directly.

A linked worktree of the same repository inside its checkout (git worktree add, one that the outer repository's git worktree list names) records its directory relative to the worktree's own root. The scan records no directory, and so archives nothing, when:

  • the directory's repository sits below another repository: a git submodule, a repository cloned inside another one's work tree, any repository under an enclosing one (a home directory kept in git, for example), or a directory whose .git file or symlink points into the outer repository's git directory without being one of its listed worktrees. git would call each of their roots ., like the outer repository's. GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES is read as git reads it (an entry after an empty entry is compared as written, without resolving symlinks), and it hides the repository above a listed directory only when that repository neither tracks the directory's repository, or a path between them (a submodule's gitlink, for example), nor lists it as untracked and not ignored. That is the opt-out for a checkout under an enclosing repository that ignores it, such as a home directory kept in git whose .gitignore leaves out src/: with the ceiling at the home directory, the checkout records its own directory. Where the enclosing repository tracks the checkout or would list it in git status, the ceiling changes nothing and the scan records no directory;
  • in container mode, the host directory is not inside a git repository, or git on the host refuses the repository (for example because another user owns it), or the directory's path relative to the repository root contains ;, \, a control character or bytes that are not UTF-8, or starts with a segment that reads as a drive (C: or a:b);
  • the directory is in a linked worktree, and the repository's git directory holds a FIFO or a symlink where git worktree list reads (a worktree's admin dir, a HEAD or a ref one names, or packed-refs): the list is not read, so the worktree counts as nested;
  • in container mode, a workspace project's mount is not a repository's root;
  • the legacy ./ash or Invoke-ASH wrapper started the scan, or you ran the ASH image yourself with the directory mounted at /src or ASH_ACTUAL_SOURCE_DIR set, and no ASH_SCAN_SOURCE;
  • the directory it would record is not UTF-8: its path relative to the repository root or, outside a repository, its own path. No scan starts on a directory whose path is not UTF-8, in any mode: a scan run on the host (local, precommit or nix mode) would write that path into its results and SARIF, so ash exits 1 at once, and container mode cannot bind-mount it, so ash exits 3 before any runtime call; either way it writes nothing and says to rename the directory.

With archiving on, results that record no directory print a notice to stderr, once per ash command (an MCP server prints it for its first such scan; every receipt still gives the reason), that nothing is archived and why.

Nothing is archived from one shard of a split scan (--shard-index), from a scan run with --changed-files-only, or from results that do not record whether they were filtered or which directory was scanned (results from an older ASH lack both). The receipt's archive_skipped says why when archiving did not apply, and archive_scanners lists the scanners it applied to.

Archiving cannot tell a fixed finding from one that a new ignore_paths entry or a scanner rule change stopped reporting; both are archived. Turn archiving on only for scans whose configuration you control, and run them from one branch (see Enable it).

A finding that comes back in a later scan is imported as ACTIVE again. Security Hub then sets its workflow status back to NEW if it was NOTIFIED or RESOLVED.

The same read keeps CreatedAt for every finding that already exists in Security Hub. With archiving off nothing is read, and CreatedAt is the scan's time on every import.

docs.title: Enable it
docs.text:
1. Enable Security Hub in the account and Region that should receive the findings:
aws securityhub enable-security-hub --region us-east-1
  1. Load the AWS plugins, enable the reporter, and set the Region and the findings scope in the operator's ASH configuration, a config file outside the scanned tree:
ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins
reporters:
  aws-security-hub:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: us-east-1
      findings_scope: my-org/my-service

The same settings from the command line:

ash --config-overrides 'ash_plugin_modules+=["automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins"]' \
    --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled=true' \
    --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.options.aws_region=us-east-1' \
    --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.options.findings_scope=my-org/my-service'

  1. Provide AWS credentials for that account: environment variables, a profile (aws_profile or AWS_PROFILE), or an instance or task role.

  2. Import from one branch. Every scan of the repository updates the same findings, so a scan of a feature branch overwrites, and with archiving on archives, what the default branch reported. In CI, enable the reporter only for the default branch, for example with --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled=true' on that job alone, and pass --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled=false' on every other job. A pull request can change the repository's .ash/.ash.yaml, and the override wins over what it says.

findings_scope is required. Choose a name unique to the repository among those that import into the same account and Region, such as its owner/name on the code host: every finding's Id and its ash/target field come from it, archiving touches only the findings recorded with it, and two repositories with the same scope would overwrite, and archive, each other's findings. It is at most 1024 characters. The reporter does not fall back to project_name, which the scanned repository's own configuration can set, or to the directory name, which is not unique (in container mode it is always /src).

docs.title: Options only the operator sets
docs.text:
enabled, aws_region, aws_profile, account_id, findings_scope and archive_resolved_findings decide whether a scan sends findings, to which account and Region, with which credentials, and which findings in the account it updates and archives. They are the operator's: set them with --config-overrides, in the file ASH_CONFIG names, or in another config file outside the scanned tree, never in the scanned repository's own configuration (a discovered .ash/.ash.yaml, a --config inside the tree, an extends base, or ASH_CONFIG naming a file inside the tree). A repository that could set them could turn the import on from a pull request, pick another profile on the operator's machine, send its findings to another account or Region, or name another repository's findings_scope and overwrite or archive its findings. On a job that must not import, --config-overrides 'reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled=false' turns the reporter off whatever the repository's configuration says.

ASH enforces this for findings_scope and archive_resolved_findings. When the configuration was read from a file inside the scanned tree, a value either option has there is ignored with a warning, unless --config-overrides or the operator's own config file outside the tree (the file ASH_CONFIG names, or a workspace's default config) sets it. A config file outside the tree that extends a file inside it, or a file a link inside the tree leads to, counts as inside for this. An ignored findings_scope leaves it unset, so the reporter refuses before any AWS call; an ignored archive_resolved_findings is false. A --config-overrides key with a dot-separated part that is empty, holds whitespace, or holds a character that does not print is refused (exit 3) rather than written to a key the reporter never reads. ash report judges its --config against the repository that holds the results as well as against the working directory. The MCP get_config tool shows both options from a config file in a checkout as <operator only; ignored from this file: VALUE>, since a scan of that checkout ignores them. ash merge ignores both in the configuration the shards recorded, since a file in a shard's repository could have set them; it imports into Security Hub only as the operator's own --config sets the reporter up. More generally, the whole section of a reporter that sends findings off the host, Security Hub's included, comes only from the operator: see Enabling the AWS reporters.

Before the report phase, ASH checks the dependencies of every enabled reporter. For this one the check needs the Region, calls securityhub:DescribeHub, and calls sts:GetCallerIdentity when account_id is not set. If the Region or the credentials are missing, or Security Hub is not enabled, it logs an ERROR and the reporter does not run.

When the reporter runs, it checks the rest before it reads from or writes to Security Hub: that findings_scope is set, and, with sts:GetCallerIdentity, that account_id (when set) is the credentials' account. If either fails, the reporter fails with a message that says what to set, and nothing is sent. The same checks run in ash report --format aws-security-hub, which skips the dependency check.

ash report --format aws-security-hub refuses unless the reporter is enabled in the configuration, and refuses a workspace's unified results file: run it once per project, with --output-dir set to projects/<key>/ under the workspace output.

--output-formats accepts aws-security-hub: with the AWS plugin module loaded and the reporter enabled, a scan that names it imports that scan's findings. A scan whose --output-formats leave it out neither checks nor runs the reporter, so the dependency check above, DescribeHub and STS included, runs only for a scan that will run the reporter. To import an earlier scan's results, run ash report --format aws-security-hub in the directory that holds .ash/ash_output, with the reporter enabled in the configuration.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Meaning findings_scope none Name of this repository's findings in the account and Region; the Ids and archiving follow it. Required, at most 1024 characters. Operator only. aws_region AWS_REGION, then AWS_DEFAULT_REGION Region whose Security Hub receives the findings. Required. Operator only. aws_profile AWS_PROFILE Named profile for the credentials. Operator only. account_id the credentials' account Account that receives the findings. Must be the credentials' account; with the default product ARN, Security Hub accepts a finding only from the account it names. An unquoted number is read as a 12-digit id, with the leading zeros YAML drops put back. Operator only. archive_resolved_findings false Archive findings this scan no longer reports (see Findings a scan no longer reports), and keep CreatedAt for existing findings. Needs securityhub:GetFindings. Operator only. max_retries 3 Retries for a throttled or failed request base_delay 1.0 Base delay in seconds between retries, doubled on each retry, plus up to one second of jitter max_delay 60.0 Longest delay in seconds between retries

The defaults of aws_region and aws_profile are read from the environment when ASH starts.

reporters:
  aws-security-hub:
    enabled: true
    options:
      findings_scope: my-org/my-service
      aws_region: us-west-2
      aws_profile: security-scanning
      account_id: "123456789012"
      archive_resolved_findings: true
      max_retries: 5

docs.title: IAM permissions
docs.text:
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ImportFindings",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "securityhub:BatchImportFindings",
        "securityhub:DescribeHub"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "ArchiveResolvedFindings",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "securityhub:GetFindings",
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
  • securityhub:BatchImportFindings imports the findings and the archive records.
  • securityhub:DescribeHub is the dependency check that Security Hub is enabled.
  • securityhub:GetFindings reads the existing findings for archiving and for CreatedAt. Only archive_resolved_findings: true needs it, so leave the ArchiveResolvedFindings statement out when archiving is off.
  • sts:GetCallerIdentity finds the account, and checks account_id before anything is sent. It needs no permission.

docs.title: Results and failures
docs.text:
When every finding is imported, reports/ash.aws-security-hub.asff.json holds the receipt and the findings exactly as they were sent. With archiving on:

{
  "product_arn": "arn:aws:securityhub:us-east-1:123456789012:product/123456789012/default",
  "aws_account_id": "123456789012",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "imported": 12,
  "requests": 1,
  "duplicates_skipped": 0,
  "archived": 1,
  "archived_ids": ["ash/..."],
  "archive_scanners": ["bandit", "checkov"],
  "archive_skipped": null,
  "findings": []
}

imported counts the findings and the archive records Security Hub accepted. With no findings and nothing to archive, ASH makes no call and writes a receipt with "imported": 0.

If any finding is not imported, the reporter fails: the scan logs Error in reporter SecurityHubReporter: ... with the counts and the cause, no receipt is written, and ash report exits 1. The scan's exit code does not change. The causes and what the message tells you to do:

Cause Message Reporter not enabled (ash report --format aws-security-hub without enabled: true) Set reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled: true. Invalid reporter configuration (for example max_retries: three) The scan refuses the configuration with exit 3 when it loads the plugins, before anything is scanned, and names the option (reporters.aws-security-hub.options.max_retries); ash report exits 1 with the same field. Fix it. A workspace's unified results (ash report over the workspace output) Run ash report with --output-dir set to a project's directory, projects/<key>/. No findings_scope Set reporters.aws-security-hub.options.findings_scope in the operator's configuration (--config-overrides, or a config file outside the scanned tree). No Region Set reporters.aws-security-hub.options.aws_region, AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION. No credentials Provide credentials for the account. account_id is not the credentials' account Use credentials for that account, or remove account_id. Security Hub not enabled (InvalidAccessException, or every finding rejected with InvalidAccess) Run aws securityhub enable-security-hub --region <region> in the account, and check that the credentials belong to it. Access denied (AccessDeniedException) Grant securityhub:BatchImportFindings. GetFindings refused The findings are still imported, then the reporter fails: grant securityhub:GetFindings, or set archive_resolved_findings: false. Throttling (LimitExceededException, HTTP 429) after the retries Retry later, or raise max_retries or base_delay. Findings rejected in a successful response (FailedCount, FailedFindings) Each rejected finding is logged with its Id, error code and message. InvalidInput means ASH built a finding Security Hub does not accept; report it. A request botocore refuses before sending it A defect in ASH's ASFF conversion; report it.

A request that fails stops the import: the findings in later requests are not sent, and the message says how many were imported before it. When Security Hub rejects a whole request with InvalidAccess, the rest are not sent either.

BatchImportFindings is limited to 10 requests per second with a burst of 30, and GetFindings to 3 with a burst of 6 (throttling limits). ASH retries a throttled request with exponential backoff.

docs.title: Viewing the findings
docs.text:
In the Security Hub console, filter findings by product name Automated Security Helper, or by the ash/target product field to see one repository. The same filter from the command line:

aws securityhub get-findings --region us-east-1 \
  --filters '{"ProductName": [{"Value": "Automated Security Helper", "Comparison": "EQUALS"}]}'

Security Hub sends a Security Hub Findings - Imported event to Amazon EventBridge for each finding it creates or updates, which you can route to a notification or a ticketing system.

docs.title: Workspace scans
docs.text: In a workspace scan the reporter runs once per project, in that project's own report phase, and imports and archives that project's findings under the scan target <findings_scope>/<project key> (just <findings_scope> when the two are the same). It does not run again at workspace level, because that would import every finding a second time.

docs.title: Built-in Plugins
docs.text: ASH ships with a comprehensive set of built-in plugins that provide core security scanning, reporting, and file processing capabilities. These plugins are automatically available and can be configured to meet your specific security requirements.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Built-in plugins are organized into four main categories:

Category Purpose Count Location Scanners Analyze code and infrastructure for security vulnerabilities 16 scanners/ Reporters Generate scan results in various output formats 15 reporters/ Converters Process and prepare files for scanning 2 converters/ Event Handlers Handle scan lifecycle events and notifications 2 event_handlers/

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Most built-in plugins are enabled by default and require no additional configuration to get started. The exceptions are the spdx and yaml reporters, which ship disabled; see Output formats for the per-reporter default.

# Run with default built-in scanners
ash /path/to/code

# Use specific built-in scanners only
ash /path/to/code --scanners bandit,semgrep

# Generate reports in multiple formats
ash /path/to/code --reporters sarif,html,csv

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Built-in plugins can be customized through configuration files:

# ash-config.yml
scanners:
  bandit:
    enabled: true
    options:
      severity_threshold: "MEDIUM"
      confidence_level: "high"    # lowercase only

  semgrep:
    enabled: true
    options:
      config: "p/ci"
      scan_timeout: 1800

reporters:
  html:
    enabled: true             # The HTML reporter exposes no options

  sarif:
    enabled: true             # The SARIF reporter exposes no options

docs.title: Security Scanners
docs.text:
Built-in scanners cover a wide range of security analysis:

  • Static Analysis: Bandit, Semgrep, OpenGrep
  • Infrastructure Security: CDK-Nag, CFN-Nag, Checkov
  • Dependency Scanning: NPM Audit, Grype
  • Secret Detection: Detect-Secrets
  • SBOM Generation: Syft

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
Multiple output formats support different use cases:

  • CI/CD Integration: SARIF, JUnit XML, GitLab SAST
  • Human Readable: HTML, Markdown, Text
  • Data Processing: CSV, JSON, YAML
  • Compliance: SPDX, CycloneDX, OCSF

docs.title: File Processing
docs.text:
Converters handle various file types:

  • Archives: Automatic extraction of zip, tar, and other compressed formats
  • Notebooks: Jupyter notebook processing for Python code analysis

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Built-in plugins may require external tools to be installed:

# Check plugin dependencies
ash dependencies --check

# Install missing dependencies (where possible)
ash dependencies --install

docs.title: Plugin-Specific Configuration
docs.text:
Each plugin supports specific configuration options:

scanners:
  checkov:
    options:
      frameworks: ["terraform", "cloudformation"]
      skip_frameworks: ["secrets"]
      skip_path:                       # Each entry needs a path and a reason
        - path: "tests/fixtures/.*"
          reason: "Vulnerable-by-design fixtures"
      config_file: ".checkov.yaml"

Selecting or skipping individual checks is done in a checkov configuration file rather than through ASH options; point config_file at one.

docs.title: Selective Plugin Execution
docs.text:
Control which plugins run:

# Run only infrastructure scanners
ash --scanners cdk-nag,cfn-nag,checkov

# Exclude specific scanners
ash --exclude-scanners grype,syft

# Generate only compliance reports
ash --reporters spdx,cyclonedx

docs.title: Integration with External Tools
docs.text:
Built-in plugins integrate with popular security tools:

  • Semgrep: Uses Semgrep Registry rules
  • Bandit: Leverages Python AST analysis
  • Checkov: Supports custom policy frameworks
  • Grype: Integrates with vulnerability databases

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common issues and solutions:

docs.title: Scanner Not Found
docs.text:
# Check if scanner dependencies are installed
ash dependencies --check --scanner bandit

# Install missing dependencies
pip install bandit

docs.title: Configuration Issues
docs.text:
# Validate configuration
ash config --validate

# Show effective configuration
ash config --show

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
# Run scanners in parallel (default)
ash --parallel

# Limit concurrent scanners
ash --max-workers 2

# Skip time-intensive scanners for quick feedback
ash --exclude-scanners grype,syft

docs.text:
