plugins:
  my-plugin:
    enabled: true
    options:
      option1: value1
      option2: value2

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Feature 1: Description
  • Feature 2: Description

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
# Example command line usage
ash --plugins my-plugin

[!CAUTION] > Community Plugin Security: Community plugins are third-party packages that you install separately (e.g., via pip install). Always verify the source and trustworthiness of these packages before installation. ASH's built-in plugins are included directly in the ASH repository under automated_security_helper/plugin_modules and don't require separate package installation.

docs.title: ASH Ferret Scan Plugin
docs.text: This plugin integrates Ferret Scan with the Automated Security Helper (ASH) to provide comprehensive sensitive data detection for source code and documents.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Ferret Scan plugin enables ASH to leverage Ferret's powerful sensitive data detection capabilities for:

  • Credit Card Detection: 15+ card brands with mathematical validation (Luhn algorithm)
  • Passport Numbers: Multi-country formats including US, UK, Canada, EU, and MRZ
  • Social Security Numbers: Domain-aware validation with HR/Tax/Healthcare context
  • API Keys & Secrets: 40+ patterns including AWS, GitHub, Google Cloud, Stripe, and more
  • Email Addresses: RFC-compliant with domain validation
  • Phone Numbers: International and domestic formats
  • IP Addresses: IPv4 and IPv6 with network context
  • Social Media Profiles: LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Facebook, GitHub, Instagram, TikTok
  • Intellectual Property: Patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets
  • Document Metadata: EXIF and document metadata extraction

docs.title: ASH Convention Compliance
docs.text: This plugin follows ASH conventions for consistent behavior across all scanners:

docs.title: Hardcoded by Plugin (Do NOT configure at plugin level)
docs.text: Feature ASH Convention Notes Output Format Always SARIF Required by ASH for result aggregation Color Output Always --no-color ASH handles formatting

docs.title: Ferret-Scan Log Controls
docs.text:
Option Description ferret_debug: true Enables ferret-scan's own debug output (preprocessing/validation flow) ferret_verbose: true Enables ferret-scan's own verbose output (detailed finding info)

Note: Bare debug and verbose are blocked to avoid confusion with ASH's --debug/--verbose flags.

docs.title: Managed by ASH Framework
docs.text: Feature ASH Convention Notes Output Directory .ash/ash_output/scanners/ferret-scan/ Follows ASH conventions Offline Mode ASH_OFFLINE=true Respects ASH offline mode Suppressions global_settings.suppressions in the ASH config file Managed centrally by ASH

docs.title: Unsupported Options
docs.text:
The following ferret-scan CLI options are NOT supported and will raise an error:

Option Reason format, output_format ASH requires SARIF format debug, verbose Use ferret_debug/ferret_verbose instead (avoids confusion with ASH flags) web, port Web server mode not applicable enable_redaction, redaction_*, memory_scrub Post-processing, not scanning generate_suppressions, show_suppressed, suppressions_file ASH manages suppressions extract_text Utility mode, not scanning preprocess_only, pre_commit_mode, list_profiles Utility/pre-commit modes — produce no SARIF scan results

docs.title: Version Compatibility
docs.text:
This plugin is tested and compatible with specific ferret-scan versions. Using versions outside the supported range may result in unexpected behavior.

Supported Versions: 2.4.5 to 2.6.0 (exclusive)

Plugin Version ferret-scan Version Notes Current 2.4.5 - 2.6.0 (exclusive) 2.4.5 and 2.5.2 verified end to end; 2.5.2 is the recommended version

docs.title: Install Ferret Scan
docs.text:
The plugin runs the ferret-scan command. ASH finds it on PATH, or beside the Python interpreter that runs ASH, which is where ash dependencies install puts it.

ASH (Recommended) — installs the version the plugin is tested against into the Python environment that runs ASH, with pip or uv, whichever owns that environment (a uv tool, uvx or uv venv install has no pip): 

ash dependencies install --config .ash/.ash_community_plugins.yaml

pip: pass the supported range. A bare pip install ferret-scan resolves to the newest release, which may sit outside the range in the table above — that is how a release published partway through a CI run once failed every open pull request without a source change. 

pip install 'ferret-scan>=2.4.5,<2.6.0'

Build from Source: 

git clone https://github.com/awslabs/ferret-scan.git
cd ferret-scan
make build

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
ferret-scan --version
ferret-scan --help

docs.title: Enable the Plugin
docs.text: The ferret-scan plugin is a community plugin that must be explicitly enabled. There are two ways to do this:

docs.title: Option 1: Add to ASH Configuration File (Recommended)
docs.text:
Include the plugin module in your ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project):

ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins

scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true

docs.title: Option 2: Command Line Flag
docs.text:
Use the --ash-plugin-modules flag when running ASH:

uv run ash scan --source-dir /path/to/code \
    --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins

docs.title: Verify Plugin is Loaded
docs.text:
# With config file
uv run ash plugin list | grep -i ferret

# Or with command line flag
uv run ash plugin list --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins | grep -i ferret

You should see ferret-scan in the list of scanners.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
Add scanner configuration to your ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project):

scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true

docs.title: Run Ferret Scan
docs.text:
# Scan current directory
uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan

# Scan specific directory
uv run ash --source-dir /path/to/project --scanners ferret-scan

# Run with ferret-scan's own debug output
uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan -o ferret_debug=true

# Run with ferret-scan's own verbose output
uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan -o ferret_verbose=true

docs.title: Run Without Configuration File
docs.text:
If you want to run Ferret Scan without saving a configuration file:

# Scan current directory only with ferret-scan
uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan \
  --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins

# Scan with all available scanners (including ferret-scan)
uv run ash --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins

docs.title: Basic Options
docs.text:
scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      confidence_levels: "all"    # high, medium, low, or combinations
      checks: "all"               # Specific checks to run
      recursive: true             # Recursively scan directories

docs.title: Configuration Options Reference
docs.text: Option Type Default Description confidence_levels string "all" Confidence levels: high, medium, low, or combinations like high,medium checks string "all" Specific checks to run (comma-separated) recursive bool true Recursively scan directories config_file string null Path to custom Ferret YAML config file use_default_config bool true Use the default config bundled with this plugin. Set by the operator only; see Using profiles profile string null Profile name from config file. Set by the operator only; see Using profiles exclude_patterns list [] Glob patterns to exclude. ASH also excludes its own output directories inside the scanned directory, except one whose path holds a comma, which ferret-scan's comma-separated --exclude cannot hold; ferret-scan then reads it, ASH logs a warning naming it, and the findings ferret-scan reports there are dropped. The files global_settings.ignore_paths ignores are excluded too, each by its full path, as ASH matches the ignore paths: an ignore path ASH matches to no file, such as a bare api (write api/ for the directory), excludes nothing. show_match bool false Display matched text in ferret-scan's own output (see show_match below) enable_preprocessors bool true Enable text extraction from documents (PDF, Office) finding_limit int 0 Max findings ferret-scan emits (--limit). 0 = unlimited. ASH defaults to 0 because ferret-scan's own default of 200 silently truncates large scans. fail_on_incomplete bool false Pass --fail-on-incomplete so ferret-scan exits 3 when a file could not be fully scanned; ASH still reports the partial findings, counts the target as failed, and records the scanner ERROR, so the completeness gate fails the scan. respect_gitignore bool false Pass --respect-gitignore to honor .gitignore. Off by default — .gitignore often hides high-value files (.env, *.pem) a sensitive-data scan should see. disable_ip_types string null Comma-separated INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY sub-types to skip (--disable-ip-types): copyright,patent,trademark,trade_secret,internal_url. explain bool false Pass --explain for an offline per-finding rationale + verdict + drafted suppression reason. No data leaves the host. validator_budget string null Per-validator time budget (--validator-budget), e.g. SSN=500ms,all=2m. Over-budget validators stop and mark the scan incomplete. max_live_bytes string null Cap on extracted content held in memory (--max-live-bytes), e.g. 256MB/1GB. Bounds peak memory on constrained hosts. ferret_debug bool false Enable ferret-scan's own debug logging (preprocessing/validation flow) ferret_verbose bool false Enable ferret-scan's own verbose output (detailed finding info) tool_version string null Version constraint for ferret-scan (e.g., >=2.4.5,<2.6.0, ==2.5.2) skip_version_check bool false Skip version compatibility check (use with caution)

docs.title: Options NOT Supported (Will Raise Error)
docs.text:
The following options are not supported because they conflict with ASH conventions. Setting one stops the scan with exit code 3 when ASH loads the plugins, before anything is converted or scanned. The error names the option's location and gives the message in the table, for example:

Configuration validation failed: scanners.ferret-scan.options (scanner 'ferret-scan'): Value error, Unsupported option 'debug' in ferret-scan plugin configuration. Use 'ferret_debug: true' instead. Bare 'debug' is blocked to avoid confusion with ASH's --debug flag.

Any other option the plugin does not declare is refused the same way, as Unknown key '<option>' with the accepted options listed. ash config validate and ash config lint do not import the plugin, so they do not catch either kind; both say its section is not checked there, and a scan checks it.

Option Error Message format, output_format "ASH requires SARIF format for result aggregation" debug "Use 'ferret_debug: true' instead. Bare 'debug' is blocked to avoid confusion with ASH's --debug flag." verbose "Use 'ferret_verbose: true' instead. Bare 'verbose' is blocked to avoid confusion with ASH's --verbose flag." web, port "Web server mode is not supported in ASH integration" enable_redaction, redaction_output_dir, redaction_strategy, redaction_audit_log, memory_scrub "Redaction is not supported in ASH integration" generate_suppressions, show_suppressed, suppressions_file "ASH manages suppressions centrally" extract_text "Text extraction mode is not supported" preprocess_only "Outputs extracted text and exits — produces no SARIF results" pre_commit_mode "ASH manages output formatting and exit codes; use ASH's own pre-commit hook" list_profiles "Only prints available profiles and exits — produces no scan results"

docs.title: show_match
docs.text:
With show_match on, ferret-scan writes each matched value (card numbers, national IDs, keys) into its own output: the result message (Matched text: '...') and the SARIF snippets. ASH masks those values before it writes ash_aggregated_results.json or any report, so they do not reach ASH's reports, the Bedrock summary or MCP responses (see "Secret values in reports" in the output formats page). They do stay in ferret-scan's own results file under scanners/ferret-scan/, and in its log output.

show_match is off by default, and every profile in the bundled ferret-config.yaml sets it to false, including debug, comprehensive, json-api, person-name, enhanced-metadata and social-media, which turned it on before. Turn it on only where the scanner's own output directory is protected.

docs.title: Available Checks
docs.text:
The authoritative list for your installed version is ferret-scan --help checks — do not hardcode it, as ferret-scan adds detectors between releases. As of v2.4.5 through v2.5.2:

  • BANK_ACCOUNT - Bank account / IBAN / routing numbers
  • CLOUD_RESOURCES - Cloud resource identifiers (AWS ARNs, Azure/GCP/OCI/IBM/Alibaba IDs)
  • CREDIT_CARD - Credit card numbers (Visa, MasterCard, Amex, etc.)
  • DATE_OF_BIRTH - Dates of birth
  • DRIVERS_LICENSE - Driver's license numbers (state formats)
  • EMAIL - Email addresses
  • INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY - Patents, trademarks, copyrights (internal-URL detection requires config)
  • IP_ADDRESS - IPv4 and IPv6 addresses
  • MEDICAL_ID - Medical / health identifiers (PHI)
  • METADATA - Document, image, audio, and video metadata
  • OTP - One-time-passcode / two-factor secrets
  • PASSPORT - Passport numbers (multi-country)
  • PERSON_NAME - Person names
  • PHONE - Phone numbers
  • PHYSICAL_ADDRESS - Physical / postal addresses
  • SECRETS - API keys, tokens, passwords
  • SOCIAL_MEDIA - Social media profiles
  • SSN - Social Security Numbers
  • VIN - Vehicle Identification Numbers

docs.title: Note: API_KEY_OR_SECRET false positives (SECRETS check)
docs.text:
The SECRETS check includes a generic API_KEY_OR_SECRET detector that matches on the name of an assignment when the name is a secret keyword (session, token, secret, password, api_key, …) — regardless of the value. So typed code and config such as a session field on a generated model, a session local, or a Terraform local named manage_auth_secret can be flagged at HIGH confidence even though no credential is present.

This detector cannot be disabled in ferret-scan's config (the tool honors disabled_types only for the INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY check, not SECRETS). The plugin keeps it enabled so real secrets are still found, and expects you to manage false positives with ASH's own controls — a path-scoped suppression:

global_settings:
  suppressions:
    - path: path/to/generated_or_test_file.py
      rule_id: API_KEY_OR_SECRET
      reason: "False positive — variable/field name matches the secret-keyword heuristic, not a credential"

or the plugin's exclude_patterns, or scoping the checks option to omit SECRETS.

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      confidence_levels: "high,medium"
      checks: "CREDIT_CARD,SECRETS,SSN,PASSPORT"
      recursive: true
      profile: "security-audit"
      config_file: "/etc/ash/ferret-config.yaml"  # outside the scanned tree
      # show_match: false  # Keep disabled to avoid logging sensitive data
      enable_preprocessors: true  # Extract text from PDFs, Office docs
      exclude_patterns:
        - "*.log"
        - "node_modules/**"
        - "vendor/**"
        - ".git/**"

profile, use_default_config and config_file take effect only from the operator: profile and use_default_config from --config-overrides or a config file outside the scanned tree, and config_file only when the file it names is outside the tree.

Note: Do NOT configure bare debug, verbose, format, or suppression options at the plugin level. Use ferret_debug/ferret_verbose for ferret-scan's own log output. Other options are managed by ASH globally.

docs.title: Version Pinning
docs.text:
Pin to a specific ferret-scan version for reproducible builds:

scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      tool_version: "==2.5.2"  # Exact version

Or use a version range:

scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      tool_version: ">=2.4.5,<2.6.0"  # Compatible range

To bypass version checks (not recommended for production):

scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      skip_version_check: true  # Use with caution

docs.title: Default Configuration
docs.text:
This plugin includes a bundled ferret-config.yaml that is automatically used when no custom config is specified. The default config includes:

  • Comprehensive validator patterns for intellectual property detection
  • Social media platform detection patterns (LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook, etc.)
  • Pre-configured profiles for common use cases
  • AWS/Amazon internal URL patterns for IP detection

docs.title: Available Profiles
docs.text:
The default configuration includes these pre-defined profiles:

Profile Description quick Fast security check (high confidence only) thorough All confidence levels with text extraction ci CI/CD integration (JUnit XML output) security-audit Security team scanning (JSON output) comprehensive Complete analysis (YAML output) credit-card PCI compliance focused passport Identity verification focused intellectual-property IP detection focused json-api Structured JSON for APIs csv-export CSV for spreadsheet analysis silent Minimal output for automation

docs.title: Using Profiles
docs.text:
A profile changes what is reported: it can run fewer checks and report only higher-confidence findings. On ASH's ferret-scan test files, with ferret-scan 2.5.3, the bundled config reported 111 findings with no profile, 30 with quick, and none with six of its profiles. The bundled redaction and secure-redaction profiles also have ferret-scan write redacted copies of the files it scans. use_default_config: false changes what is reported too, since the empty config it gives ferret-scan has none of the bundled validators' patterns.

So profile and use_default_config are the operator's choice. A config file inside the scanned tree, or one an MCP client delivered, does not set them, and the scan's warnings name the value that was ignored (see Settings a repository's config cannot choose). Set them with --config-overrides:

ash --config-overrides 'scanners.ferret-scan.options.profile=security-audit'

or in a config file outside the scanned tree, named with --config:

scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      profile: "security-audit"

docs.title: Option 1: Custom Config File Path
docs.text:
scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      config_file: "/path/to/your/custom-ferret.yaml"

docs.title: Option 2: Config File in Source Directory
docs.text: A config file inside the scanned tree is not passed to ferret-scan, whether config_file names it or the plugin finds it by name (ferret.yaml, ferret.yml, .ferret.yaml, .ferret.yml, .ash/ferret.yaml or .ash/ferret-scan.yaml in the source directory). The bundled config is used instead, and the scan's warnings name the file. Put the file outside the scanned tree and name it with config_file.

docs.title: Option 3: Disable Default Config
docs.text:
scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      use_default_config: false  # Use ferret-scan's built-in defaults only

Like profile, this is honored only from the operator: --config-overrides or a config file outside the scanned tree.

docs.title: Creating a Custom Config File
docs.text:
Copy the default config from the plugin:

cp $(python -c "import automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins as p; print(p.__path__[0])")/ferret-config.yaml ./my-ferret-config.yaml

Or create a minimal config that only overrides what you need:

# my-ferret-config.yaml
defaults:
  confidence_levels: high,medium
  checks: SECRETS,CREDIT_CARD,SSN

validators:
  intellectual_property:
    internal_urls:
      - "http[s]?:\\/\\/.*\\.mycompany\\.com"
      - "http[s]?:\\/\\/internal\\..*"

docs.title: High Confidence Findings Only
docs.text:
scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      confidence_levels: "high"

docs.title: PCI Compliance Scan
docs.text:
scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      checks: "CREDIT_CARD"
      confidence_levels: "all"
      profile: "credit-card"

docs.title: Secrets Detection Only
docs.text:
scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      checks: "SECRETS"
      confidence_levels: "high,medium"

docs.title: Combined with Other Scanners
docs.text:
# Use Ferret Scan alongside other ASH scanners
uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan,bandit,detect-secrets

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text:
# Run in container mode for CI/CD
uv run ash --mode container --scanners ferret-scan

docs.title: Output Integration
docs.text:
Ferret Scan results are integrated into ASH's unified reporting system:

  • SARIF Format: Machine-readable results for CI/CD integration
  • HTML Reports: Visual security dashboard with remediation guidance
  • JSON/CSV: Structured data for analysis and tracking
  • Markdown: Human-readable summaries for pull requests

Results are written to: 

.ash/ash_output/
├── scanners/
│   └── ferret-scan/
│       └── source/
│           └── ferret-scan.sarif
└── reports/
    └── ash.sarif  # Aggregated results

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Ferret Scan not found: 

# Check if ferret-scan is in PATH
which ferret-scan

# Install if missing
pip install ferret-scan

Unsupported option error: If the scan exits 3 with an error like: 

Configuration validation failed: scanners.ferret-scan.options (scanner 'ferret-scan'): Value error, Unsupported option 'debug' in ferret-scan plugin configuration. Use 'ferret_debug: true' instead. Bare 'debug' is blocked to avoid confusion with ASH's --debug flag.

This means you used a bare option name that's blocked. Use the ferret_ prefixed version instead: 

scanners:
  ferret-scan:
    enabled: true
    options:
      ferret_debug: true    # Correct
      ferret_verbose: true  # Correct

Empty directory warnings: The plugin will skip scanning if the target directory is empty or doesn't exist, logging an appropriate warning message.

No findings in output: 

# Check if ferret-scan works directly
ferret-scan --format sarif --file /path/to/test/file

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Enable ferret-scan's own debug/verbose output to troubleshoot issues:

# Enable ferret-scan's debug output (shows preprocessing and validation flow)
uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan -o ferret_debug=true

# Enable ferret-scan's verbose output (shows detailed finding info)
uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan -o ferret_verbose=true

docs.title: Pre-commit Hook
docs.text:
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: ash-ferret-scan
        name: ASH Ferret Scan Sensitive Data Detection
        entry: uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan --mode precommit
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/security.yml
name: Security Scan
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install ferret-scan
          pip install uv
      - name: Run ASH with Ferret Scan
        run: |
          uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan --output-format sarif \
            --config-overrides "ash_plugin_modules+=[\"automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins\"]"
      - name: Upload SARIF results
        # Also when ASH exits non-zero on findings: without a status function
        # GitHub skips this step after any failed step.
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2
        with:
          sarif_file: .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.sarif

docs.title: GitLab CI
docs.text:
# .gitlab-ci.yml
ferret-security-scan:
  stage: test
  image: python:3.11
  before_script:
    - pip install ferret-scan uv
  script:
    - uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan \
        --config-overrides "ash_plugin_modules+=[\"automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins\"]"
  artifacts:
    reports:
      sast: .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.sarif

docs.title: Comparison with detect-secrets
docs.text:
Feature Ferret Scan detect-secrets Credit Cards ✅ 15+ brands with Luhn ❌ Passports ✅ Multi-country + MRZ ❌ SSN ✅ Domain-aware ❌ API Keys ✅ 40+ patterns ✅ Multiple patterns High Entropy ❌ ✅ Social Media ✅ ❌ IP Detection ✅ ❌ Document Metadata ✅ EXIF extraction ❌

Consider using both scanners together for comprehensive coverage: 

uv run ash --scanners ferret-scan,detect-secrets

docs.title: Snyk Plugin CI/CD Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide provides detailed instructions for setting up the Snyk plugin in CI/CD environments, specifically for the GitHub Actions workflow in the automated-security-helper repository.

docs.title: GitHub Secret Configuration
docs.text: The Snyk plugin requires a SNYK_TOKEN to authenticate with Snyk's services. This token must be configured as a GitHub repository secret.

docs.title: Setting up SNYK_TOKEN Secret
docs.text:
1. Obtain a Snyk API Token:
  2. Log in to your Snyk account
  3. Navigate to Account Settings → API Token
  4. Generate a new token or copy your existing one

  5. The token format will look like: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx

  6. Add Secret to GitHub Repository:

  7. Navigate to your GitHub repository
  8. Go to Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
  9. Click New repository secret
  10. Name: SNYK_TOKEN
  11. Value: Your Snyk API token from step 1
  12. Click Add secret

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
The GitHub Actions workflow will automatically use the SNYK_TOKEN secret when running community plugin tests. You can verify the setup by:

  1. Checking that the secret appears in your repository's Actions secrets list
  2. Running the workflow and ensuring Snyk CLI authentication succeeds
  3. Reviewing the workflow logs for successful Snyk plugin execution

docs.title: Local Development Setup
docs.text: For local development and testing, you can set up Snyk authentication using one of these methods:

docs.title: Option 1: Environment Variable
docs.text: export SNYK_TOKEN=your-snyk-token-here

docs.title: Option 2: CLI Authentication
docs.text:
snyk auth
This will open a browser window for authentication and store credentials locally.

docs.title: Option 3: Configuration File
docs.text: Snyk CLI will automatically check for credentials at ~/.config/configstore/snyk.json.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Authentication Failed: - Verify the SNYK_TOKEN secret is correctly set in GitHub - Ensure the token is valid and hasn't expired - Check that the token has appropriate permissions for Snyk Code

Workflow Fails on Community Plugin Tests: - The workflow will skip Snyk tests gracefully if SNYK_TOKEN is not available - Check the workflow logs for specific error messages - Ensure npm is available for Snyk CLI installation

Rate Limiting: - Snyk may apply rate limits based on your subscription tier - Consider upgrading your Snyk plan for higher rate limits - Implement retry logic if needed

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
To troubleshoot issues in the workflow, you can:

  1. Check the "Install Community Plugin Tools" step logs
  2. Look for Snyk CLI version and authentication status
  3. Review the scan execution logs for detailed error messages

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
• Token Security: Never commit Snyk tokens to version control
  • Token Rotation: Regularly rotate your Snyk API tokens
  • Access Control: Limit repository access to trusted contributors
  • Monitoring: Monitor token usage in your Snyk dashboard

docs.title: Integration Testing
docs.text:
The community plugin legs scan with .ash/.ash_community_plugins.yaml. That file is inside the scanned tree, and a config file there cannot load the Snyk plugin, so the legs pass it with --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins (see .github/actions/run-scan-test/action.yml). snyk-code is disabled in that file, so the legs install the Snyk CLI and load the plugin without running a Snyk Code scan.

The GitHub Actions workflow tests both Snyk and Trivy plugins together to ensure:

  • Both tools install correctly on all supported platforms
  • Plugins don't conflict with each other
  • Scan results are properly generated and formatted
  • All output formats (SARIF, JSON, HTML, etc.) work correctly

docs.title: Platform Support
docs.text:
The Snyk plugin is tested on:

  • Linux: Ubuntu (x86_64 and ARM64)
  • macOS: Latest version (x86_64)
  • Windows: Latest version (x86_64)

All platforms use npm for cross-platform Snyk CLI installation, ensuring consistent behavior across environments.

docs.title: ASH Snyk Code Plugin
docs.text: This plugin integrates Snyk Code CLI tool with the Automated Security Helper (ASH) to provide comprehensive static application security testing (SAST) for source code vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Snyk Code plugin enables ASH to leverage Snyk's powerful static analysis capabilities for:

  • Static Application Security Testing (SAST): Identifies security vulnerabilities in source code
  • Real-time Analysis: Fast scanning with minimal false positives
  • Multi-language Support: Supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, PHP, Go, Ruby, Scala, Swift, and mor. See a full list here
  • Developer-friendly Results: Provides actionable remediation guidance with code examples

docs.title: Install Snyk CLI
docs.text:
The plugin requires Snyk CLI to be installed and available in your system PATH.

npm (Recommended): 

npm install -g snyk

Homebrew (macOS): 

brew install snyk/tap/snyk

Manual Installation: 

# Download and install latest release
curl -Lo snyk https://github.com/snyk/cli/releases/latest/download/snyk-linux
chmod +x snyk
sudo mv snyk /usr/local/bin/

Other platforms: See Snyk CLI Installation Guide

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Snyk Code requires authentication to access the scanning service:

Option 1: Environment Variable 

export SNYK_TOKEN=your-snyk-token

Option 2: CLI Authentication 

snyk auth

Option 3: Configuration File The plugin will automatically check for credentials at ~/.config/configstore/snyk.json

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
snyk --version
snyk code test --help

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
The Snyk Code plugin is not loaded by default. Its scanner sends the scanned source to Snyk with your Snyk token, so only the operator running ASH can load it. A config file inside the scanned tree, such as the repository's own .ash/.ash.yaml, cannot: an ash_plugin_modules entry there that names the package, or a module inside it, is ignored with a warning naming the entry.

Load it with --ash-plugin-modules:

uv run ash --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins

or with the ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES environment variable, which the commands on the rest of this page assume is set:

export ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES=automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins

A repository's own config cannot load the package, or select the scanner through another installed package that lists or imports it: the scanner is selected only when --ash-plugin-modules, ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES, --config-overrides or a config file outside the scanned tree loads this package or the package that lists it.

A config file outside the scanned tree, passed with --config, can list it too:

ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins

The scanner's settings, except honor_tree_exclusions (see Exclusion files in the scanned tree), can stay in the repository's .ash/.ash.yaml:

scanners:
  snyk-code:
    enabled: true
    options:
      severity_threshold: "MEDIUM"

docs.title: Run Snyk Code Scan
docs.text:
snyk-code does not scan a source directory that holds ASH's output directory (see ASH's output directory), so these commands write ASH's output outside the scanned tree with --output-dir. With the default .ash/ash_output, snyk-code reports ERROR for the source and names the output directory.

# Scan current directory
uv run ash --scanners snyk-code --output-dir ../ash_output

# Scan specific directory
uv run ash --scanners snyk-code --output-dir /path/to/ash_output /path/to/project

docs.title: Run Snyk Code Scan without an ASH configuration file
docs.text:
If you want to run Snyk code scan without saving a configuration file for ASH, use the following command to enable the plugin

# Scan current directory only with snyk-code
uv run ash --scanners snyk-code --output-dir ../ash_output --config-overrides "ash_plugin_modules+=[\"automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins\"]"

# SCan current directory with all available scanners (including snyk-code)
uv run ash --output-dir ../ash_output --config-overrides "ash_plugin_modules+=[\"automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins\"]"

docs.title: Severity Filtering
docs.text:
Configure the minimum severity level for reported vulnerabilities:

scanners:
  snyk-code:
    enabled: true
    options:
      severity_threshold: "HIGH"  # Options: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL

docs.title: Exclusion files in the scanned tree
docs.text:
snyk code test reads exclusions from files in the directory it tests, at any depth, and leaves the files they name out of its analysis: the exclude.code and exclude.global entries of a .snyk file, and the rules of a .dcignore file. Its legacy implementation also reads any file whose name ends in .snyk, .dcignore or .gitignore. It has no option that turns this off, and snyk code test takes no --policy-path. So when the tree has such a file, snyk-code does not run, and its error names the files. A .snyk file with only open source ignore entries or other exclude sections does not count, and neither does .gitignore, which ASH's own scan set honors too.

To accept a repository's exclusions, set honor_tree_exclusions with --config-overrides:

uv run ash --scanners snyk-code --config-overrides 'scanners.snyk-code.options.honor_tree_exclusions=true'

or in a config file outside the scanned tree, passed with --config:

scanners:
  snyk-code:
    enabled: true
    options:
      honor_tree_exclusions: true

A config file inside the scanned tree, such as the repository's own .ash/.ash.yaml, or one an MCP client delivered, does not set it.

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text:
scanners:
  snyk-code:
    enabled: true
    options:
      severity_threshold: "MEDIUM"
      # Additional scanner-specific options can be added here

docs.title: High Severity Issues Only
docs.text:
scanners:
  snyk-code:
    enabled: true
    options:
      severity_threshold: "HIGH"

docs.title: All Severity Levels
docs.text:
scanners:
  snyk-code:
    enabled: true
    options:
      severity_threshold: "LOW"

docs.title: Combined with Other Scanners
docs.text:
# Use Snyk Code alongside other ASH scanners
uv run ash --scanners snyk-code,bandit,semgrep --output-dir ../ash_output

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text:
# Run in container mode for CI/CD
uv run ash --mode container --scanners snyk-code --output-dir ../ash_output --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins

docs.title: Output Integration
docs.text:
Snyk Code results are integrated into ASH's unified reporting system:

  • SARIF Format: Machine-readable results for CI/CD integration
  • HTML Reports: Visual security dashboard with remediation guidance
  • JSON/CSV: Structured data for analysis and tracking
  • Markdown: Human-readable summaries for pull requests

snyk code test exits 0 when it finds nothing and 1 when it finds something. ASH treats both as a completed scan and reports the findings from the SARIF file Snyk writes, each at the level Snyk gave it (error as CRITICAL, warning as MEDIUM, note as LOW) and a finding Snyk marks ignored as suppressed. Whether the scan then fails is decided by ASH's severity threshold, as for every scanner. A run that exits 1 but whose SARIF file holds no results, and any other exit code except 3, such as 2 (a failed run), is reported as a snyk-code scanner error. Exit code 3, no supported files found, evaluated nothing and is reported SKIPPED (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: What ASH sends to Snyk
docs.text:
snyk code test uploads the files of the directory it tests, and it has no option that leaves a path out. For the source directory, once it holds none of what snyk-code refuses to run on (a link leaving it, ASH's output directory, or a file an ignore path matches; see Performance Considerations), ASH therefore runs it on a copy of the scan set. The copy is made in a new directory under the system temporary directory (TMPDIR), outside both the scanned directory and the output directory, and is removed when the scan of that directory ends; snyk-code reports an error rather than run when TMPDIR is inside either of them. A run that is killed (with SIGKILL, or SIGTERM) leaves its copy behind. On Linux and macOS, each later snyk-code run removes such copies: the user's own ash-snyk-code-* directories that no running scan holds and that were last modified longer ago than the scan timeout (scanners.snyk-code.options.scan_timeout, 1800 seconds by default, or an hour when it is null). On Windows, remove them yourself. Under the scanner sandbox, the Snyk CLI is given read access to that directory for its run. The copy leaves out:

  • files under global_settings.ignore_paths, matched the way ASH matches findings against ignore paths;
  • files that a .gitignore or .ignore file excludes from the scan set, and ASH's own output directory, apart from the files git tracks there;
  • symlinks, files with more than one hard link, paths outside the scanned directory, and files ASH cannot read, which ASH counts in a warning.

If ASH cannot write the copy, because the disk is full for example, snyk-code reports a scanner error instead of testing part of the tree. It reports one too when it leaves out every file it would have sent, so a tree of links is not reported as a clean scan. When the scan set holds no file to send, nothing is sent, snyk-code does not run, and the log says so. Files the converters wrote are tested where ASH wrote them. Making the copy takes time and disk space in proportion to the scan set. As for every scanner, a finding in a file under an ignore path is also left out of the reports.

Ignores managed in the Snyk app belong to a Snyk project, and Snyk may rely on the tested directory's git remote to find that project. The copy ASH sends carries no .git directory, so Snyk may not match it to that project, and those ignores may not apply: a finding ignored in the Snyk app can be reported again. To keep a finding out of ASH's results, suppress it in ASH's configuration.

docs.title: Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• First Run: May require initial authentication and setup
  • Network Dependency: Requires internet connection for cloud-based analysis
  • Large Codebases: Scanning time scales with codebase size
  • Rate Limits: Snyk may apply rate limits based on your subscription tier
  • Offline Mode: Snyk Code needs Snyk's service, so offline it does not run and is reported MISSING (see Offline Mode)
  • Links leaving the tree: snyk code test uploads the files it reads and has no option that leaves out one path, so ASH does not run it on a directory holding a link, to a file or to a directory, whose target is outside that directory. snyk-code is then ERROR, and the error names the link. Remove the link, or exclude snyk-code for that scan. The check reads no ignore file, so a link in a directory a .gitignore excludes, such as the interpreter link in a virtual environment, counts.
  • ASH's output directory: by default it is inside the scanned tree (.ash/ash_output), and it holds an earlier run's reports and logs and the converted files, which snyk code test would upload with the source. So snyk-code refuses a source directory that holds ASH's output directory: it is ERROR, snyk code test is not started, and the error names the output directory. To run snyk-code on the source, pass --output-dir with a directory outside the scanned tree. The .gitignore ASH writes in an output directory inside the tree is not relied on for this, since that snyk honors it is read from snyk's sources, not measured. The converted files are still scanned, as their own target.
  • Ignored paths: for the same reason, snyk-code refuses a directory holding a file that global_settings.ignore_paths matches, since the file would be uploaded. The files are every file snyk would be given: the source directory for the source, and ASH's directory of converted files, wherever it is, for the converted files. Each is matched as ASH matches the location snyk reports for a finding in it, its path below the directory snyk tests, so snyk-code refuses a file exactly when ASH would drop its findings. A converted file is matched by its path below the directory of converted files, such as archive/src__bundle__zip/vendor/m.js; an ignore path naming a source archive or notebook exactly keeps it from being converted at all. snyk code test is then not started, snyk-code is ERROR, and the error names the first such file and the pattern that matched it, and gives the number of files and the patterns. Narrow ignore_paths, or exclude snyk-code with --exclude-scanners snyk-code. The check reads no ignore file either, so an ignore path that matches only files a .gitignore excludes still refuses. ASH's own default exclusions for bandit and checkov, such as node_modules/, are not ignore paths: they do not drop findings, and do not stop snyk-code. snyk-code has no exclusion option of its own. This applies to the operator's ignore paths: the ignore paths in a config an MCP client delivered drop their findings but do not stop the upload, so a client that does not want its files sent leaves snyk-code out with the excluded_scanners argument of run_ash_workspace_scan. run_ash_scan has no argument that selects scanners, so a client using it does not deliver the files it does not want sent.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Snyk CLI not found: 

# Check if Snyk is in PATH
which snyk

# Install if missing
npm install -g snyk

Authentication errors: 

# Check authentication status
snyk auth

# Set token via environment variable
export SNYK_TOKEN=your-token-here

Network connectivity issues: 

# Test connectivity to Snyk services
snyk test --dry-run

Empty directory warnings: The plugin will skip scanning if the target directory is empty or doesn't exist, logging an appropriate warning message.

No supported files (exit code 3): snyk code test exits 3 when the target holds no file Snyk Code supports, for example a tree of only Terraform or YAML. snyk-code then evaluated nothing and is reported SKIPPED, not ERROR, so it does not fail the completeness gate. Exit code 2 is a Snyk failure and is reported ERROR.

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Enable verbose logging to troubleshoot issues:

uv run ash --scanners snyk-code --output-dir ../ash_output --log-level DEBUG

docs.title: Offline Mode
docs.text:
Snyk Code analyzes code on Snyk's service, so it cannot run offline. In offline mode snyk-code does not run and is reported MISSING, which fails the scan under the default completeness gate (fail_on_incomplete_scanners, exit code 1). To scan offline without it, leave it out. Both commands assume the plugin is enabled in your configuration, as shown above:

# snyk-code is MISSING here, and the scan exits 1
uv run ash --offline --scanners snyk-code

# An offline scan that does not ask for snyk-code
uv run ash --offline --exclude-scanners snyk-code

docs.title: Pre-commit Hook
docs.text:
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: ash-snyk-code
        name: ASH Snyk Code Security Scan
        entry: uv run ash --scanners snyk-code --mode precommit --output-dir ../ash_output --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/security.yml
name: Security Scan
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install Snyk CLI
        run: npm install -g snyk
      - name: Run ASH with Snyk Code
        env:
          SNYK_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SNYK_TOKEN }}
          ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES: automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins
        # ASH's output outside the checkout, so snyk-code scans the source.
        run: |
          uv run ash --scanners snyk-code --output-format sarif --output-dir "${{ runner.temp }}/ash_output"
      - name: Upload SARIF results
        # Also when ASH exits non-zero on findings: without a status function
        # GitHub skips this step after any failed step.
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2
        with:
          sarif_file: ${{ runner.temp }}/ash_output/reports/ash.sarif

docs.title: GitLab CI
docs.text:
# .gitlab-ci.yml
snyk-security-scan:
  stage: test
  image: node:18
  before_script:
    - npm install -g snyk
  script:
    # ASH's output outside the checkout, so snyk-code scans the source; the
    # report is copied back in afterwards, since artifacts come from the checkout.
    - uv run ash --scanners snyk-code --output-dir /tmp/ash_output
  after_script:
    - cp /tmp/ash_output/reports/ash.sarif ash.sarif
  variables:
    SNYK_TOKEN: $SNYK_TOKEN
    ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES: automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - ash.sarif

docs.title: Supported Languages
docs.text:
Snyk Code supports static analysis for:

  • JavaScript/TypeScript: Node.js, React, Angular, Vue.js
  • Python: Django, Flask, FastAPI
  • Java: Spring, Maven, Gradle projects
  • C#/.NET: .NET Framework, .NET Core
  • PHP: Laravel, Symfony, WordPress
  • Go: Standard library and popular frameworks
  • Ruby: Rails, Sinatra
  • Scala: Play Framework, Akka
  • Swift: iOS/macOS applications

Full list of supported languages is available at the Snyk Website

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: For comprehensive documentation and advanced configuration options, see: - ASH Community Plugins Documentation - Snyk CLI Documentation - Snyk Code Documentation

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
• ASH Issues: GitHub Issues
  • Snyk Issues: Snyk Support
  • Community: ASH Discussions

docs.title: Trivy Plugin
docs.text:
ASH also has a builtin trivy scanner, trivy, which runs trivy fs with only the vuln scanner by default and is on in every scan. See Trivy filesystem scanner. Listing this module for trivy-repo therefore runs trivy twice, and each finding is reported once per scanner; set scanners.trivy.enabled: false to keep only trivy-repo.

Description: The Trivy plugin integrates Aquasec's Trivy CLI tool to provide comprehensive repository scanning for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, secrets, and license issues. This plugin extends ASH's security scanning capabilities with Trivy's advanced detection algorithms and extensive vulnerability database.

Repository: Ships with ASH; loaded only when listed in ash_plugin_modules

Author: ASH Development Team

License: Apache 2.0

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Trivy is a comprehensive security scanner that can detect: - Vulnerabilities in OS packages and language-specific packages - Misconfigurations in Infrastructure as Code (IaC) files - Secrets and sensitive information in code - License compliance issues

The ASH Trivy plugin provides seamless integration with Trivy's repository scanning capabilities, allowing you to incorporate Trivy scans into your ASH security workflows with unified reporting and configuration management.

docs.title: Trivy CLI Installation
docs.text: ash dependencies install installs the pinned trivy release (v0.75.0, checked against the SHA256 in automated_security_helper/utils/tool_downloads.py) that both trivy and trivy-repo run, and the ASH container image ships it. A trivy you install yourself, as below, is used when it is on PATH; ASH is tested against the pinned version.

docs.title: Installation Options
docs.text:
Using Homebrew (macOS/Linux): 

brew install trivy

Using Package Managers: 

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install wget apt-transport-https gnupg lsb-release
wget -qO - https://aquasecurity.github.io/trivy-repo/deb/public.key | sudo apt-key add -
echo "deb https://aquasecurity.github.io/trivy-repo/deb $(lsb_release -sc) main" | sudo tee -a /etc/apt/sources.list.d/trivy.list
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install trivy

# RHEL/CentOS
sudo vim /etc/yum.repos.d/trivy.repo
# Add repository configuration
sudo yum -y update
sudo yum -y install trivy

Using Binary Releases:

Linux/macOS: 

# Download and install from GitHub releases
curl -sfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aquasecurity/trivy/main/contrib/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin

Windows: 

# Download and install using the official endpoint
curl -sfL -o trivy.zip "https://get.trivy.dev/trivy?type=zip&os=windows&arch=amd64"
unzip trivy.zip
# Move trivy.exe to a directory in your PATH

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Verify Trivy installation: 

trivy version

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
Add the Trivy plugin to your ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project):

ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_trivy_plugins

Configure the scanner based on your requirements:

scanners:
  trivy-repo:
    enabled: true
    options:
      scanners: ["vuln", "misconfig", "secret", "license"]
      severity_threshold: "MEDIUM"
      ignore_unfixed: false
      license_full: false
      disable_telemetry: true

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
Option Type Default Description scanners List[str] ["vuln", "misconfig", "secret", "license"] Types of scans to perform severity_threshold str null Minimum severity that fails the scan (ALL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL); null uses the global threshold. Findings below it are still reported; ASH does not pass it as trivy --severity ignore_unfixed bool true Ignore vulnerabilities without available fixes license_full bool true Enable full license scanning (more comprehensive but slower) disable_telemetry bool true Disable Trivy telemetry data collection. Only --config-overrides or a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory can set it to false; any config can set it to true config_file str null A trivy config file, passed as trivy --config; see below module_dir str null A directory of trivy modules, passed as trivy --module-dir; see below ignore_file str null A trivy ignore file, passed as trivy --ignorefile; see below secret_config_file str null A trivy secret-scanning config, passed as trivy --secret-config; see below offline bool false Run offline even when ASH does not; ASH's offline mode applies regardless scan_timeout int 1800 Seconds ASH lets trivy run; ASH does not pass trivy --timeout, so trivy's own 5-minute default still applies

trivy-repo always passes trivy --config and trivy --module-dir, so trivy does not load a trivy.yaml from the directory it runs in. config_file and module_dir are honored only when set through --config-overrides or a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory (one that is not repository-written), and only for paths outside the scanned tree, which a path written inside the tree and led out of it by a symbolic link there is not; otherwise they are ignored with a warning. A relative path is taken from the directory of the ASH config file that sets it, or from the working directory for --config-overrides, not from the source directory (see Relative paths in the operator's settings). A configured path that does not exist fails the scan. Unset or ignored, --config names TRIVY_CONFIG when that is a file outside the scanned tree (a relative path in it is taken from the working directory ASH runs in), and otherwise an empty config ASH ships; --module-dir names an empty directory ASH creates outside the scanned tree for each scanner run and removes when the run ends.

ignore_file and secret_config_file follow the same rule, a relative path included. Unset or refused, trivy-repo uses TRIVY_IGNOREFILE or TRIVY_SECRET_CONFIG from the environment for a file outside the scanned tree (a relative path in either is taken from the working directory ASH runs in), and otherwise an empty file ASH writes outside the scanned tree, so a .trivyignore or trivy-secret.yaml in the scanned repository does not remove findings or disable secret rules.

docs.title: Scanner Types
docs.text:
The scanners option accepts the following values:

  • vuln: Vulnerability scanning for OS and language packages
  • misconfig: Infrastructure as Code misconfiguration detection
  • secret: Secret and sensitive information detection
  • license: License compliance scanning

docs.title: Severity Levels
docs.text: Trivy supports the following severity levels (from lowest to highest): - UNKNOWN: Unknown severity - LOW: Low severity issues - MEDIUM: Medium severity issues - HIGH: High severity issues - CRITICAL: Critical severity issues

docs.title: Basic Repository Scan
docs.text:
# Scan current directory with default Trivy settings
ash --scanners trivy-repo

# Scan specific directory
ash --target /path/to/project --scanners trivy-repo

docs.title: Vulnerability-Only Scan
docs.text:
# ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project)
scanners:
  trivy-repo:
    enabled: true
    options:
      scanners: ["vuln"]
      severity_threshold: "HIGH"
      ignore_unfixed: true

ash --scanners trivy-repo

docs.title: Comprehensive Security Scan
docs.text:
# ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project)
scanners:
  trivy-repo:
    enabled: true
    options:
      scanners: ["vuln", "misconfig", "secret", "license"]
      severity_threshold: "LOW"
      license_full: true

docs.title: Integration with Other Scanners
docs.text:
# ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project)
scanners:
  # Combine Trivy with other ASH scanners
  trivy-repo:
    enabled: true
    options:
      scanners: ["vuln", "misconfig"]
      severity_threshold: "MEDIUM"

  bandit:
    enabled: true
    options:
      severity_threshold: "MEDIUM"

  semgrep:
    enabled: true
    options:
      severity_threshold: "MEDIUM"

docs.title: Output and Reporting
docs.text:
The Trivy plugin integrates with ASH's unified reporting system, producing results in SARIF format that can be converted to various output formats.

trivy-repo accepts only exit code 0 as a completed run. trivy exits 0 whether or not it found anything and 1 on an error, so a run that exits 1 is recorded ERROR and its results file is not graded. ASH passes --exit-code=0, which outranks an exit-code setting in your trivy config or in TRIVY_EXIT_CODE, so a run with findings still exits 0 and is reported; a trivy.yaml in the scanned directory is not read at all. ASH decides the scan's exit code from the findings. See A Scanner Is ERROR With an Exit Code It Does Not Accept.

#!/bin/bash
# incremental-scan.sh

# Only scan changed files since last scan
if [ -f .last_trivy_scan ]; then
  CHANGED_FILES=$(find . -newer .last_trivy_scan -name "*.py" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.yaml")

  if [ -n "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
    echo "Scanning changed files: $CHANGED_FILES"
    echo "$CHANGED_FILES" | xargs -I {} dirname {} | sort -u | while read dir; do
      ash --target "$dir" --scanners trivy-repo
    done
  else
    echo "No changes detected, skipping scan"
  fi
else
  echo "First scan, scanning entire repository"
  ash --scanners trivy-repo
fi

touch .last_trivy_scan

docs.text:
# performance_monitor.py
import json
import time
import psutil
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path


class TrivyPerformanceMonitor:
    def __init__(self):
        self.metrics = []

    def run_monitored_scan(self):
        start_time = time.time()
        start_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().used

        # Run ASH with Trivy
        process = subprocess.Popen(
            ["ash", "--scanners", "trivy-repo", "--reporters", "json"],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        )

        # Monitor resource usage
        max_memory = start_memory
        while process.poll() is None:
            current_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().used
            max_memory = max(max_memory, current_memory)
            time.sleep(1)

        end_time = time.time()

        # Collect metrics
        duration = end_time - start_time
        memory_used = max_memory - start_memory

        # Count results
        results_file = Path(".ash/ash_output/reports/ash_aggregated_results.json")
        finding_count = 0
        if results_file.exists():
            with open(results_file) as f:
                data = json.load(f)
                finding_count = sum(
                    len(run.get("results", [])) for run in data.get("runs", [])
                )

        # Store metrics
        metric = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "duration_seconds": duration,
            "memory_mb": memory_used / (1024 * 1024),
            "finding_count": finding_count,
            "exit_code": process.returncode,
        }

        self.metrics.append(metric)
        return metric

    def save_metrics(self, filename="trivy_performance.json"):
        with open(filename, "w") as f:
            json.dump(self.metrics, f, indent=2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor = TrivyPerformanceMonitor()
    metric = monitor.run_monitored_scan()
    monitor.save_metrics()

    print(f"Scan completed in {metric['duration_seconds']:.1f}s")
    print(f"Memory used: {metric['memory_mb']:.1f}MB")
    print(f"Findings: {metric['finding_count']}")

#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/pre-commit

# Quick scan of staged files only
STAGED_FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

if [ -n "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
  echo "Running security scan on staged files..."

  # Create temporary directory with staged files
  TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
  echo "$STAGED_FILES" | while read file; do
    if [ -f "$file" ]; then
      mkdir -p "$TEMP_DIR/$(dirname "$file")"
      cp "$file" "$TEMP_DIR/$file"
    fi
  done

  # Scan staged files
  ash --target "$TEMP_DIR" --scanners trivy-repo --config-file .ash/precommit.yaml
  SCAN_RESULT=$?

  # Cleanup
  rm -rf "$TEMP_DIR"

  if [ $SCAN_RESULT -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Security scan failed. Commit aborted."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# .github/workflows/pr-security-scan.yml
name: PR Security Scan
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed-files
        run: |
          git diff --name-only origin/${{ github.base_ref }}..HEAD > changed_files.txt
          echo "files=$(cat changed_files.txt | tr '\n' ' ')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Scan changed files
        run: |
          # Create directory structure for changed files
          mkdir -p scan_target
          while read file; do
            if [ -f "$file" ]; then
              mkdir -p "scan_target/$(dirname "$file")"
              cp "$file" "scan_target/$file"
            fi
          done < changed_files.txt

          # Run security scan
          ash --target scan_target --scanners trivy-repo --reporters sarif,markdown

      - name: Comment PR
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            if (fs.existsSync('.ash/ash_output/reports/security-report.md')) {
              const report = fs.readFileSync('.ash/ash_output/reports/security-report.md', 'utf8');
              github.rest.issues.createComment({
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                body: '## Security Scan Results\n\n' + report
              });
            }

#!/bin/bash
# license-compliance-check.sh

echo "Running comprehensive license scan..."
ash --scanners trivy-repo --config-file .ash/license-audit.yaml

# Process license results
python3 << 'EOF'
import json
import csv
from collections import defaultdict

# Load scan results
with open('.ash/ash_output/reports/ash_aggregated_results.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Extract license information
licenses = defaultdict(list)
for run in data.get('runs', []):
    for result in run.get('results', []):
        if 'license' in result.get('ruleId', '').lower():
            license_name = result.get('message', {}).get('text', 'Unknown')
            file_path = result.get('locations', [{}])[0].get('physicalLocation', {}).get('artifactLocation', {}).get('uri', 'Unknown')
            licenses[license_name].append(file_path)

# Generate license summary
print("License Summary:")
print("================")
for license_name, files in licenses.items():
    print(f"{license_name}: {len(files)} files")
    for file_path in files[:5]:  # Show first 5 files
        print(f"  - {file_path}")
    if len(files) > 5:
        print(f"  ... and {len(files) - 5} more files")
    print()

# Check for problematic licenses
problematic_licenses = ['GPL-3.0', 'AGPL-3.0', 'SSPL-1.0']
issues = []
for license_name in licenses:
    if any(prob in license_name for prob in problematic_licenses):
        issues.append(license_name)

if issues:
    print("⚠️  Potentially problematic licenses found:")
    for issue in issues:
        print(f"  - {issue}")
else:
    print("✅ No known problematic licenses detected")
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# establish-security-baseline.sh

echo "Establishing security baseline..."

# Run comprehensive scan
ash --scanners trivy-repo --reporters json --config-file .ash/baseline.yaml

# Store baseline
mkdir -p .security-baseline
cp .ash/ash_output/reports/ash_aggregated_results.json .security-baseline/baseline-$(date +%Y%m%d).json

# Generate baseline suppressions
python3 << 'EOF'
import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

with open('.ash/ash_output/reports/ash_aggregated_results.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

suppressions = []
expiration = (datetime.now() + timedelta(days=90)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')

for run in data.get('runs', []):
    for result in run.get('results', []):
        rule_id = result.get('ruleId')
        file_path = result.get('locations', [{}])[0].get('physicalLocation', {}).get('artifactLocation', {}).get('uri')

        if rule_id and file_path:
            suppression = {
                'rule_id': rule_id,
                'path': file_path,
                'reason': 'Baseline finding - review and update',
                'expiration': expiration
            }
            suppressions.append(suppression)

# Write suppressions to YAML
import yaml
with open('.security-baseline/baseline-suppressions.yaml', 'w') as f:
    yaml.dump({'global_settings': {'suppressions': suppressions}}, f, default_flow_style=False)

print(f"Generated {len(suppressions)} baseline suppressions")
print("Review .security-baseline/baseline-suppressions.yaml and merge approved suppressions into your ASH config file (.ashrc.yaml in a new project)")
EOF

docs.title: Regression Detection
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# detect-security-regressions.sh

echo "Checking for security regressions..."

# Run current scan
ash --scanners trivy-repo --reporters json

# Compare with baseline
python3 << 'EOF'
import json
from pathlib import Path

# Load current results
with open('.ash/ash_output/reports/ash_aggregated_results.json') as f:
    current_data = json.load(f)

# Load baseline (most recent)
baseline_files = sorted(Path('.security-baseline').glob('baseline-*.json'))
if not baseline_files:
    print("No baseline found. Run establish-security-baseline.sh first.")
    exit(1)

with open(baseline_files[-1]) as f:
    baseline_data = json.load(f)

# Extract findings
def extract_findings(data):
    findings = set()
    for run in data.get('runs', []):
        for result in run.get('results', []):
            rule_id = result.get('ruleId')
            file_path = result.get('locations', [{}])[0].get('physicalLocation', {}).get('artifactLocation', {}).get('uri')
            if rule_id and file_path:
                findings.add(f"{rule_id}:{file_path}")
    return findings

current_findings = extract_findings(current_data)
baseline_findings = extract_findings(baseline_data)

# Detect regressions (new findings)
regressions = current_findings - baseline_findings
improvements = baseline_findings - current_findings

print(f"Security Status:")
print(f"  Current findings: {len(current_findings)}")
print(f"  Baseline findings: {len(baseline_findings)}")
print(f"  New issues (regressions): {len(regressions)}")
print(f"  Fixed issues: {len(improvements)}")

if regressions:
    print("\n🚨 Security Regressions Detected:")
    for regression in sorted(regressions):
        rule_id, file_path = regression.split(':', 1)
        print(f"  - {rule_id} in {file_path}")
    exit(1)
else:
    print("\n✅ No security regressions detected")

if improvements:
    print("\n🎉 Security Improvements:")
    for improvement in sorted(improvements):
        rule_id, file_path = improvement.split(':', 1)
        print(f"  - Fixed {rule_id} in {file_path}")
EOF

docs.title: Trivy CLI Not Found
docs.text:
Error: Trivy CLI not found in PATH

Symptoms: - ASH reports "Dependencies not satisfied" for trivy-repo scanner - Scanner is skipped during execution - No Trivy results in output

Solutions: 1. Verify Installation: Check if Trivy is installed 

trivy version
which trivy

  1. PATH Configuration: Ensure Trivy is in your PATH 

    echo $PATH
export PATH=$PATH:/path/to/trivy/bin

  2. Reinstall Trivy: Use your preferred installation method 

    # Homebrew
brew install trivy

# Direct download
curl -sfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aquasecurity/trivy/main/contrib/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin

  3. Container Mode Alternative: Use ASH container mode 

    ash --mode container --scanners trivy-repo

docs.title: Database Update Failures
docs.text:
Error: Failed to update vulnerability database

Symptoms: - Trivy hangs during database download - Network timeout errors - Outdated vulnerability data

Solutions: 1. Check Connectivity: Verify internet access 

curl -I https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-db/releases

  1. Clear Cache: Remove corrupted database cache 

    rm -rf ~/.cache/trivy/
trivy image --download-db-only

  2. Proxy Configuration: Configure proxy settings 

    export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.company.com:8080
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.company.com:8080
trivy image --download-db-only

  3. Offline Mode: Use pre-downloaded database 

    # Download database separately
trivy image --download-db-only --cache-dir /shared/trivy-cache

# Use cached database, with ASH offline: online, ASH updates the database
# before the scan and fails without network
export TRIVY_CACHE_DIR=/shared/trivy-cache
export ASH_OFFLINE=YES
ash --scanners trivy-repo

docs.title: Permission Issues
docs.text:
Error: Permission denied accessing scan target

Symptoms: - Scanner fails to read files - Empty scan results - Access denied errors in logs

Solutions: 1. Check Permissions: Verify directory access 

ls -la /path/to/target
find /path/to/target -type f ! -readable

  1. Fix Ownership: Correct file ownership 

    sudo chown -R $USER:$USER /path/to/target
chmod -R u+r /path/to/target

  2. Run with Sudo: Use elevated permissions (not recommended) 

    sudo ash --scanners trivy-repo --target /path/to/target

  3. Container Mode: Use container with proper volume mounts

Trivy supports extensive configuration through environment variables:

export TRIVY_TIMEOUT=10m

docs.title: Offline Scanning Setup
docs.text:
# 1. Download database on internet-connected machine
trivy image --download-db-only --cache-dir /shared/trivy-cache

# 2. Copy cache to air-gapped environment
rsync -av /shared/trivy-cache/ airgapped-server:/opt/trivy-cache/

# 3. Configure offline scanning
export TRIVY_CACHE_DIR=/opt/trivy-cache
export ASH_OFFLINE=YES
ash --scanners trivy-repo

In offline mode (--offline, ASH_OFFLINE, or options.offline: true) ASH passes --skip-db-update, --skip-java-db-update, --offline-scan and --skip-check-update, and sets TRIVY_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=true and TRIVY_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true: trivy's version check and telemetry contact check.trivy.dev, and --skip-check-update covers only the checks bundle. Variables rather than flags, because a trivy too old to know the flags refuses the command, while it ignores the variables.

Online and offline, ASH passes --config: the operator's config_file, else TRIVY_CONFIG when that names a file outside the scanned tree, otherwise an empty config ASH ships, so a trivy.yaml in the scanned repository is never read. Its settings can reach the network (a VEX repository, client/server mode) or change what is reported. A relative path in TRIVY_CONFIG is taken from the working directory ASH runs in, as one in TRIVY_IGNOREFILE or TRIVY_SECRET_CONFIG is, not from the source directory.

Offline, trivy's Terraform checks do not run. trivy downloads the source of every module block it evaluates (a registry module from registry.terraform.io, a git:: source with the host's git, an https:// archive), whatever offline flags it is given, so ASH passes --misconfig-scanners with the installed trivy's default list minus terraform, read from trivy repository --help. When that list cannot be read, the misconfig scanner is left out of the offline scan, with a warning. checkov still checks Terraform offline.

The copied database has to be current. After the scan ASH reads its UpdatedAt (from trivy version --format json) and exits 1 once it is more than 24 hours old, which is trivy's own rule: the published database sets NextUpdate 24 hours after UpdatedAt, and trivy online replaces it after that. Offline, trivy --skip-db-update bypasses that rule, so ASH applies it instead. Repeat steps 1 and 2 to refresh the database, or pass --allow-stale-content-db (config: content_db_staleness: warn) to scan with an older one and have the reports say so.

docs.title: Dynamic Suppressions
docs.text:
# Scan, then turn each finding not already suppressed into a suppression entry
ash scan --scanners trivy-repo --output-formats sarif
jq '[.runs[].results[]
     | select((.suppressions // []) | length == 0)
     | {rule_id: .ruleId,
        path: .locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri,
        reason: "Baseline finding: review it before the suppression expires",
        expiration: (now + 90 * 86400 | strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))}]
    | unique' .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.sarif > suppressions.json

# Review suppressions.json, then append the entries to global_settings.suppressions
# in your ASH config file, 200 at a time: on Linux one command-line argument holds
# at most 128 KiB, and a single --set with a few hundred entries is refused with
# "Argument list too long".
jq -c '. as $all | range(0; length; 200) | $all[.:. + 200]' suppressions.json |
  while read -r part; do
    ash config update --set "global_settings.suppressions+=$part"
  done

Appending YAML to the config file (cat suppressions.yaml >> .ashrc.yaml) does not work: it adds a second top-level global_settings, YAML keeps only the last one, and every other global setting in the file is dropped. ash config update keeps them, and writes each entry with only the fields it sets. It rewrites the whole file, without its comments, and refuses a file that reads environment variables (!ENV or ${VAR:default}); add the entries to such a file by hand.

import json
import requests
from pathlib import Path


def send_trivy_results():

        with open(results_file) as f:

# store_results.py
import json
import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path


def store_trivy_results():
    conn = sqlite3.connect("security_results.db")

    # Create table if not exists
    conn.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS trivy_findings (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            scan_date TEXT,
            rule_id TEXT,
            severity TEXT,
            file_path TEXT,
            message TEXT,
            fixed_version TEXT
        )
    """)

    # Load and store results
    results_file = Path(".ash/ash_output/reports/ash_aggregated_results.json")
    if results_file.exists():
        with open(results_file) as f:
            data = json.load(f)

        scan_date = datetime.now().isoformat()

        for run in data.get("runs", []):
            if run.get("tool", {}).get("driver", {}).get("name") == "trivy-repo":
                for result in run.get("results", []):
                    conn.execute(
                        """
                        INSERT INTO trivy_findings 
                        (scan_date, rule_id, severity, file_path, message, fixed_version)
                        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                    """,
                        (
                            scan_date,
                            result.get("ruleId"),
                            result.get("level"),
                            result.get("locations", [{}])[0]
                            .get("physicalLocation", {})
                            .get("artifactLocation", {})
                            .get("uri"),
                            result.get("message", {}).get("text"),
                            result.get("fixes", [{}])[0]
                            .get("description", {})
                            .get("text"),
                        ),
                    )

    conn.commit()
    conn.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    store_trivy_results()

# trend_analysis.py
import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path


def analyze_security_trends():
    # Load historical data
    history_dir = Path("security-history")

    dates = []
    vuln_counts = []

    for result_file in sorted(history_dir.glob("*.json")):
        with open(result_file) as f:
            data = json.load(f)

        date = datetime.fromisoformat(result_file.stem)
        dates.append(date)

        # Count vulnerabilities by severity
        vuln_count = sum(
            1
            for run in data.get("runs", [])
            for result in run.get("results", [])
            if result.get("level") in ["error", "warning"]
        )
        vuln_counts.append(vuln_count)

    # Generate trend chart
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
    plt.plot(dates, vuln_counts, marker="o")
    plt.title("Security Findings Trend")
    plt.xlabel("Date")
    plt.ylabel("Number of Findings")
    plt.xticks(rotation=45)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("security-trend.png")

    return dates, vuln_counts


if __name__ == "__main__":
    analyze_security_trends()
